title: Comparison of diagnostic performance of a deep learning algorithm, emergency physicians, junior radiologists and senior radiologists in the detection of appendicular fractures in children.
headline_result: sensitivity 95.6%, specificity 91.6%, negative predictive value 98.8%; against 98.4% for pediatric radiologists, 95.1% for senior residents, 90.1% for junior residents and 81.9% for emergency physicians

model_family: machine learning image analysis of standard ultrasound planes, using no measurement inputs
patient_population: two independent ultrasound datasets, one for training and internal validation and one for external validation, with gestational age ground truth from a reliable last menstrual period date confirmed by first-trimester crown-rump length
clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy in the second and third trimesters, where biometry assumes an average fetal size at each gestational age and its error widens to at least two weeks as growth deviates from that average
model_description: Attacks the assumption rather than the measurement. Conventional dating converts size to age through a population growth curve, so any fetus off the average is mis-dated - which is exactly the growth-restricted fetus whose dating matters most. Reading the image directly, with no measurements at all, sidesteps that and the paper shows it holds up in intrauterine growth restriction. Blinded external validation against first-trimester-confirmed dates is the right standard and rarely met in this literature.
title: Machine learning for accurate estimation of fetal gestational age based on ultrasound images.
study_design: retrospective model development with blinded external validation
dataset_size: two independent datasets, sizes not stated in the abstract
headline_result: mean absolute error 3.0 days (95% CI 2.9-3.2) in the second trimester and 4.3 days (95% CI 4.1-4.5) in the third, better than current ultrasound-based clinical biometry at those ages

model_family: DeepMedic, a 3D convolutional neural network
patient_population: 244 children with de novo brain tumors of varied subtype: 215 internal and 29 from an external institution
clinical_problem: delineating pediatric brain tumor subregions for surgery, treatment planning and response monitoring
model_description: Extracts the brain and then segments the tumor into enhancing, non-enhancing, cystic and edematous components from four routine sequences. Performance held up on a withheld external cohort, which matters because most pediatric tumor segmentation work is single-institution. The subregion breakdown is what makes it usable for response assessment rather than only for volume.
title: Automated tumor segmentation and brain tissue extraction from multiparametric MRI of pediatric brain tumors: A multi-institutional study.
dataset_size: 244 children (151 training, 43 validation, 21 internal test, 29 external test)
headline_result: Dice 0.91 internal and 0.88 external for whole tumor, 0.73/0.84 for enhancing tumor, and 0.98 for brain tissue

model_family: annotated dataset release rather than a model
patient_population: 9125 studies retrospectively collected from a major pediatric hospital in Vietnam between 2020 and 2021, each read by a pediatric radiologist with more than ten years of experience
clinical_problem: the shortage of physician-annotated pediatric chest radiographs that has kept pediatric CXR AI far behind adult CXR AI
model_description: Infrastructure, and the most consequential kind for this field. Adult chest radiograph AI advanced because large annotated datasets existed and pediatric CXR AI did not; PediCXR is a direct attempt to close that gap. What distinguishes it from re-used public collections is lesion-level annotation - 36 findings and 15 diseases, each abnormality drawn as a bounding box, not merely an image-level label - with a fixed 7728/1397 split so results are comparable across groups. Publicly released on PhysioNet.
release_evidence: the dataset is publicly available on PhysioNet at https://physionet.org/content/vindr-pcxr/1.0.0/
title: PediCXR: An open, large-scale chest radiograph dataset for interpretation of common thoracic diseases in children.
headline_result: the first and largest pediatric chest radiograph dataset with both lesion-level bounding boxes and image-level labels, covering 36 findings and 15 diseases

model_family: 21 submitted algorithms, all deep learning and mostly U-Nets
patient_population: fetuses in the open FeTA dataset of reconstructed brain MRI segmented into seven tissues
clinical_problem: segmenting the developing fetal brain into tissues, the step every quantitative prenatal neurodevelopment study depends on
model_description: The benchmark this subfield lacked: an open dataset, seven tissue labels, and 20 international teams evaluated on the same terms. The finding is instructive about the state of the art — almost all 21 submissions performed similarly, four of the top five used ensembles, and the differences that mattered were fine-tuning and pre- and post-processing rather than architecture. One asymmetrical U-Net stood apart.
release_evidence: the challenge used the FeTA Dataset, an open dataset of fetal brain MRI reconstructions
title: Fetal brain tissue annotation and segmentation challenge results.
dataset_size: the open FeTA dataset; 21 algorithms from 20 teams
headline_result: almost all submissions performed similarly; one asymmetrical U-Net performed significantly better than the rest

model_family: FDA-cleared AI app interpreting cine-sweep images from a handheld probe, with real-time decision support
patient_population: 369 scans in 306 infants, scanned by nurses or family physicians at three primary care clinics after video, slide and brief in-person training
clinical_problem: universal newborn screening for developmental dysplasia of the hip, which prevents premature osteoarthritis if caught in infancy but is not cost-effective when every scan needs an expert to perform and a radiologist or surgeon to read
model_description: The clearest example in this database of AI changing who can do a study rather than how well it is read. Nurses and family physicians with an afternoon of training, a handheld probe and real-time decision support reached follow-up and case-detection rates comparable to formal screening done by a sonographer and read by a specialist. The learning curve is quantified rather than asserted - follow-up rates fell from 40% to 14% after about 60 cases per site. All six infants referred on had confirmed dysplasia, and four had no risk factors that would have flagged them for selective screening.
release_evidence: the FDA-cleared MEDO-Hip AI app used with a commercial handheld ultrasound probe
title: AI aided workflow for hip dysplasia screening using ultrasound in primary care clinics.
dataset_size: 369 scans in 306 infants across three primary care clinics
headline_result: internal follow-up rate fell from 40% (nurses) and 20% (physicians) to 14% after about 60 cases per site; all 6 infants referred to pediatric orthopedics had confirmed dysplasia, 4 of them with no risk factors

patient_population: children imaged in radiology practice generally
clinical_problem: the near absence of AI tools developed and validated for children, framed as a health equity problem
model_description: The ACR Pediatric AI Workgroup's position statement. Its argument is that pediatric AI is not adult AI applied to smaller patients: design, training, validation and safe deployment in children all require distinct approaches, and the current shortage of pediatric-specific tools is a health equity issue rather than a market gap. It closes by inviting the community to join the Image Gently-affiliated Image IntelliGently initiative.
journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
title: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Radiology: Impact on Pediatric Patients, a White Paper From the ACR Pediatric AI Workgroup.

patient_population: pregnancies in the 127 reviewed studies
clinical_problem: the whole span of obstetric ultrasound, from first-trimester scanning to fetal echocardiography and neurosonography
task: detection / diagnosis; measurement / quantification; outcome prediction
model_description: The broadest map of AI in obstetric ultrasound: 127 studies sorted by application, covering first-trimester scanning, placenta, biometry, echocardiography, neurosonography, anatomy assessment, lung maturity and adverse-outcome prediction. Its stated promise is efficiency and improved outcomes in low-resource settings, which is where the strongest evidence in this database also sits.
title: Artificial intelligence in obstetric ultrasound: A scoping review.

model_family: deep learning model deployed inside the AlignProCARE open platform smartphone app
patient_population: adolescent patients attending spine clinics, with radiographs and smartphone photographs; ground truth annotated by two experienced spine specialists from spine radiographs
clinical_problem: classifying severity and curve type in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and detecting progression, from a single photograph of the unclothed back instead of a radiograph
model_description: A radiation-sparing substitute for the screening examination rather than for the diagnostic radiograph. The comparison is the honest one - the app's output and the radiographic ground truth were both put blind against two spine surgeons judging the same unclothed back - so the question asked is whether the model beats the clinical examination it would replace, not whether it beats the X-ray. Progression detection over six-month follow-up is the harder and more clinically valuable half.
release_evidence: incorporated into and tested in the AlignProCARE open platform app in 2022
title: Deep Learning Model to Classify and Monitor Idiopathic Scoliosis in Adolescents Using a Single Smartphone Photograph.
dataset_size: not stated in the abstract beyond a prospective training cohort and a clinic test cohort
headline_result: the app classified AIS severity and curve type and distinguished six-month progression, benchmarked blind against two spine surgeons assessing unclothed back appearance

model_family: Faster R-CNN object detection compared against EfficientNetV2 image classification
patient_population: 58,846 upper extremity radiographs from 14,873 pediatric and young adult patients, with internal and external test splits
clinical_problem: pediatric upper extremity fractures, which respond to injury differently from adult bone and which most fracture AI has ignored
model_description: The development paper behind the openly shared childfx model, and unusually explicit about sharing it. It compares strong supervision (object detection with boxes) against weak supervision (whole-image classification) and finds the former clearly better. The comparison that matters operationally is against on-call residents on the cases they actually preliminary-read overnight, where the model was more accurate.
release_evidence: develop and transparently share an AI model capable of detecting a range of pediatric upper extremity fractures
title: Artificial intelligence to identify fractures on pediatric and young adult upper extremity radiographs.
study_design: retrospective development with external testing and resident comparison
headline_result: AUC 0.96, accuracy 89.7%, sensitivity 90.8%, specificity 88.7%; accuracy on overnight preliminary-read cases 89.4% versus 85.1% for residents (P = 0.01)

model_family: penalized logistic regression over 145 multimodal baseline variables, including structural MRI features
patient_population: a subsample of the multisite IMAGEN adolescent cohort: 407 for training and 137 from three independent IMAGEN sites held out for validation, grouped by 2-year and 5-year follow-up diagnosis
clinical_problem: identifying which healthy 14-year-olds will develop major or subthreshold depression, so that risk can be monitored and early intervention offered
model_description: Imaging is one of four modalities here rather than the whole model, and the honest reading of the result is that it contributes modestly - one structural feature, supramarginal gyrus surface area, survives alongside baseline symptom severity, sex, neuroticism and stressful life events. That is itself worth recording: a well-powered multimodal test of how much brain structure adds over cheap clinical variables. Validation on three independent sites held the AUC, which most prediction studies in this literature cannot show.
journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
title: Predicting Depression Onset in Young People Based on Clinical, Cognitive, Environmental, and Neurobiological Data.
headline_result: AUC 0.70-0.72 in training and 0.68-0.72 in the independent validation sample

patient_population: not specified; the review is written for a pediatric radiology readership
clinical_problem: whether radiology AI actually improves efficiency, dose, accuracy and outcomes
model_description: A review, not a model. It names six clinical objectives AI is meant to serve — faster workflow, shorter reading time, less dose and contrast, earlier detection, better accuracy, more personalized diagnostics — and grades the published evidence for each against a hierarchical model of efficacy. Its conclusion is that the market is still maturing and very little is known about what AI contributes in practice, which is the argument for real-world monitoring before procurement.
title: How does artificial intelligence in radiology improve efficiency and health outcomes?

model_family: convolutional neural network brain masking model, packaged with existing fMRI preprocessing steps
patient_population: 1241 manually traced fetal fMRI images from 207 fetuses, with two held-out test sets from separate scanners and populations
clinical_problem: isolating the fetal brain from surrounding maternal tissue across thousands of non-stationary volumes, the step that blocks any resting-state functional MRI study of the brain before birth
model_description: Fetal resting-state fMRI grew faster than the tooling to process it, and brain masking is where that gap bites - the brain moves unpredictably between volumes, so a single mask never holds. Rather than publishing a network alone, the authors wire it into the surrounding preprocessing steps and explain each adaptation, and release code and data openly. Two held-out test sets from different scanners and populations is a stronger generalization claim than the field usually makes.
release_evidence: openly shared code and data, presented as an advance toward a fully comprehensive open-source workflow
title: Automated Brain Masking of Fetal Functional MRI with Open Data.
headline_result: excellent auto-masking performance across two held-out test sets from separate scanners and populations

model_family: 3D U-Net segmentation with automated bidimensional and volumetric measurement
patient_population: 794 children with preoperative MRI and 122 with serial postoperative MRI, covering high-grade glioma, medulloblastoma and leptomeningeal seeding tumors
clinical_problem: measuring tumor burden reproducibly across serial MRI to judge whether a child's brain tumor is responding
model_description: Segments the tumor on contrast-enhanced T1 and T2/FLAIR and then computes the RAPNO response measurement automatically, both as bidimensional product and as volume. The result worth noting is not accuracy but repeatability: it was more consistent than human raters when a child had multiple lesions, which is exactly where manual response assessment becomes unreliable and where treatment decisions turn.
title: Deep learning-based automatic tumor burden assessment of pediatric high-grade gliomas, medulloblastomas, and other leptomeningeal seeding tumors.
study_design: retrospective study with two independent expert raters
headline_result: intraclass correlation with expert volumes 0.90-0.96; agreement of automated with manual RAPNO scores 0.85-0.91; superior repeatability to human raters for multifocal disease

patient_population: children in the reviewed literature
clinical_problem: where AI stands in pediatric musculoskeletal imaging, beyond bone age
model_description: A sober review from Pediatric Radiology: bone age has been in clinical use for a decade and is deployed in an assist mode rather than replacing anyone, and almost everything else — appendicular fracture detection, vertebral fracture detection — remains in the research literature. It ends by asking pediatric radiologists to join the research teams rather than wait for products, which is a reasonable reading of why so little pediatric-specific development happens.
title: Current and emerging artificial intelligence applications for pediatric musculoskeletal radiology.

patient_population: children undergoing chest radiography or CT
clinical_problem: whether any of the certified chest AI products can be used in children
model_description: A review of the more than 40 certified AI products for chest radiography and chest CT, read from a pediatric standpoint. Its central finding is blunt: none of them is designed for children. The partial exceptions are adult tuberculosis detectors, which are also applicable to children, and software under development for early cystic fibrosis change on chest CT, which the authors flag as the most promising pediatric opening.
release_evidence: more than 40 certified AI products are available for chest radiography or chest CT
title: Current and emerging artificial intelligence applications in chest imaging: a pediatric perspective.

patient_population: children imaged in radiology practice
clinical_problem: where AI fits in the pediatric radiologist's working day, and what it cannot do
model_description: A review in Pediatric Radiology arguing for augmentation rather than replacement. It sets out what AI does better than a person (measuring size, shape, texture and kinetics; handling high-dimensional data) against what it does worse (it is only as good as its training sample and cannot reason toward a near-optimal solution), and proposes explainable AI and an assistant that frees the radiologist's attention for the generic parts of the job.
title: The augmented radiologist: artificial intelligence in the practice of radiology.

model_family: k-means clustering over 120 radiomics features from pre-therapeutic chest CT
patient_population: 283 adolescents and adults with cystic fibrosis from a French multicentre real-world prospective study, with pre-therapeutic and one-year follow-up chest CT
clinical_problem: identifying, before treatment starts, which people with cystic fibrosis will respond to lumacaftor-ivacaftor, and measuring the structural lung change the drug produces
model_description: Unsupervised rather than supervised, and that choice carries the argument: the clusters are morphological phenotypes discovered in the pre-treatment CT without reference to who responded, and only afterwards are they checked against response. One of the three clusters contained most of the responders. Alongside this, visual Bhalla scoring quantifies what the drug did to the airways - mucus plugging, wall thickening and consolidation all fell over a year.
title: Using chest computed tomography and unsupervised machine learning for predicting and evaluating response to lumacaftor-ivacaftor in people with cystic fibrosis.
study_design: prospective multicentre observational study with retrospective radiomic analysis
headline_result: Bhalla score fell 1.40 +/- 1.53 points at one year (p<0.001); 54% of one radiomic cluster achieved a >= 5% FEV1 gain versus 32% and 33% in the others (p=0.02)

model_family: commercial deep-learning fracture detection algorithm
patient_population: 2,549 children aged 0-17 (mean 8.5 years) referred from a pediatric emergency room for trauma
clinical_problem: detecting fractures on radiographs of children presenting to the emergency room after trauma
model_description: This is the study a department should read before buying: an independent external validation of a marketed fracture-detection product on a consecutive real-life pediatric emergency cohort, scored three ways (is there a fracture, how many, and are they in the right place) with subgroup analysis by age and by whether the limb was in a cast. Performance was materially worse in children under 5 and in casted limbs, which are exactly the pediatric cases that matter.
release_evidence: external validation of the commercially available Rayvolve algorithm
title: External validation of a commercially available deep learning algorithm for fracture detection in children.
headline_result: sensitivity 95.7%, specificity 91.2%, accuracy 92.6% for detection; sensitivity and negative predictive value significantly lower in children aged 0-4 and in casted limbs

model_family: real-time YOLOv3 object detection
patient_population: 16,297 pregnancies at 18-40 weeks from two tertiary Chinese hospitals for development, a third hospital for external validation, and 166 pregnancies for prospective video testing
clinical_problem: screening for congenital central nervous system malformation on standard neurosonographic planes
model_description: Detects ten distinct intracranial abnormality patterns during the scan itself, not afterwards, using a real-time detection architecture. The evaluation ladder is unusually complete: internal validation, external validation at a third hospital, comparison against sonologists of differing experience, and then a prospective video dataset simulating live scanning. Performance drops from internal to external, as it should, and stays useful.
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Use of real-time artificial intelligence in detection of abnormal image patterns in standard sonographic reference planes in screening for fetal intracranial malformations.
study_design: retrospective development with external and prospective validation
dataset_size: 43,890 images from 16,297 pregnancies and 169 videos from 166 pregnancies
headline_result: micro-average AUC 0.977 internally and 0.898 on external validation across ten intracranial patterns, with prospective real-time video evaluation

model_family: hybrid model combining an HRNet landmark detector with rule-based post-processing
patient_population: 1542 consecutive patients with scoliosis at two Hong Kong clinics from December 2019 to November 2020 for development, then prospective validation in a further 337 patients; biplanar EOS radiographs recaptured with smartphones or screenshots
clinical_problem: automatic measurement of spine alignment in scoliosis, where existing auto-analysis is unreliable and where the image a clinician has is often a phone photo or a screenshot rather than the original radiograph
model_description: Two things set it apart. First, it is deliberately trained on degraded images - smartphone photographs and screenshots of radiographs - because that is what gets sent between clinics, and robustness to that is the difference between a research tool and a usable one. Second, rules are layered on the network's landmarks so the output can be explained and checked, rather than emerging from an opaque regression. Prospectively validated on 337 further patients, which is rare in this literature.
title: An artificial intelligence powered platform for auto-analyses of spine alignment irrespective of image quality with prospective validation.
dataset_size: 1542 development patients plus 337 prospective validation patients
headline_result: mean landmark error 2.78 pixels posteroanterior and 5.52 lateral; mean angle error 3.18 degrees coronal and 6.32 degrees sagittal; curve detection sensitivity 95.7% and specificity 88.1%; all predicted alignments strongly correlated with ground truth (R2 > 0.97)

model_family: deep learning detection model for plain radiographs
patient_population: children with head trauma who had both skull radiography and cranial CT: development sets of 149 and 264 from two hospitals, external test set of 95 from a third; cranial CT was the reference standard
clinical_problem: detecting skull fractures on plain radiographs in children with head trauma, the film that is often taken first and read by whoever is on shift
model_description: One of the cleaner pediatric AI evaluations in the literature: multi-center development, a genuinely external test hospital, CT as the reference standard, and a two-session reader study with the crossed design that shows who the tool is for. The answer is the one that keeps recurring in pediatric AI - it significantly helped radiology residents and emergency physicians and did nothing measurable for the pediatric radiologist. That is an argument about staffing and coverage, not about accuracy.
title: Deep Learning-Assisted Diagnosis of Pediatric Skull Fractures on Plain Radiographs.
study_design: retrospective multi-center model development with a crossed reader study
dataset_size: 413 development cases from two hospitals, 95 external test cases from a third
headline_result: AUROC 0.922 internal and 0.870 external; with AI assistance AUROC rose by 0.094 for radiology residents (p = 0.012) and 0.069 for emergency physicians (p = 0.043), but by only 0.008 for the pediatric radiologist (p = 0.850)

model_family: multi-task convolutional network doing spatio-temporal feature extraction and standard plane detection on ultrasound video
patient_population: 50 freehand fetal ultrasound video scans, compared against five experienced sonographers measuring at two time points at least two weeks apart
clinical_problem: fetal biometry - head circumference, biparietal diameter, abdominal circumference, femur length - and the gestational age and weight estimates derived from it, in settings short of sonographers who can interpret fetal ultrasound
model_description: Works from video rather than from a frozen frame, so the model chooses the measuring plane as well as the caliper positions - the part of biometry that actually takes skill. The evaluation is the strongest form available short of a trial: five sonographers measured twice, weeks apart, establishing both intra- and inter-observer variability, and the model's disagreement with each expert fell inside that band. Six minutes of expert time becomes a few seconds.
title: Deep learning fetal ultrasound video model match human observers in biometric measurements.
study_design: retrospective model development with a multi-reader repeatability study
headline_result: automated measurements comparable to five experienced sonographers, with differences within inter- and intra-observer variability and not statistically significant against any individual expert; seconds versus an average of six minutes

model_family: depthwise-separable U-shaped network with a conditional random field boundary refinement and Mean Teacher noisy-data training
patient_population: more than 80 000 osteosarcoma MRI images from three hospitals in China; osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumor of children and adolescents
clinical_problem: segmenting osteosarcoma on MRI and computing tumor area in settings where radiologist time is the binding constraint and outcomes are worst
model_description: Explicitly engineered for a low-resource deployment rather than for a leaderboard: separable convolutions keep the model cheap to run, a Mean Teacher stage lets noisy studies be used rather than discarded, and a conditional random field cleans up boundaries that a light network gets wrong. The stated objective is a balance of speed, accuracy and cost, which is an unusual and honest framing for a segmentation paper.
journal: Computational and mathematical methods in medicine
title: Intelligent Segmentation Medical Assistance System for MRI Images of Osteosarcoma in Developing Countries.
dataset_size: more than 80 000 MRI images from three hospitals
headline_result: improved segmentation accuracy while holding the balance of speed and cost, tested across three hospitals

model_family: U-Net segmentation of the fetal head and placenta applied to volume sweep imaging acquisitions
patient_population: obstetric volume sweep imaging examinations performed in Peru by an operator with no previous ultrasound experience after eight hours of training
clinical_problem: obtaining fetal biometry, presentation and placental position where there is neither a sonographer to scan nor a radiologist to interpret
model_description: The title states the design goal exactly. Both halves of the expertise requirement are removed at once: a standardized sweep protocol keyed to external body landmarks replaces the sonographer's judgment about where to put the probe, and a U-Net replaces the interpreting provider. Eight hours of operator training is the whole input. Placental location is the weak point - substantial rather than near-perfect agreement - which is the finding a deployment plan would have to build around.
title: No sonographer, no radiologist: New system for automatic prenatal detection of fetal biometry, fetal presentation, and placental location.
study_design: prospective diagnostic study in an under-resourced setting
headline_result: 100% agreement for fetal presentation (kappa 1, p<0.0001) and 76.7% for placental location (kappa 0.59); relative error 5.6% for biparietal diameter and 7.9% for head circumference; gestational age within 2 weeks of standard of care in up to 89%

model_family: multi-feature fuzzy clustering with weighted majority ruling over conventional, diffusion-weighted and dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI features
patient_population: 15 patients with newly diagnosed high-grade appendicular osteosarcoma enrolled in a single-center observational study, of whom 13 contributed usable data
clinical_problem: predicting tumor necrosis - and thus response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy - in childhood osteosarcoma, a cancer whose systemic treatment has been essentially unchanged for 30 years for want of a biomarker
model_description: The methodological core is the co-registration of histologic sections with the MR images, so that MRI features are learned against necrosis measured at the same physical location rather than against a whole-tumor percentage. Necrosis on the resection specimen is the current response measure and it arrives only after surgery; an imaging surrogate would arrive during treatment. Fifteen patients, so this is a proof of principle for a testable biomarker rather than a biomarker.
title: Correlation of histopathology and multi-modal magnetic resonance imaging in childhood osteosarcoma: Predicting tumor response to chemotherapy.
headline_result: MRI-estimated necrosis compared against pathologist estimates and deep-learning quantification of digitized histologic sections, through direct histologic-MR co-registration

model_family: deep learning-based CT reconstruction
patient_population: 65 children aged 6 years or younger (mean 25 months) undergoing contrast-enhanced 80-kVp CT, plus a phantom study
clinical_problem: how far pediatric CT dose can be cut at low tube voltage before diagnostic quality fails
model_description: Compares deep-learning reconstruction against hybrid and model-based iterative reconstruction on low-tube-voltage pediatric CT, at roughly half the dose. Two radiologists scored noise, texture, streak, sharpness and overall quality, and a phantom study measured task-based detectability across six dose levels. The finding that matters: lower-dose deep-learning images scored higher than standard-dose hybrid iterative images, while lower-dose model-based iterative images scored worse.
title: Radiation Dose Reduction for 80-kVp Pediatric CT Using Deep Learning-Based Reconstruction: A Clinical and Phantom Study.
study_design: retrospective clinical and phantom study with reader assessment
dataset_size: 65 children (31 standard dose, 34 lower dose) plus phantom imaging at six dose levels
headline_result: size-specific dose estimate 54% lower in the reduced-dose group; lower-dose deep-learning reconstruction scored higher than standard-dose hybrid iterative reconstruction on texture, sharpness and overall quality (p < .001)

model_family: autonomous commercial bone age system
patient_population: 97 radiologists across 18 European countries already using the software, from 282 surveyed
clinical_problem: what actually happens when an AI tool designed to replace the radiologist is installed in a department
model_description: The most useful deployment study in this database, and it contains no images. BoneXpert was built as an AI-replace tool; asked how they actually use it, only 18% of radiologists let it replace them, 60% still review the radiograph themselves to exclude underlying disease, and 40% have never overruled it. Reporting time fell sharply. The authors' conclusion is the general lesson: bone age rating is not the whole of reading a bone age radiograph, so a tool validated for one task cannot autonomously own the examination.
release_evidence: the autonomous AI system for bone age rating (BoneXpert), in clinical use in European departments
title: Autonomous artificial intelligence in pediatric radiology: the use and perception of BoneXpert for bone age assessment.
headline_result: radiologists taking over 2 minutes per rating fell from 86% to 21% after installation; only 18% used it to replace the radiologist, 60% still checked the radiograph themselves, and 40% never overruled it

model_family: deep neural network with a visualized internal representation used as an explainable overlay
patient_population: fetal cardiac ultrasound screening read by experts, fellows and residents
clinical_problem: screening for congenital heart disease on fetal cardiac ultrasound, where detection rates are low because the technique is hard to master
model_description: The measured outcome is the examiner's performance, not the model's - which is the right endpoint for a screening aid and a rare one to see reported. The gain scales inversely with experience: residents improved most, fellows next, experts least, exactly the gradient you would want from a tool meant to spread a hard skill. The explainability is not a post-hoc heatmap but a purpose-built representation of the network's internals, offered as the thing that earns clinician trust.
title: Medical Professional Enhancement Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Fetal Cardiac Ultrasound Screening.
headline_result: mean AUC rose from 0.966 to 0.975 for experts, 0.829 to 0.890 for fellows and 0.616 to 0.748 for residents

model_family: convolutional neural network trained few-shot, compared against training on many weakly labelled atlas-derived segmentations
patient_population: 9 manually annotated volumes for training; the trained models were then applied to 278 ultrasound volumes from a diverse healthy population
clinical_problem: quantifying subcortical brain volume development from 3D fetal ultrasound, which manual segmentation makes impractical because of low soft tissue contrast, speckle and shadowing
model_description: Two contributions worth separating. Methodologically, it settles a practical question - nine careful manual annotations beat many weak atlas-derived labels, reaching close to intra-observer variability - which changes how a group with limited annotation time should spend it. Substantively, applying the result to 278 healthy volumes produced ultrasound-specific second-trimester growth curves for choroid plexus, ventricle horns, cavum septum pellucidum and cerebellum, which is a normative reference that did not previously exist for this modality.
title: Subcortical segmentation of the fetal brain in 3D ultrasound using deep learning.
study_design: retrospective model development and normative study
dataset_size: 9 manually annotated training volumes; 278 volumes for the growth curves
headline_result: segmentation performance close to intra-observer variability from only nine manual annotations, and novel ultrasound-specific second-trimester growth curves for four subcortical structures

model_family: two-stage sequential radiomics classifier selected from six candidate models
patient_population: 263 children with newly diagnosed medulloblastoma at 12 international pediatric sites, mean age 87 months
clinical_problem: identifying the molecular subgroup of a medulloblastoma from the preoperative MRI, which determines risk group and therapy
model_description: Extracts 1,800 texture and intensity features from preoperative T2 and contrast-enhanced T1 MRI and assigns the tumor to one of the four clinically actionable molecular subgroups, in two stages: first separating non-WNT/non-SHH tumors, then splitting WNT from SHH. A separate classifier distinguishes high-risk group 3 from group 4. If it held up prospectively it would let subgroup-directed decisions be made before surgery, and narrow who needs targeted genetic testing.
title: MRI Radiogenomics of Pediatric Medulloblastoma: A Multicenter Study.
headline_result: microaveraged F1 88% across subgroups, 95% for WNT specifically, and AUC 98% for group 3 versus group 4

model_family: commercial deep-learning fracture detection algorithm
patient_population: 300 radiographic examinations from patients aged 2-21 (167 boys, 133 girls, mean age 10.8 years), balanced across five body parts
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: detecting acute appendicular fractures in children
model_description: An independent external validation of a marketed fracture-detection product on pediatric extremity radiographs, deliberately balanced across five anatomical regions with 60 examinations each. Performance held up across body parts and fracture types with one clear exception, avulsion fractures, where sensitivity fell to 73% with a wide confidence interval. Avulsions are a characteristically pediatric injury, which makes that the finding to carry into a procurement discussion.
release_evidence: external validation of an existing commercial AI software program (BoneView)
title: Automated detection of acute appendicular skeletal fractures in pediatric patients using deep learning.
headline_result: sensitivity per patient 91.3%, specificity 90.0%, AUC 0.93; sensitivity for avulsion fractures only 72.7%

patient_population: 6,091 children treated for wrist trauma at one pediatric surgery department between 2008 and 2018
clinical_problem: the absence of an annotated public pediatric fracture dataset, which is what keeps most fracture AI adult-trained
model_description: A public dataset rather than a model, and arguably worth more than another classifier: 20,327 de-identified pediatric wrist radiographs across 10,643 studies, annotated by pediatric radiologists with lines, boxes and polygons marking fractures and periosteal reactions, plus age and sex. Given that children are under 1% of public medical imaging data, a dataset of this size in the commonest pediatric fracture is a substantive contribution.
release_evidence: this dataset is publicly available to encourage computer vision research
title: A pediatric wrist trauma X-ray dataset (GRAZPEDWRI-DX) for machine learning.
dataset_size: 20,327 images from 10,643 studies of 6,091 patients, with 74,459 tags and 67,771 labeled objects

model_family: 3D CNN localisation and landmark-guided pose estimation feeding automated deformable slice-to-volume registration
patient_population: T2-weighted fetal MRI datasets across the 21-36 week gestational age range
clinical_problem: reconstructing a high-resolution 3D fetal trunk volume from motion-corrupted T2-weighted stacks, which is what makes detailed assessment of body anomalies including congenital heart defects possible
model_description: Extends to the trunk what had only been solved for the fetal brain. Two specific failures are targeted: existing trunk pipelines need manual input, and gradient-descent registration has too narrow a capture range for the severe motion typical at early gestational age. A 3D localisation network plus landmark-based pose estimation replaces both, and an outlier-rejection step throws out stacks ruined by motion or poor quality without a human deciding. The result lands in standard radiological space regardless of how the fetus is lying.
title: Automated 3D reconstruction of the fetal thorax in the standard atlas space from motion-corrupted MRI stacks for 21-36 weeks GA range.
headline_result: fully automated deformable slice-to-volume reconstruction of the fetal thorax in the standard atlas space across 21-36 weeks, independent of fetal trunk position or stack coverage

patient_population: children in the nine eligible studies, most on radiographs and most of the elbow
clinical_problem: how well AI actually detects fractures in children, given that development has concentrated on adults
model_description: A systematic review with a pointed premise: missed fractures carry greater long-term clinical and medicolegal consequence in children than in adults, yet almost all research and commercial effort has been on adults. Only nine studies qualified. Nearly all used single-institution data and only two performed external validation, so the reported accuracies of 89 to 98 percent cannot be assumed to generalize. Its recommendation is multicentre real-world evaluation.
title: Artificial intelligence for radiological paediatric fracture assessment: a systematic review.
headline_result: reported AI accuracies 88.8-97.9%; only 2 of 9 studies performed external validation, and AI sensitivity exceeded human readers non-significantly in 2 of 3 comparative studies

model_family: commercial adult-developed lesion detection software
patient_population: 2,273 chest radiographs from patients 18 or younger
clinical_problem: whether chest AI built and approved for adults can be pointed at children's radiographs
model_description: Takes software developed on adults and runs it on 2,273 pediatric chest radiographs against a pediatric radiologist reference. Overall sensitivity was only 67%, and age was a significant predictor of error. Excluding cardiomegaly and children under two lifted accuracy from 87.5% to 96.9%, which locates the failure precisely: the youngest children and the finding most dependent on age-specific normal anatomy. The conclusion, that these tools need validation in younger children, is the practical one.
release_evidence: an AI-based lesion detection software developed for adult chest radiographs
title: Diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence approved for adults for the interpretation of pediatric chest radiographs.
headline_result: sensitivity 67.2%, specificity 91.1%, accuracy 87.5% overall; accuracy rose to 96.9% and sensitivity to 86.4% after excluding cardiomegaly and children 2 years or younger (all p < 0.001)

model_family: CNN trained on synthetically generated images
patient_population: subjects from newborn to adult, across a range of acquisitions including clinically common thick-slice fast spin-echo
clinical_problem: removing non-brain signal (skull-stripping) as a first step in any brain MRI analysis
model_description: Takes any brain MRI, of any contrast or resolution, and returns a brain mask. It is trained entirely on synthetic images whose anatomy, intensities and artifacts are deliberately pushed beyond the realistic range, so that a single model generalizes to acquisitions it never saw, including neonatal and clinical thick-slice scans that defeat conventional tools.
release_evidence: our method and labeled evaluation data are available at https://w3id.org/synthstrip
title: SynthStrip: skull-stripping for any brain image.
headline_result: substantial accuracy improvement over popular skull-stripping baselines with a single trained model

model_family: three-dimensional regression convolutional neural network with layer-wise relevance propagation attention maps
patient_population: 518 neonates and infants aged 0-25 months with reported normal myelination scanned at one academic center between January 1995 and June 2019 (mean gestationally corrected age 67 weeks +/- 33), with an external test set from the National Institutes of Health
clinical_problem: judging whether an infant's myelination is appropriate for age, which today means a radiologist visually inspecting T1 and T2 images against remembered milestones and comparing to gestationally corrected age
model_description: Automates an assessment that is already part of every pediatric brain MRI report, rather than inventing a new biomarker - the output is the age the brain looks like, which is exactly what the radiologist is estimating by eye. The attention maps are the convincing part: the network attended to cerebellum, posterior white matter and basal ganglia in the youngest infants and to anterior white matter in the oldest, which is the known caudal-to-rostral, posterior-to-anterior order of myelination. Combining T1 and T2 beat either alone, and it held up on an external NIH set.
title: Deep Learning to Predict Neonatal and Infant Brain Age from Myelination on Brain MRI Scans.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
headline_result: mean absolute error 9.8 +/- 2.3 weeks (T1), 9.1 +/- 1.9 (T2) and 7.7 +/- 1.7 (both) internally; 9.1 weeks on the external NIH test set

body_region: abdomen, chest, head, neck and pelvis
patient_population: children in the 16 reviewed studies
clinical_problem: how much radiation dose AI can actually save in children, and where
model_description: A systematic review answering a single procurement-shaped question: which AI techniques have been used for pediatric dose optimization, where, and how well. Almost all of it is deep-learning CT reconstruction, and the reported dose reductions are large. It notes that commercially available models dominate but locally built ones matched them, and that the evidence base is narrow: three modalities, small samples, and most examination types untouched.
release_evidence: commercially available AI models based on deep convolutional networks dominate the reviewed studies
title: Artificial Intelligence for Radiation Dose Optimization in Pediatric Radiology: A Systematic Review.
headline_result: most studies reported 36-70% radiation dose reduction without loss of diagnostic information

model_family: commercial deep-learning fracture detection aid
patient_population: 300 radiographs from patients aged 2 to 21, half with at least one fracture, read by three senior pediatric radiologists and five residents
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: missed fractures on pediatric emergency radiographs, particularly by trainees
model_description: A multi-reader study of what an AI aid does to human performance rather than of the model alone. Eight readers read 300 radiographs unaided and then again with the AI. Sensitivity rose by about 10 points overall with no meaningful loss of specificity, and the gain was largest for residents, which is the group covering nights and weekends in a pediatric emergency department.
release_evidence: described as an artificial intelligence aid evaluated as a reading adjunct
title: Assessment of an artificial intelligence aid for the detection of appendicular skeletal fractures in children and young adults by senior and junior radiologists.
headline_result: mean reader sensitivity rose from 73.3% to 82.8% (P < 0.001) with specificity essentially unchanged; stand-alone AI sensitivity 91% and specificity 90%

model_family: sixteen radiomics models combining two feature selection methods (ReliefF and t test), ComBat harmonization, and two classifiers (artificial neural network and support vector machine)
patient_population: 176 patients treated between January 2007 and December 2018 at three centers in France, median age 20 years (range 5-71), 107 male
clinical_problem: predicting histologic response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in osteosarcoma before treatment starts, when the current prognostic measure - percent necrosis - is only available after surgery and imaging has no predictive value
model_description: The clinical gap is stated precisely: histologic response is among the strongest survival predictors in osteosarcoma but arrives after the surgery it might have informed. Sixteen model configurations are built and compared rather than one being reported, and ComBat harmonization is tested explicitly - a necessary step for a three-centre retrospective radiomics study where scanner differences would otherwise be learned as signal. Training and validation performance are close, which is reassuring for a radiomics model of this size.
title: Prediction of Histologic Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Response in Osteosarcoma Using Pretherapeutic MRI Radiomics.
headline_result: best model AUC 0.95 with 91% sensitivity and 92% specificity in training, and 0.97 / 91% / 92% in validation

model_family: neural network trained on expert plus community-scientist quality ratings
patient_population: 2747 diffusion MRI datasets from children and adolescents in the Healthy Brain Network study
clinical_problem: quality control of diffusion MRI at a scale where no expert can look at every scan, which otherwise limits every downstream analysis of pediatric white matter
model_description: Two deliverables in one paper, and the second is the interesting one. The first is a curated, preprocessed, analysis-ready pediatric diffusion MRI resource in BIDS format, openly released. The second is a way of scaling quality control: a small expert-scored subset plus a much larger set scored by community scientists trains a network that agrees with experts on held-out data, and an interpretability check confirms it keys on features that actually bear on quality. That paradigm - crowdsource the bulk, anchor with experts, learn the rest - transfers to any large pediatric imaging cohort.
release_evidence: preprocessed, analysis-ready data made openly available from the openly-available Healthy Brain Network study
title: An analysis-ready and quality controlled resource for pediatric brain white-matter research.
headline_result: quality control highly concordant with experts on a held-out set, ROC-AUC 0.947

model_family: mobile-optimized deep learning models over blind-sweep ultrasound, running on-device
patient_population: blind sweep ultrasounds collected by sonographers in the USA and Zambia and by novice operators in Zambia; 406 for gestational age and 613 for malpresentation
clinical_problem: estimating gestational age and detecting fetal malpresentation where there is no trained sonographer, which is where most of the world's antenatal ultrasound gap sits
model_description: Designed backwards from the deployment constraint rather than from the dataset. Six freehand sweeps replace the standard examination, so the operator needs no plane-finding skill; the model runs on an Android phone in under three seconds with no internet; and the accuracy claim is a formal non-inferiority test against standard biometry rather than a correlation. The most consequential result is that non-inferiority held when novices performed only two of the six sweep types, which is a statement about how little training the pathway actually requires.
title: A mobile-optimized artificial intelligence system for gestational age and fetal malpresentation assessment.
dataset_size: 406 gestational age cases and 613 malpresentation cases
headline_result: gestational age non-inferior to standard biometry (error difference -1.4 +/- 4.5 days, 95% CI -1.8 to -0.9); malpresentation AUC-ROC 0.977 (95% CI 0.949-1.00); under 3 s on-device

patient_population: children with autism across the reviewed computer-aided diagnosis literature
clinical_problem: automated detection of autism spectrum disorder from structural and functional MRI
model_description: A review of computer-aided diagnosis systems for autism built on structural and functional MRI, covering both conventional machine learning and the smaller deep learning literature, with a comparison of the two and a catalogue of the obstacles each faces. Useful as an entry point to a literature that is large, heterogeneous and rarely externally validated.
title: Automatic autism spectrum disorder detection using artificial intelligence methods with MRI neuroimaging: A review.

model_family: DenseNet201, selected after comparing four convolutional architectures
patient_population: fetal ultrasound images covering seven congenital heart defects - ventricular and atrial septal defect, atrioventricular septal defect, Ebstein anomaly, tetralogy of Fallot, transposition of the great arteries and hypoplastic left heart syndrome - plus normal controls
clinical_problem: detecting major congenital heart disease at routine prenatal ultrasound screening, where detection rates are held down by the scarcity of fetal cardiologists and the volume of scans
model_description: Seven named lesions rather than a normal-versus-abnormal split, which is what a screening tool would have to distinguish to be more than a flag. Reporting the intra-patient and inter-patient splits separately is the paper's most useful discipline: the perfect intra-patient numbers are an artefact of frames from the same fetus appearing on both sides, and the inter-patient figures are the ones to read. Validated against three expert fetal cardiologists.
title: Deep Learning for Improving the Effectiveness of Routine Prenatal Screening for Major Congenital Heart Diseases.
study_design: retrospective model development with expert comparison
headline_result: inter-patient sensitivity 99%, specificity 97% and accuracy 98% (intra-patient 100% across the board)

patient_population: children with congenital heart disease across the 2002-2022 literature
clinical_problem: diagnosis, risk stratification and management of congenital heart disease in children
model_description: A scoping review across cardiac MRI, echocardiography, CT and electrocardiography in children, extending to postoperative outcome prediction and prenatal prediction from maternal risk factors. It is candid about why adoption lags: few appropriate algorithms, limited physician training, fear of over-mechanization, and the worry about losing the human element.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Cardiology: A Scoping Review.

model_family: neural network on ultrasound cineloop sweeps
patient_population: 4,695 pregnant volunteers in North Carolina and Zambia, with separate test sets of IVF pregnancies and of sweeps collected by untrained users on low-cost devices
clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy where there is no sonographer and no high-end ultrasound machine
model_description: Estimates gestational age from blind sweeps of the pregnant abdomen: the operator simply passes the probe along predefined lines without needing to find any standard plane. The model was more accurate than a trained sonographer's standard biometry, and the accuracy held when the sweeps were collected by untrained providers in Zambia using battery-powered devices. This is one of the clearest demonstrations in the corpus that AI can move an imaging capability to where the expertise is not.
title: AI Estimation of Gestational Age from Blind Ultrasound Sweeps in Low-Resource Settings.
headline_result: mean absolute error 3.9 days for the model versus 4.7 days for standard biometry (P < 0.001); 4.9 versus 5.4 days for sweeps collected by untrained users on low-cost devices

patient_population: the population covered by FDA-cleared AI/ML-enabled medical devices, with pediatric representation as one axis of analysis
clinical_problem: what has actually been cleared for use, through which pathway, and for whom
model_description: An analysis of every FDA-cleared AI/ML-enabled device by clearance pathway, timeline, specialty, decision type and recall history. Radiology dominates, approvals surged from 2018, and most went through 510(k) on substantial equivalence, which means no new clinical trial. Two gaps are named that bear directly on children: pediatric-focused devices and trials are underrepresented, and trials are geographically concentrated in the United States.
release_evidence: analysis of FDA-cleared commercial medical devices
title: FDA approved Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML)-Enabled Medical Devices: An updated landscape
dataset_size: the full FDA AI/ML-enabled device list
headline_result: a significant surge in approvals since 2018 with clear radiology dominance, reliance on the 510(k) pathway, and underrepresentation of pediatric-focused devices and trials

model_family: radiomics with three feature selection methods and four classifiers compared
patient_population: 51 children (24 ependymoma, 27 medulloblastoma)
clinical_problem: telling ependymoma from medulloblastoma in a child, when the two look alike in age, location and symptoms
model_description: Extracts radiomic features from contrast-enhanced T1 and apparent diffusion coefficient maps of semi-automatically segmented tumors and classifies which of the two common posterior fossa tumors it is. Twelve combinations of feature selection and classifier were compared, which is the honest way to do this on 51 patients; the authors note explicitly that no single combination is best for every dataset.
title: Differentiation Between Ependymoma and Medulloblastoma in Children with Radiomics Approach.
headline_result: best model (logistic feature selection with random forest) reached AUC 0.91 (95% CI 0.787-0.968)

patient_population: children imaged in radiology practice
clinical_problem: which parts of the pediatric imaging pathway AI could plausibly improve
model_description: Walks the pediatric patient pathway and asks, at each step, where AI has been shown feasible and where it has not, borrowing from the adult literature to propose targets. Its opening observation is the important one for this database: cancer screening AI has had enormous attention while children's imaging has been neglected, which is a statement about where development effort has gone rather than where the clinical need is.
title: Artificial intelligence in paediatric radiology: Future opportunities.

model_family: deep learning noise reduction applied to virtual monoenergetic dual-energy reconstructions
patient_population: 29 pediatric patients aged 2-19 years, each with a prior standard single-energy CT for comparison
clinical_problem: reducing both radiation dose and iodinated contrast load in children undergoing abdominal CT
model_description: Combines two dose-sparing ideas that are usually studied separately: dual-energy acquisition with reduced iodine concentration, and deep-learning denoising of the resulting low-energy virtual monoenergetic images. Each alone increases noise; together they held image quality while cutting radiation by about 20% and iodine by 14%. Contrast load matters independently of dose in children with repeated imaging or impaired renal function.
title: Noise reduction approach in pediatric abdominal CT combining deep learning and dual-energy technique.
headline_result: overall and diagnostic image quality maintained against standard single-energy CT, with 19.6% lower dose index and 14.3% lower total iodine administration

patient_population: children undergoing bone age assessment
clinical_problem: bone age assessment in pediatric endocrinology, sixty years after the atlases were published
model_description: An endocrinology-side overview of how bone age is measured now. It covers the Greulich-Pyle and Tanner-Whitehouse atlases, the automated programs that have been validated against them (which are precise, remove inter- and intra-rater variability and cut reading time), and the radiation-free alternatives using ultrasound or MRI that are the least-developed part of this field.
journal: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology
title: Traditional and New Methods of Bone Age Assessment-An Overview.

model_family: radiomics signature combined with clinical factors in a nomogram
patient_population: 78 children with neuroblastoma (55 training, 23 test)
clinical_problem: predicting MYCN amplification in neuroblastoma, which determines risk group and therapy
model_description: A second, independent CT radiomics attempt at MYCN status in neuroblastoma, on a smaller cohort than the other in this database. It reports that both pre- and post-contrast phases contribute, and that adding clinical factors to the radiomics signature clearly beats a clinical model alone. Two independent groups reaching similar conclusions on this question is worth more than either result on its own.
title: Radiogenomics of neuroblastoma in pediatric patients: CT-based radiomics signature in predicting MYCN amplification.
headline_result: combined clinical-radiomics nomogram AUC 0.95 in training and 0.91 in testing, against 0.82 and 0.70 for the clinical model alone

model_family: CNN with joint spatial, channel and scale attention
body_region: placenta and fetal brain (and skin lesions, non-radiologic)
patient_population: fetuses imaged with MRI; a second application uses dermoscopic skin lesion images
clinical_problem: segmenting the placenta and fetal brain on fetal MRI
model_description: Takes a fetal MRI slice and returns a segmentation of the placenta or fetal brain, using three kinds of attention so the network weighs the right location, the right feature channels and the right scale at once. The attention maps can be displayed, which is the paper's explainability claim. It is about fifteen times smaller than a comparable state-of-the-art segmentation network.
release_evidence: our code is available at https://github.com/HiLab-git/CA-Net
title: CA-Net: Comprehensive Attention Convolutional Neural Networks for Explainable Medical Image Segmentation.
headline_result: Dice improved over U-Net from 84.79% to 87.08% for the placenta and 93.20% to 95.88% for the fetal brain

model_family: similarity network fusion across imaging and behavioral measures
patient_population: 176 children aged 6-16 with autism, ADHD or OCD from the POND network, all scanned on the same 3T scanner
clinical_problem: whether the diagnostic boundaries between autism, ADHD and OCD correspond to anything in the brain
model_description: Fuses cortical thickness, subcortical volume, white matter anisotropy and behavioral measures into a single similarity structure, then finds groups that cut across the three diagnoses. The four resulting transdiagnostic groups differed in everyday adaptive functioning, which the DSM categories did not capture as well. Scanning all children on one scanner removes the usual site confound.
journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
title: Integration of brain and behavior measures for identification of data-driven groups cutting across children with ASD, ADHD, or OCD.
headline_result: four transdiagnostic groups driven mainly by cortical thickness in socio-emotional and attention networks plus inattention symptoms; groups remained stable across resampling and differed significantly in adaptive functioning

model_family: deep-learning CT reconstruction algorithm
patient_population: children undergoing clinical CT (19 patients, mean age 11 years)
clinical_problem: keeping diagnostic image quality on pediatric CT while cutting radiation dose
model_description: Reconstructs the CT image from the raw projection data with a trained network in place of filtered back projection or iterative reconstruction, removing noise without the waxy texture model-based iterative reconstruction introduces. Assessed both by a mathematical observer model across object sizes and contrasts and by three pediatric radiologists scoring edge definition, noise and conspicuity of low-contrast structures.
release_evidence: the abstract does not say whether the algorithm is a vendor product or research software
title: Improving Image Quality and Reducing Radiation Dose for Pediatric CT by Using Deep Learning Reconstruction.
study_design: retrospective single-center image-quality study with reader assessment
headline_result: object detectability improved 51% over filtered back projection, 18% over statistical iterative and 11% over model-based iterative reconstruction; radiologists preferred it (7.0 vs 6.2, 6.2 and 4.6); 52% greater dose reduction than statistical iterative reconstruction

model_family: support vector machine with recursive feature elimination on FreeSurfer cortical measures
patient_population: 66 adolescents and young adults with major depressive disorder
clinical_problem: separating adolescents with depression who have attempted suicide from those with ideation only
model_description: Takes structural MRI cortical thickness and volume measures and classifies whether a depressed adolescent has attempted suicide or has ideation without attempt. The top-ranked features were orbitofrontal and cingulate thickness. The clinical framing is risk stratification for prevention, though the design is cross-sectional so it separates groups rather than predicting a future attempt.
title: Identification of suicidality in adolescent major depressive disorder patients using sMRI: A machine learning approach.
headline_result: 78.6% cross-validated balanced accuracy (sensitivity 73.2%, specificity 84.0%, positive predictive value 88.2%)

model_family: encoder-decoder convolutional neural network
patient_population: 200 children with obstructive hydrocephalus from four pediatric hospitals plus 199 controls, with external testing at a fifth hospital
clinical_problem: tracking ventricular size objectively over time in children with hydrocephalus, which currently drives shunt decisions by eye
model_description: Takes a T2-weighted MRI and returns the ventricles outlined and their volume in about a second and a half. Built deliberately for clinical use rather than research: trained across four pediatric hospitals, tested at a fifth, and benchmarked against FreeSurfer, which it beat on both accuracy and speed. Serial volumes rather than subjective impression are what would change hydrocephalus management.
title: Artificial intelligence for automatic cerebral ventricle segmentation and volume calculation: a clinical tool for the evaluation of pediatric hydrocephalus.
study_design: retrospective multicenter study with external validation
dataset_size: 399 children across four hospitals, plus an external dataset from a fifth
headline_result: Dice 0.901 overall (0.946 in hydrocephalus), 0.926 on external data from a fifth hospital, more accurate than FreeSurfer at 1.48 seconds per scan

model_family: 3D patch-based U-net networks, one per modality
patient_population: 80 children with neuroblastoma or Wilms tumour
clinical_problem: choosing between proton and photon radiotherapy for a child, which currently requires planning both
model_description: Predicts what the proton and the photon dose distribution would look like for a specific child's anatomy, without running either planning process. Two radiation oncologists then chose a modality from the predicted organ-at-risk dose difference and reached the same decision as from the fully planned distributions in 18 of 20 patients. The intended use is explicit: to identify the better technique where proton planning expertise or capacity is not available.
journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
title: Deep learning prediction of proton and photon dose distributions for paediatric abdominal tumours.
study_design: retrospective single-center technical validation with clinician assessment
dataset_size: 80 children (60 for training with 5-fold cross-validation, 20 for inference)
headline_result: dose-volume histogram differences within 6% of planned distributions; identical modality selection in 18 of 20 patients

model_family: fully convolutional network with deep attentive modules, mixed kernel convolutions, deep supervision and residual connections
patient_population: reconstructed fetal brain MRI of fetuses scanned at 16 to 39 weeks gestation (mean 28.6 +/- 5.3)
clinical_problem: segmenting the fetal cortical plate, the measurement that quantitative studies of cortical folding and brain maturation depend on and that is otherwise refined by hand
model_description: A segmentation network built around the specific difficulty of this structure: the cortical plate is thin relative to the resolution of reconstructed fetal MRI, partial volume is severe, and its shape changes continuously across the second and third trimesters. Attention modules with mixed kernel sizes are the response. Under a minute per brain, which is what makes population-scale studies of cortical folding practical.
title: A Deep Attentive Convolutional Neural Network for Automatic Cortical Plate Segmentation in Fetal MRI.
study_design: retrospective model development with expert evaluation
headline_result: average Dice 0.87, Hausdorff distance 0.96 mm and symmetric surface difference 0.28 mm, outperforming several state-of-the-art deep models and a multi-atlas method

model_family: symmetricity-driven pair-of-cube Siamese convolutional neural network over 386 symmetry features
patient_population: 201 pediatric patients with temporal lobe epilepsy and 24 age-matched controls who underwent 18F-FDG PET-CT
clinical_problem: localizing the epileptic focus on 18F-FDG PET in children with temporal lobe epilepsy, where the focus may be either hypo- or hyper-metabolic with no clear boundary and misdiagnosis is common
model_description: The architecture encodes the way a nuclear medicine physician actually reads these studies - by comparing the two hemispheres - as a Siamese network over paired cubes, and then reports the metabolic abnormality of the predicted focus as an asymmetry index. Comparison is against the three things it would replace: visual assessment, SPM, and a divergence-based logistic regression. Dice around 0.5 sounds modest until read against expert visual assessment at 0.31 to 0.44 on the same cases.
journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
title: A deep learning framework for 18F-FDG PET imaging diagnosis in pediatric patients with temporal lobe epilepsy.
headline_result: Dice 0.51 for focus localization versus 0.24 for SPM (P < 0.01) and 0.31-0.44 for visual assessment; classification AUC 0.93 versus 0.72 for logistic regression

model_family: V-Net with attention gates, deep supervision and a multi-scale loss
patient_population: fetuses across trimesters in the public HC18 challenge dataset (355 test images)
clinical_problem: measuring head circumference from a fetal ultrasound image automatically
model_description: Segments the fetal skull on a 2D ultrasound image, then fits an ellipse to it and reports head circumference. Attention gates and deep supervision are what lift it above plain U-Net and V-Net on this task, which is hard because the appearance of the fetal head changes markedly between trimesters. Benchmarked on a public challenge, so the numbers are directly comparable with other entries.
release_evidence: the code of DAG V-Net will be made available publicly on https://github.com/xiaojinmao-code/
title: Fetal Ultrasound Image Segmentation for Automatic Head Circumference Biometry Using Deeply Supervised Attention-Gated V-Net.
study_design: technical development on a public benchmark
dataset_size: HC18 challenge training set with augmentation; 355 test images
headline_result: Dice 97.93%, head circumference absolute difference 1.77 ± 1.69 mm, Hausdorff distance 1.29 ± 0.79 mm; fifth place in the HC18 challenge

model_family: 30 competing deep-learning segmentation methods, 8 reviewed in detail
patient_population: 6-month-old infants; training from UNC, testing from UNC/UMN, Stanford and Emory with different protocols and scanners
clinical_problem: segmenting 6-month infant brain MRI, and whether any method survives being moved to another site's scanner
model_description: A challenge report rather than a single model. Thirty teams segmented 6-month infant brain MRI into white matter, gray matter and CSF, at the age when the two tissues are nearly isointense and conventional tools fail. The design deliberately puts the test data at different institutions from the training data, and the conclusion is the useful one: multi-site consistency remains unsolved, so a model that works on one scanner should not be assumed to work on another.
title: Multi-Site Infant Brain Segmentation Algorithms: The iSeg-2019 Challenge.
headline_result: top methods reviewed across whole brain, regions of interest and gyral landmarks; multi-site consistency identified as still an open issue

model_family: deep neural network classification models on structural MRI
patient_population: children and adults with ADHD and controls, drawn from ENIGMA-ADHD consortium samples
clinical_problem: whether the structural brain signature of ADHD in children is the same one seen in adults, tested by asking a model trained on one age group to classify the other
model_description: A study that uses classification accuracy as a hypothesis test rather than as a product claim. The interesting result is the cross-age transfer: a model trained only on adults still separated children with ADHD from controls, which is evidence that the anatomy the network keys on is continuous from childhood into adulthood. Prediction was stronger in children than adults, consistent with the ENIGMA effect sizes.
title: Evidence for similar structural brain anomalies in youth and adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a machine learning analysis.
headline_result: structural MRI significantly separated ADHD from control in both children and adults, and the adult-trained model significantly predicted ADHD in the child sample

model_family: convolutional neural network taking paired ultra-low-dose PET and MRI input
patient_population: 33 children and young adults aged 3-30 with lymphoma undergoing whole-body FDG PET/MRI
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: cutting the radiation burden of repeated staging PET scans in children with cancer
model_description: Takes a simulated 6.25% dose PET scan together with the MRI acquired at the same time and outputs an image that behaves like a standard-dose PET. What makes this credible is that it checks the quantitative measure clinicians act on: SUVmax, which noise inflates at ultra-low dose, was restored to standard-dose values, and reader confidence agreed with the standard scans far better than with the low-dose ones.
journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
title: Artificial intelligence enables whole-body positron emission tomography scans with minimal radiation exposure.
study_design: retrospective single-center study with reader assessment
dataset_size: 33 children and young adults with lymphoma
headline_result: reader agreement with standard clinical scans kappa 0.942 for AI-reconstructed images versus 0.650 for 6.25% dose images; SUVmax restored to standard-dose values

model_family: multitask scheme of three convolutional networks - feature extraction, class prediction and region proposal
patient_population: fetal head, abdominal and heart standard-plane images
clinical_problem: quality control of 2D fetal sonographic standard planes, the labor-intensive check that biometry and anomaly diagnosis depend on and that currently needs a professional sonographer
model_description: Operationalizes the criterion sonographers actually apply - every essential anatomical structure present, complete and clearly bounded - by having the network identify each structure, judge whether it meets standard, and say where it is. Quality control rather than measurement, which is the step upstream of everything else and the one most automation skips. Under a second per image.
title: Automatic quality assessment for 2D fetal sonographic standard plane based on multitask learning.
headline_result: quality assessment of a fetal sonographic image in under a second, with segmentation and diagnosis competitive with state-of-the-art methods

model_family: convolutional neural network on three-dimensional depth sensor images of the back
patient_population: 160 subjects suspected to have adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, from a consecutive prospectively collected series at five scoliosis centers in Japan
clinical_problem: screening for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis without radiation, by predicting the Cobb angle from a surface scan rather than from a radiograph
model_description: Existing scoliosis screening methods - forward bend test, scoliometer - detect asymmetry but predict the Cobb angle poorly, and that is the specific gap this fills: a depth sensor plus a network that outputs a number on the same scale clinicians decide with. The reported accuracy is framed at the two thresholds that matter, 10 degrees for calling it scoliosis and 20 degrees for considering a brace, which is more useful than a bare correlation. Five centers and ten repeats of five-fold cross-validation.
journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
title: An algorithm for using deep learning convolutional neural networks with three dimensional depth sensor imaging in scoliosis detection.
study_design: retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected multicenter series
headline_result: correlation 0.91 with the actual Cobb angle, mean absolute error 4.0 degrees and RMSE 5.4 degrees; 94% accuracy at the 10-degree threshold and 89% at 20 degrees

model_family: deep learning temporal video segmentation followed by automated workflow description
patient_population: full-length routine second-trimester fetal ultrasound scans, over 200 hours of recordings
clinical_problem: characterizing how sonographers actually perform a routine anomaly scan, so that scanning skill, scan time and machine interfaces can be studied at scale
model_description: Not a diagnostic model at all, and that is the point - it treats the scan itself as the object of study. The network temporally segments a full-length recording into semantically meaningful segments, turning an unwatchable archive of 200 hours into a structured description of operator behavior. The stated uses are training sonographers, optimizing scan times and designing better machine interfaces, which is the non-interpretive side of imaging AI that pediatric and fetal services rarely have data on.
title: Knowledge representation and learning of operator clinical workflow from full-length routine fetal ultrasound scan videos.
dataset_size: more than 200 hours of full-length routine scan video
headline_result: first fully-automatic framework to describe operator clinical workflow from full-length routine second-trimester scan video

model_family: convolutional network with a learned pairwise attention module, trained self-supervised by inverting a slice-sampling process
patient_population: 2D slices sampled from 3D fetal brain volumes at 18-22 weeks gestational age, then real 2D transthalamic plane images and freehand scan video
clinical_problem: locating where a 2D fetal neurosonography image sits in 3D atlas space, the alignment step that standard plane finding and any 3D interpretation depend on
