model_description: The annotation problem is dissolved rather than solved: instead of labeling each 2D scan with its 3D position, slices are sampled from volumes and the network is trained to invert the sampling, so supervision is free. It takes a set of images rather than one and learns which pairs to weight, so accuracy improves as more images from the same scan are given - useful, since a real examination produces a stream, not a single frame. It transfers to real standard-plane images and to freehand video.
title: Learning to map 2D ultrasound images into 3D space with minimal human annotation.
dataset_size: 3D fetal brain volumes at 18-22 weeks, plus real 2D images and freehand video
headline_result: outperforms the baseline by up to 23% on Euclidean distance, plane angle and normalized cross correlation as the number of input images grows, and matches human annotation on real transthalamic plane images

model_family: extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) over 651 radiomic features per MRI sequence, with feature selection
patient_population: 109 patients from three academic centers, 60 of them pediatric (55%); 50 H3K27M-mutant and 59 wild-type
clinical_problem: predicting H3K27M mutation status in midline gliomas non-invasively, a molecular marker with prognostic weight that conventional MRI features do not distinguish
model_description: A radiogenomics model for a tumor - diffuse midline glioma - where tissue is often not obtainable and the mutation defines the entity. The motivation is stated as a negative result from the prior literature: enhancement, necrosis and edema rates vary and none separates mutant from wild-type, so the signal, if there is one, is in texture rather than in anything a radiologist reports. Multi-institutional, majority pediatric, but a single random split of 109 patients and test performance below training, so the estimate is fragile.
title: Machine Learning-Based Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging Radiomics for Prediction of H3K27M Mutation in Midline Gliomas.
headline_result: AUC 0.791 training and 0.737 test; test accuracy 72.7%, precision 76.5%, recall 72.2%, F1 74.3%

model_family: cross-validated elastic-net regression on multimodal imaging features
patient_population: children aged 9-10 in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study
clinical_problem: identifying which 9-10 year olds will gain weight pathologically over the following year
model_description: Uses structural, diffusion, resting-state and task-based MRI to model current body mass index and, separately, to predict pathological weight gain a year later. Structural features generalized to held-out data and predicted future pathological gain; functional and reward-task measures did not. The practical reading is that the cheap, routinely acquired structural sequence carried the signal and the elaborate functional paradigms did not.
title: Multimodal brain predictors of current weight and weight gain in children enrolled in the ABCD study ®.
headline_result: structural features explained 27% of held-out variance in body mass index and predicted pathological weight gain with area under the curve 0.83 in both training and test sets

model_family: paired U-Net models for level localization and muscle segmentation
patient_population: 370 patients sampled uniformly from 0 to 18 years and across both sexes
clinical_problem: measuring skeletal muscle mass on CT, a marker of nutritional status and sarcopenia, which requires finding the L3 level and outlining muscle by hand
model_description: Two problems in one pipeline: locating the L3 vertebral level on the sagittal reformat, then segmenting muscle on the corresponding axial slice. Sampling uniformly across ages from birth to 18 is the design choice that makes it pediatric rather than adult-with-children-included, since body habitus changes completely over that range. Level localization landed within the slice thickness.
title: Automated Segmentation of Abdominal Skeletal Muscle on Pediatric CT Scans Using Deep Learning.
headline_result: L3 localization error 3.23 ± 2.61 mm, within the reconstructed slice thickness; muscle segmentation Dice 0.93 ± 0.03

model_family: LASSO Cox regression on wavelet-filtered radiomic features
patient_population: 177 treatment-naive children with diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma from an international cohort, split into training and independent testing sets
clinical_problem: prognostication in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma, a uniformly fatal childhood tumor that is rarely biopsied
model_description: Predicts overall survival from texture features of the routine T1-post-contrast and T2 images at diagnosis, before any treatment. It beats a clinical-only model built from age and sex, and holds up in an independent test set, though the concordance drops from 0.70 to 0.59 when it does. For a tumor where biopsy is often avoided and MRI is the only longitudinal measure, an objective imaging prognostic is worth having even at that accuracy.
title: MRI-based radiomics for prognosis of pediatric diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma: an international study.
headline_result: concordance 0.68 for radiomics versus 0.57 for clinical variables alone in training; 0.59 in the independent testing dataset (P = .02)

model_family: ensemble of neural networks with segmentation models
patient_population: fetuses at 18 to 24 weeks undergoing screening ultrasound or echocardiography
clinical_problem: prenatal detection of complex congenital heart disease on screening ultrasound
model_description: Takes a whole fetal ultrasound survey, picks out the five recommended cardiac views, and classifies the heart as normal or complex congenital heart disease, while separate segmentation models compute standard cardiothoracic measurements. It addresses a specific failure of practice: the five screening views can detect 90% of complex disease, but real-world sensitivity is nearer 30%. Performance held up on outside-hospital and lower-quality images.
title: An ensemble of neural networks provides expert-level prenatal detection of complex congenital heart disease.
dataset_size: 107,823 training images from 1,326 echocardiograms and screening ultrasounds; internal test set of 4,108 fetal surveys and over 4.4 million images
headline_result: AUC 0.99, sensitivity 95%, specificity 96%, negative predictive value 100%; sensitivity comparable to clinicians

model_family: random forest, gradient boosting and logistic regression compared
patient_population: 430 children and adolescents aged 0-18 with suspected appendicitis
clinical_problem: three separate decisions in suspected pediatric appendicitis: is it appendicitis, does it need surgery, and is it complicated
model_description: Combines history, examination, laboratory values and abdominal ultrasound findings to predict diagnosis, management and severity at once, which no earlier model had done. The authors also identified small subsets of 6 to 18 predictors that performed as well as all 38, and deployed the result as a free online tool. Severity, the target that would justify antibiotics instead of surgery, remains the weakest of the three.
release_evidence: deployed as an open access easy-to-use online tool (the Appendicitis Prediction Tool)
title: Using Machine Learning to Predict the Diagnosis, Management and Severity of Pediatric Appendicitis.
headline_result: area under the precision-recall curve 0.94 for diagnosis, 0.92 for management and 0.70 for severity

model_family: unsupervised deep image prior with a learned temporal manifold
patient_population: fetuses in retrospective and real fetal cardiac MRI datasets
clinical_problem: reconstructing a moving fetal heart from sparsely sampled dynamic MRI without cardiac gating
model_description: Reconstructs a dynamic MRI series by fitting a network to that one patient's measurements, with no prior training and no other data. For fetal cardiac imaging this matters because there is no reliable heartbeat signal to gate on, and this method needs none: a low-dimensional manifold encodes the temporal variation and a convolutional network generates the image series consistent with the acquired k-space.
title: Time-Dependent Deep Image Prior for Dynamic MRI.
headline_result: outperformed state-of-the-art methods quantitatively and qualitatively on retrospective and real fetal cardiac datasets

model_family: radiomics with four classifiers compared, combined into a nomogram
patient_population: 172 children with abdominal neuroblastoma, 47 MYCN-amplified and 125 not
clinical_problem: identifying MYCN amplification in neuroblastoma, which defines the high-risk group and currently requires tissue
model_description: Extracts radiomic features from three-phase CT and predicts whether the tumor is MYCN-amplified, then folds the signature into a nomogram with clinicopathological and radiographic variables. If it held up prospectively it would let risk stratification start from the staging CT rather than waiting on genetics, which matters most where molecular testing is slow or unavailable.
title: CT-Based Radiomics Signature With Machine Learning Predicts MYCN Amplification in Pediatric Abdominal Neuroblastoma.
headline_result: training AUC 0.940 for logistic and support vector machine models, 0.927 for random forest and 0.780 for Bayes

model_family: unrolled deep-learning reconstruction with separable 3D convolutions and data consistency steps
patient_population: 50 children and young adults aged 5-30 (mean 16 years) undergoing cardiac MRI at a children's hospital, prospectively scanned with both sequences
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: getting ventricular volumes and mass in children without repeated breath-holds
model_description: Reconstructs a 12-fold accelerated free-breathing cine cardiac MRI, so a child gets ventricular volumetry in about a minute of free breathing instead of three minutes of repeated breath-holds. The honest result is a trade: image quality scored slightly lower than the reference sequence, but the volumetric measurements two radiologists derived from it agreed closely, which is what the examination is actually for.
title: Free-breathing Accelerated Cardiac MRI Using Deep Learning: Validation in Children and Young Adults.
dataset_size: trained on 10 adult volunteers; prospectively validated in 50 children and young adults
headline_result: acquisition time 0.9 versus 3.0 minutes (P < .001); image quality 3.8 versus 4.3 on a five-point scale; intraclass correlation 0.76-0.97 for all measurements

model_family: vendor deep learning CT reconstruction algorithm, high setting (DLIR-H)
patient_population: 46 children (mean age 5.9 +/- 4.2 years) scanned at 70 kVp with 0.8-1.2 ml/kg contrast, versus 46 age-matched controls at 100 kVp with 1.3-1.8 ml/kg
clinical_problem: cutting both radiation and iodinated contrast dose in pediatric chest CT angiography, where iterative reconstruction runs out of headroom at low dose and 100 kVp gives too little enhancement at low contrast dose
model_description: The clearest pediatric statement of what deep learning reconstruction actually buys: it is spent on lowering two doses at once. Dropping to 70 kVp raises vascular enhancement but also noise, and DLIR absorbs the noise, so the child receives 11 percent less radiation and 24 percent less contrast and the images come out quieter and better enhanced than the standard protocol. A vendor algorithm evaluated in clinical practice rather than a research model.
release_evidence: a vendor deep learning image reconstruction algorithm running on the clinical CT scanner, evaluated against the scanner's adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction-V
title: Performance evaluation of a deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) algorithm in "double low" chest CTA in children: a feasibility study.
study_design: prospective feasibility study with two-reader qualitative scoring
dataset_size: 46 children in the study group and 46 age-matched controls
headline_result: dose-length-product down 11.2% (p = 0.01) and contrast dose down 24% (p < 0.001), with higher aortic enhancement (416.5 vs 342.0 HU) and lower noise (15.1 vs 18.6 HU), both p < 0.001

model_family: differentially private stochastic gradient descent framework for PyTorch
patient_population: children in the public pediatric pneumonia chest radiograph dataset, plus an adult liver segmentation benchmark
clinical_problem: training diagnostic models on children's images without exposing individual patients
model_description: Not a diagnostic model but the plumbing beneath one: an open-source framework that trains networks under formal differential privacy guarantees, so that what the model learns cannot be traced back to an individual child. Demonstrated on pediatric pneumonia classification and liver segmentation, with the finding that rigorous privacy costs some classification accuracy but very little segmentation accuracy. Relevant to any children's hospital weighing data sharing against consent.
release_evidence: deepee is presented as a free-and-open-source framework for use with PyTorch
title: Medical imaging deep learning with differential privacy.
dataset_size: the pediatric pneumonia dataset and the Medical Segmentation Decathlon liver dataset
headline_result: acceptable classification and excellent segmentation performance under formal privacy guarantees, with favorable memory and compute against other frameworks

model_family: deep learning image reconstruction compared against filtered back projection and iterative reconstruction
patient_population: 50 children undergoing low-dose axial head CT with age-dependent tube current
clinical_problem: seeing small intracranial lesions on a low-dose pediatric head CT at thin slice thickness
model_description: Tests the specific claim that matters for thin-slice head CT: only the deep-learning reconstruction produced diagnostically usable 0.625 mm images, and those images had the same noise as conventional 5 mm images while showing more lesions (69 against 65). The authors translate that into a dose implication of roughly 85% if current image quality and slice thickness were the target.
release_evidence: compares vendor reconstruction options available on the scanner
title: Application of a deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) algorithm in head CT imaging for children to improve image quality and lesion detection.
headline_result: 0.625 mm deep-learning images matched 5 mm iterative images on noise and quality while detecting 69 versus 65 lesions, implying up to 85% potential dose reduction

model_family: vendor deep learning CT reconstruction, high setting (DLIR-H)
patient_population: 33 children scanned at 70 kVp with automatic tube current modulation and 0.8-1.2 mL/kg contrast
clinical_problem: keeping thin-slice pediatric chest CT angiography diagnostic at low radiation dose and low contrast volume, where iterative reconstruction over-smooths and loses arterial margins
model_description: The complement to the same group's larger comparison study: here the comparator is not a standard-dose protocol but the two iterative reconstruction strengths at the same low dose, which isolates what the network adds. The finding is qualitative rather than numerical - 100% ASIR-V matched DLIR on measured noise but produced over-smoothed artery margins, and only DLIR-H was acceptable on all three subjective criteria. Noise numbers alone would have missed that.
release_evidence: a vendor deep learning image reconstruction algorithm on the clinical CT scanner, compared against the scanner's ASIR-V
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: Improving the image quality of pediatric chest CT angiography with low radiation dose and contrast volume using deep learning image reconstruction.
study_design: retrospective image quality study with two-reader consensus scoring
headline_result: aortic noise 19.24 +/- 5.77 HU with DLIR-H versus 29.45 +/- 7.59 HU with 50% ASIR-V (p<0.001), at CTDIvol 1.37 +/- 0.29 mGy and 25.43 +/- 13.32 mL contrast; only DLIR-H acceptable on all three qualitative criteria

model_family: supervised classifiers - support vector machines, neural networks, random forest, logistic regression, naive Bayes and k-nearest neighbour
patient_population: 828 children admitted with traumatic brain injury to a trauma center in southern Thailand between January 2009 and July 2020, all of whom had a brain CT; median age 72 months
clinical_problem: predicting functional outcome after pediatric traumatic brain injury, from the vital signs, Glasgow coma scale and intracranial injury characteristics available on admission
model_description: A prognostic model built on the features a trauma team already has, including the characteristics of the intracranial injuries read off the CT - a head CT was an inclusion requirement. Outcome is the King's Outcome Scale for Childhood Head Injury dichotomized into favourable and unfavourable, which keeps the target clinically legible. Six algorithms are compared on the same 70/30 split rather than one being tuned and reported.
journal: Chinese journal of traumatology = Zhonghua chuang shang za zhi
title: Application of machine learning to predict the outcome of pediatric traumatic brain injury.
headline_result: machine learning models trained on admission clinical and CT injury characteristics predicted dichotomized functional outcome in the held-out 30%

model_family: low-memory 3D U-Net
patient_population: children including those with cystic fibrosis, adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease from a lung cancer screening trial, and the public EXACT'09 dataset
clinical_problem: extracting the airway tree from chest CT, which quantitative assessment of cystic fibrosis lung disease depends on
model_description: Segments the airway tree from a chest CT in a single pass over large 3D patches, often the whole lungs at once, which keeps the method simple and fast. Validated deliberately across three very different datasets, one of them pediatric cystic fibrosis, to show it does not depend on the disease or acquisition it was tuned on. Generalization across datasets is the claim, not just accuracy on one.
title: Automatic airway segmentation from computed tomography using robust and efficient 3-D convolutional neural networks.
dataset_size: three datasets including a pediatric cystic fibrosis cohort and the public EXACT'09 set
headline_result: highly complete airway trees with few false positives across all three datasets; second highest sensitivity among methods reporting good specificity on EXACT'09

model_family: ensemble of eight machine learning models over cervical vertebrae morphometric ratios plus age and sex
patient_population: 499 paired hand-wrist radiographs and lateral cephalograms from 455 orthodontic patients aged 6-18 years, collected at two university hospitals and a paediatric dental clinic
clinical_problem: estimating hand-wrist skeletal maturation stage from the lateral cephalogram already taken for orthodontics, so that treatment timing can be judged without a second radiograph of the hand
model_description: Radiation arithmetic rather than accuracy chasing: the growth information is inferred from a film the patient is already getting, which removes the hand-wrist radiograph from the pathway entirely. Features are explicit and interpretable - width-height, width-perpendicular-height and concavity ratios from 13 cervical vertebra landmarks - and adding chronological age and sex improved prediction, which is worth noting since those are free.
title: Prediction of hand-wrist maturation stages based on cervical vertebrae images using artificial intelligence.
headline_result: mean absolute error 0.90 Fishman stages (round MAE 0.87, RMSE 1.20) under five-fold cross-validation

model_family: convolutional neural network trained on synthesized fetal-like diffusion data
patient_population: fetal brain scans, with high-quality scans of prematurely-born newborns used to generate training data; 100 fetal test scans for accuracy, 20 for precision and expert review
clinical_problem: estimating diffusion parameters from fetal DW-MRI, where fetal motion and low SNR defeat standard fitting
model_description: The contribution is the training data, not the network. Reliable fetal diffusion ground truth does not exist, so the authors estimate accurate parameter maps from high-quality newborn scans and then degrade them to match the fetal measurement scheme and noise distribution - manufacturing a fetal training set out of neonatal data. This is a reusable pattern for any pediatric imaging problem where the population of interest cannot be imaged well enough to label.
title: Deep learning-based parameter estimation in fetal diffusion-weighted MRI.
study_design: retrospective methods development with expert reader assessment
dataset_size: 100 fetal scans for accuracy, 20 for precision, 20 for expert quality assessment
headline_result: significantly lower reconstruction error (n=100, p<0.001) and higher precision (n=20, p<0.001) than standard estimation, with better expert-rated quality in 11 regions of interest

patient_population: pregnancies across gestation
clinical_problem: the repetitive parts of obstetric ultrasound: positioning, structure identification, gestational age, and real-time quality assurance
task: detection / diagnosis; measurement / quantification; workflow / non-interpretive
model_description: A review that frames AI in obstetric ultrasound around repetition rather than diagnosis: the tasks worth automating are the ones done identically many times per scan. It also makes a point rarely stated in this literature, that realizing any of it depends on interdisciplinary communication between the people building the models and the sonographers who would use them.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Obstetric Ultrasound: An Update and Future Applications.

model_family: Boruta feature selection with multiple kernel learning fusing structural MRI, functional MRI and diffusion tensor features, classified by a support vector machine
patient_population: comorbidity-free children with ADHD and covariable-matched healthy children aged 9-10 from the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development (ABCD) study
clinical_problem: diagnosing ADHD in early adolescence, where current criteria rest on behavior analysis that is subjective and inconsistent especially in children
model_description: Fusion at the kernel level rather than by concatenating features, which is the point of the paper - it is compared directly against early feature fusion and against each modality alone, and wins. The cohort design is unusually clean for this literature: comorbidity-free cases, covariable-matched controls, a narrow 9-10 age band, drawn from ABCD. The resulting AUC of 0.698 is the sober number that clean design produces, and it is a useful calibration against the higher figures reported on less controlled samples.
title: Multimodal MR Images-Based Diagnosis of Early Adolescent Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Using Multiple Kernel Learning.
study_design: retrospective model development on a public cohort
dataset_size: ABCD subjects aged 9-10, size not stated in the abstract
headline_result: AUC 0.698 and accuracy 64.3%, significantly better than early feature fusion or any single modality

model_family: convolutional neural network reconstruction engines
patient_population: children undergoing CT for a range of clinical indications
clinical_problem: getting diagnostic image quality out of low-dose CT in the population where dose matters most
model_description: A RadioGraphics review of deep-learning CT reconstruction for children: how the engines are trained on paired low-dose and high-dose data to tell true attenuation from noise, how the resulting images look and behave differently from filtered back projection and iterative reconstruction, and what dose reduction is achievable in practice. Written for a department deciding whether to adopt what is already a purchasable scanner option.
release_evidence: deep learning-based reconstruction has been introduced to overcome the limitations of the FBP and IR approaches and is currently available clinically
journal: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc
title: Deep Learning-based Reconstruction for Lower-Dose Pediatric CT: Technical Principles, Image Characteristics, and Clinical Implementations.

model_family: self-attentive capsule network with two-stage transfer learning, on a region of interest centered at the curve apex
patient_population: skeletally immature patients (Risser <= 2) with 11-30 degree curves presenting between October 2015 and April 2020: 328 for training and cross-validation, 110 for independent testing on biplanar EOS, plus 52 on standard PA radiographs for cross-platform validation
clinical_problem: telling at the first clinic visit which mild adolescent idiopathic scoliosis curves will progress, the prediction that decides who is braced and who is watched
model_description: Prior work showed three-dimensional morphology predicts progression but needed biplanar equipment and slow software reconstruction; this puts the same prediction on the plain standing PA radiograph every clinic already takes. The 3D reconstruction is used only to establish which parameters matter - apical rotation and torsion - and then discarded from the deployed pathway. The separate 52-patient cross-platform cohort on standard radiographs is the part that makes it portable beyond an EOS centre.
title: Application of deep learning upon spinal radiographs to predict progression in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis at first clinic visit.
study_design: retrospective cohort model development with cross-platform validation
headline_result: accuracy 76.6%, sensitivity 75.2%, specificity 80.2% for progressive versus non-progressive curves, outperforming conventional CNNs and a clinical parameter logistic regression

model_family: three-stage pipeline: Mask R-CNN pelvic bone segmentation, HRNet landmark localization, then measurement and classification
patient_population: 1265 pediatric pelvic radiographs for training and 133 from two other medical institutions for validation, with three orthopedic surgeons as comparators
clinical_problem: measuring and classifying developmental dysplasia of the hip on pediatric pelvic radiographs, where the acetabular index and centre-edge angle are drawn by hand and observers disagree
model_description: The decomposition matches how the measurement is actually made - find the ilium, pubis, ischium and femoral heads, then place the landmarks, then compute the angles - which makes each stage checkable. The result that matters clinically is not accuracy but variance: intraclass consistency across surgeons was 0.79-0.98 while the model's was 1.00, because a deterministic model measuring the same film twice cannot disagree with itself. It also matched an intermediate surgeon on Tonnis and IHDI grading, in less time.
title: A Deep-Learning Aided Diagnostic System in Assessing Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip on Pediatric Pelvic Radiographs.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation and observer comparison
headline_result: Tonnis and IHDI classification accuracy 0.86-0.95 for both hips; no statistically significant difference from surgeons on the numeric indices; intraclass consistency 1.00 for the model versus 0.79-0.98 among surgeons, and significantly faster

model_family: dynamic UNet built on the MONAI framework
patient_population: fetuses with suspected pathology, particularly spina bifida
clinical_problem: brain masking for super-resolution reconstruction of fetal MRI in spina bifida, where a failed localisation step forces manual correction
model_description: Replaces a two-step localise-then-segment pipeline with a single well-trained network, on the argument that the two-step design fails irrecoverably when localisation fails. It reduced outliers as well as improving average accuracy, which matters more here: super-resolution reconstruction is only automatic if the mask never needs a human. Built on MONAI, so it drops into existing fetal pipelines.
release_evidence: presented as a tool built on the open MONAI framework
title: MONAIfbs: MONAI-based fetal brain MRI deep learning segmentation
headline_result: single-step dynamic UNet outperformed the published two-step approach, including when that approach was retrained on the same expanded dataset, and reduced the number of outliers

model_family: residual network with dilated convolutions, transfer-learned
patient_population: children undergoing chest radiography for suspected pneumonia
clinical_problem: diagnosis of childhood pneumonia on chest radiographs
model_description: Takes a pediatric chest radiograph and returns a pneumonia classification, with dilated convolutions chosen so that going deeper does not throw away the spatial detail that locates the inflammatory area. Initialized from weights learned on large datasets in the same field because the pediatric data alone is too small. The authors argue it copes better with low-resolution images and partially obscured consolidation than earlier methods.
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
title: A transfer learning method with deep residual network for pediatric pneumonia diagnosis.
headline_result: recall 96.7% and F1 score 92.7% on the test set

model_family: multivariate classification on whole-brain functional connectivity
patient_population: 202 children and adults with Tourette syndrome and control subjects
clinical_problem: whether Tourette syndrome has an imaging signature, and whether it is the same signature in children as in adults
model_description: Classifies Tourette syndrome from functional connectivity separately in children and in adults, then asks whether either classifier transfers to the other age group. It does not, which is the finding: the connections that distinguish the disorder are age-specific. For anyone building pediatric models from adult data, this is a clean demonstration of why that assumption fails in a developmental disorder.
title: Atypical Functional Connectivity in Tourette Syndrome Differs Between Children and Adults.
headline_result: successful classification in children and adults separately, with no generalization across age groups

model_family: machine-learning pipeline on clinical and sonographic biometry features
patient_population: 686 singleton vaginal deliveries in Israel for derivation and 2,584 in California for validation, with 131 and 31 cases of shoulder dystocia
clinical_problem: predicting shoulder dystocia, so that Cesarean delivery for suspected macrosomia is offered to the right pregnancies
model_description: Uses sonographic fetal biometry, adjusted for gestational age at delivery, together with obstetric history to predict shoulder dystocia, and validates on a cohort from a different country and health system. It beat the current paradigm of estimated fetal weight plus maternal diabetes. Adjusted estimated fetal weight and abdominal circumference were the strongest imaging contributors, which is a check that the model is using the anatomy one would expect.
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Development and validation of a machine-learning model for prediction of shoulder dystocia.
headline_result: AUC 0.793 versus 0.745 for adjusted estimated fetal weight combined with diabetes (P = 1e-16)

model_family: three-network pipeline: basic CNN, deeper multi-task CNN, and an aggregated residual visual block detector
patient_population: fetuses undergoing cardiac screening ultrasound
clinical_problem: deciding whether a fetal cardiac four-chamber view is adequate to diagnose from
model_description: Scores the quality of a fetal four-chamber view in three steps: is this actually a four-chamber plane, are the gain and zoom right, and are the key anatomical structures visible. The three outputs combine into one quantitative score. It runs at 101 frames per second, which is fast enough to give the sonographer feedback while the probe is still on the abdomen.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: A Generic Quality Control Framework for Fetal Ultrasound Cardiac Four-Chamber Planes.
dataset_size: an institutional fetal ultrasound dataset; size not stated
headline_result: mean average precision 93.52% at 101 frames per second

model_family: two-stage CNN localization and segmentation plus outlier-robust super-resolution
patient_population: fetuses with normal brains and with varying ventriculomegaly associated with open spina bifida
clinical_problem: producing a usable high-resolution fetal brain volume from motion-corrupted stacks, including brains malformed by open spina bifida
model_description: A four-stage pipeline that takes the motion-corrupted 2D slice stacks of a fetal brain MRI and returns a high-resolution volume in standard anatomical space with no user input. One network finds the brain, a second segments it finely, then a super-resolution step reconstructs the volume. It removes the manual brain-masking step that has kept fetal volume reconstruction out of routine practice.
title: An automated framework for localization, segmentation and super-resolution reconstruction of fetal brain MRI.
headline_result: each stage outperformed state-of-the-art methods on segmentation and reconstruction, including expert-reader quality assessment

model_family: problem-based CNN architecture with transfer learning and custom preprocessing
patient_population: children in the pediatric chest X-ray dataset, with a separate dataset used to test generalization
clinical_problem: detecting consolidation on a child's chest radiograph
model_description: Argues that networks designed to win on ImageNet are the wrong shape for radiographs, and designs an architecture around the problem instead, with preprocessing chosen to preserve the information that consolidation lives in. It checks its own reasoning with an occlusion test showing which region drove each decision, and tests generalization on a second dataset rather than a held-out split of the same one.
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
title: Deep learning, reusable and problem-based architectures for detection of consolidation on chest X-ray images.
dataset_size: the pediatric chest X-ray dataset plus an external validation dataset
headline_result: 94.67% accuracy for consolidation detection, above the previously published architectures on the same dataset

model_family: dual-input CNN merging two ResNet branches
patient_population: children undergoing elbow radiography; 1,266 AP and lateral pairs for development, 258 for temporal testing and 95 from a second hospital
clinical_problem: detecting supracondylar fracture of the humerus in children on conventional radiographs
model_description: Reads the anteroposterior and lateral elbow radiographs together, as a radiologist does, by merging two networks rather than judging each view alone. Tested twice on data the model had never seen: a later year at the same hospital and a different hospital entirely. Its errors are asymmetric in a clinically useful direction, with very high negative predictive value and lower specificity, meaning it over-calls rather than misses.
title: Using a Dual-Input Convolutional Neural Network for Automated Detection of Pediatric Supracondylar Fracture on Conventional Radiography.
study_design: retrospective development with temporal and geographic external validation and reader study
dataset_size: 1,266 radiograph pairs for development; 258 temporal and 95 geographic external test pairs
headline_result: AUC 0.985 (temporal) and 0.992 (geographic) external test sets, comparable to human readers; geographic sensitivity 100%, specificity 86.1%, negative predictive value 100%

modality: x-ray / radiography; CT; MRI; nuclear / PET
patient_population: adults and children in the reviewed literature
clinical_problem: where deep learning stands for musculoskeletal lesion detection, progression and prediction, including pediatric bone age
task: detection / diagnosis; measurement / quantification; outcome prediction
model_description: A review that sorts musculoskeletal deep learning by modality and by how close each application is to the clinic. Its judgment is that pediatric bone age and fracture detection on radiographs perform well enough to be nearly ready for practice, while CT and especially MRI applications remain harder because the abnormality has to be tracked across slices and contrasts. It closes by insisting on prospective multi-institution evaluation before deployment.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: Deep Learning for Lesion Detection, Progression, and Prediction of Musculoskeletal Disease.

model_family: ensemble of semi-dense 3D fully convolutional networks
patient_population: 6-month-old infants in the public MICCAI iSEG-2017 challenge data
clinical_problem: segmenting the 6-month infant brain, where gray and white matter are nearly isointense
model_description: An ensemble of networks segmenting infant brain tissue from paired T1 and T2 images. The useful property is that where the ensemble members disagree, the segmentation is usually wrong, so the disagreement map tells a human where to look and correct. The architecture uses an order of magnitude fewer parameters than a 3D U-Net, which matters for anyone deploying this on ordinary hardware.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: Deep CNN ensembles and suggestive annotations for infant brain MRI segmentation.
study_design: technical development on a public challenge
headline_result: ranked first or second on most metrics among 21 teams; ensemble disagreement highly correlated with segmentation error

model_family: deep-learning segmentation, classification and localization models
patient_population: images from 10,251 normal and 2,529 abnormal pregnancies, with abnormality confirmed by neonatal ultrasound, follow-up or autopsy
clinical_problem: recognizing an abnormal fetal brain on standard axial screening planes
model_description: Takes a standard axial fetal brain ultrasound image, segments the skull outline, classifies the brain as normal or abnormal, and overlays a heat map indicating where the abnormality is. Trained on a large hospital archive with outcomes confirmed after birth rather than by the reporting sonographer, and split at case rather than image level, which is the methodologically careful choice.
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Using deep-learning algorithms to classify fetal brain ultrasound images as normal or abnormal.
dataset_size: 15,372 normal and 14,047 abnormal images from 12,780 pregnancies
headline_result: classification accuracy 96.3%, sensitivity 96.9%, specificity 95.9%, AUC 0.989; lesions localized precisely in 61.6% of abnormal images and closely in a further 24.6%

patient_population: fetuses undergoing echocardiography
clinical_problem: assessing fetal cardiac structure and function when the heart is small, moving, and often scanned by someone without fetal echocardiography training
model_description: A short review for fetal cardiologists of where machine learning can help: improving the acquired image, extracting measurements and segmentations automatically, and supporting the prenatal diagnosis of cardiac remodeling and structural abnormality. Written as an orientation to the technology rather than an evaluation of specific models.
title: Machine Learning in Fetal Cardiology: What to Expect.

model_family: pixel-level texture classification on multi-scale Gaussian derivative features
patient_population: 858 interpretable pediatric chest radiographs, 39% with primary-endpoint pneumonia by radiologist consensus
clinical_problem: identifying WHO-defined primary-endpoint pneumonia on a child's chest radiograph, the definition used in vaccine efficacy and epidemiological studies
model_description: Targets a specific and consequential definition rather than pneumonia in general: the WHO primary-endpoint criterion is what vaccine trials are scored against, and it depends on three radiologists agreeing. Automating it would make large epidemiological studies tractable and remove reader variability from vaccine efficacy estimates. Three radiologists independently set the reference, and the harder task of separating primary-endpoint pneumonia from other infiltrate is reported separately.
title: Computer-aided diagnosis for World Health Organization-defined chest radiograph primary-endpoint pneumonia in children.
headline_result: AUC 0.850 against radiologist consensus (sensitivity 76%, specificity 80%); AUC 0.810 separating primary-endpoint pneumonia from other infiltrate

model_family: four-stage framework: transfer learning, deep feature extraction, feature reduction and classification, with feature fusion across pretrained networks
patient_population: embryonic MRI images across various gestational ages
clinical_problem: detecting embryonic neurodevelopmental disorders on prenatal MRI, where up to three in a thousand pregnancies carry a brain defect and earlier detection changes counseling
model_description: The argument is against the handcrafted-feature pipelines that preceded it: enhancement, segmentation and feature engineering each introduce choices, and a deep network learns from the raw image instead. Feature fusion across several pretrained backbones stands in for the training data that prenatal MRI cohorts do not have. Comparison is against prior work on embryonic images rather than a held-out external set, so the performance claim is relative.
title: Deep Learning Techniques for Automatic Detection of Embryonic Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
headline_result: identified embryonic neurodevelopmental disorders from MRI across a range of gestational ages, performing competitively with prior work on embryonic images

model_family: transfer-learned convolutional network regressing a continuous value from the chest radiograph
patient_population: 1031 cardiac catheterizations in 657 patients at a tertiary center from January 2005 to April 2019 (median age 3.4 years, IQR 1.2-8.6), with 78 patients / 100 catheterizations held out; mean Fick-derived pulmonary to systemic flow ratio 1.43 (SD 0.95)
clinical_problem: quantifying pulmonary blood flow in congenital heart disease from the chest radiograph, which today is read subjectively and qualitatively and whose gold standard is an invasive catheterization
model_description: Turns a qualitative impression - does the pulmonary vasculature look plethoric - into a number on the same scale as the catheter measurement, with the Fick-derived ratio from a simultaneous catheterization as ground truth. The comparison against three certified pediatric cardiologists reading the same films is what establishes the claim, and the clinically salient operating point (a ratio of 2.0 or more, the shunt magnitude that prompts intervention) is reported separately. A non-invasive stand-in for part of what catheterization is done to answer.
title: Prediction of Pulmonary to Systemic Flow Ratio in Patients With Congenital Heart Disease Using Deep Learning-Based Analysis of Chest Radiographs.
study_design: retrospective observational study with expert comparison
dataset_size: 1031 catheterizations in 657 patients; 100 held out for evaluation
headline_result: prediction of the pulmonary to systemic flow ratio from chest radiographs evaluated by intraclass correlation and Bland-Altman analysis, with the diagnostic concordance rate compared against three certified pediatric cardiologists

model_family: dilated convolutional chain followed by a W-Net refinement stage
patient_population: 895 apical four-chamber views from fetal echocardiography
clinical_problem: outlining the seven key structures of the apical four-chamber view, from which congenital heart disease is judged
model_description: Segments seven anatomical structures in the fetal four-chamber view, contending with speckle, chambers that look alike, and boundaries that simply are not visible in places. A dilated convolution chain localizes the chambers across scales and a second stage sharpens the boundaries. The output is intended as the input to automated cardiac indices rather than as a diagnosis in itself.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: DW-Net: A cascaded convolutional neural network for apical four-chamber view segmentation in fetal echocardiography.
headline_result: Dice 0.827, pixel accuracy 0.933, AUC 0.990, substantially above established segmentation methods

model_family: fully automated AI bone age software
patient_population: 514 patients undergoing hand radiography for bone age
clinical_problem: bone age assessment against the Greulich-Pyle standard, in both accuracy and reading time
model_description: Compares a commercial-style automated bone age program against three blinded radiologists applying Greulich-Pyle, with a two-expert consensus as reference. The software was more accurate than the individual readers, not merely comparable, and cut reading time by 87%. Performance did not differ by sex. The design is the useful part: blinded readers, a consensus reference, and time measured alongside accuracy.
release_evidence: described as a novel AI software version; commercial availability not stated in the abstract
title: Artificial intelligence in bone age assessment: accuracy and efficiency of a novel fully automated algorithm compared to the Greulich-Pyle method.
headline_result: mean absolute deviation from reference 0.34 years for the software versus 0.79 years for the readers (p < 0.001); reading time reduced by 87%

model_family: end-to-end deep network (feature extractor, connectivity network, classifier)
patient_population: children in the public ADHD-200 dataset, contributed by several imaging sites
clinical_problem: diagnosing ADHD, which currently rests entirely on behavioral assessment
model_description: Takes preprocessed resting-state fMRI time series and outputs an ADHD diagnosis, learning the functional connectivity representation as part of the network rather than computing it beforehand. Because connectivity is learned end to end, the model can be interrogated for which regions carried the decision; here the frontal lobe dominated. Trained and tested on a public multi-site dataset, so the numbers are directly comparable with prior work.
title: DeepFMRI: End-to-end deep learning for functional connectivity and classification of ADHD using fMRI.
study_design: technical development on a public benchmark
headline_result: 73.1% accuracy at the New York University site (specificity 91.6%, sensitivity 65.5%), above prior state of the art

model_family: fuzzy c-means clustering over ten 3D parameters measured on biplanar radiograph reconstructions
patient_population: patients from a multicenter adolescent idiopathic scoliosis database, all with biplanar radiographs and 3D reconstruction of the entire spine; cluster sizes 11 to 290
clinical_problem: classifying adolescent idiopathic scoliosis in three dimensions, since the classifications surgeons plan from are two-dimensional and do not describe the deformity they are actually operating on
model_description: Unsupervised, and deliberately so - the point is to let the data propose subgroups rather than test an existing scheme. Eleven clusters emerged from ten 3D parameters, and the validation step is the one that matters for a taxonomy: four experienced spine surgeons from the SRS 3D Scoliosis Committee reviewed representative cases and unanimously agreed each cluster was a group current classifications do not name. Whether these subgroups predict surgical outcome is the unanswered question.
title: Towards a new 3D classification for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
headline_result: eleven statistically distinct 3D subgroups, all judged by four spine surgeons to be undefined in current classifications

patient_population: children undergoing MRI
clinical_problem: shortening pediatric MRI enough to reduce or avoid sedation and general anesthesia
model_description: A RadioGraphics review of the commercially available ways to shorten a pediatric MRI (parallel imaging, simultaneous multislice, radial sampling, compressed sensing, automated protocol selection) and the ones still under investigation, including AI-based reconstruction and prospective motion correction. It is the practical counterpart to the model papers: it says which of these a department can buy today.
release_evidence: the reviewed acceleration techniques are described as commercially available products in clinical use
journal: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc
title: MRI Techniques to Decrease Imaging Times in Children.

model_family: machine learning classifiers on combined diffusion and perfusion features
patient_population: children with brain tumours imaged at multiple centres
clinical_problem: non-invasive diagnosis of the three common childhood brain tumour types, which is a genuine radiological challenge
model_description: Most quantitative work in this area is single-centre and single-modality; this combines diffusion and perfusion imaging across sites. It also takes features from the whole brain as well as the tumour, and finds both contribute, which is a useful observation for a field that segments the lesion and discards everything else.
title: Distinguishing between paediatric brain tumour types using multi-parametric magnetic resonance imaging and machine learning: A multi-site study.
dataset_size: a multi-centre paediatric brain tumour cohort
headline_result: combining diffusion and perfusion features from tumour and whole brain gave the optimal classifier at over 80% predictive precision

model_family: five-layer convolutional neural network
patient_population: 673 patients aged 0 to 116 months (mean 16.5 months) with 2,420 sagittal renal ultrasound images across all five Society for Fetal Urology grades
clinical_problem: grading hydronephrosis severity on renal ultrasound, currently a subjective five-point judgment
model_description: Assigns a Society for Fetal Urology grade to a renal ultrasound image. The reported numbers are refreshingly candid: it places 94% of images correctly or within one grade, but only 51% exactly right on the five-way task, and the clinically decisive distinctions (low versus high grade, and grade II versus III) reach 78% and 71%. The authors frame it as a decision and teaching aid rather than a grader.
title: Using Deep Learning Algorithms to Grade Hydronephrosis Severity: Toward a Clinical Adjunct.
headline_result: 94% of images correct or within one grade on the five-way task (51% exactly correct); 78% accuracy for low versus high grade and 71% for grade II versus III

model_family: convolutional network for spine segmentation on tracked ultrasound
patient_population: trained on eight healthy adult volunteers and tested on eight pediatric patients
clinical_problem: measuring scoliosis without radiographs, which children with scoliosis undergo repeatedly through growth
model_description: Segments the spine on tracked ultrasound and reconstructs a 3D volume from which the scoliosis angle is measured, offering a radiation-free substitute for the serial radiographs that scoliosis follow-up requires. The paper is honest about the adult-to-pediatric transfer: fuzzy segmentation metrics dropped when the network trained on adults was applied to children, and thresholds had to be re-optimized. Measurement error against radiography was nonetheless within 2.2 degrees.
title: Automatic Spine Ultrasound Segmentation for Scoliosis Visualization and Measurement.
dataset_size: eight adult volunteers for training, eight pediatric patients for testing
headline_result: maximum error 2.2 degrees against radiographic scoliosis measurement, with each measurement taking under one minute; segmentation metrics fell when translating from adults to children

model_family: machine learning and multiscale tumour growth simulation on an open cloud platform
patient_population: children with neuroblastoma or diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma across 16 European partner institutions
clinical_problem: phenotyping, treatment allocation and prognosis in neuroblastoma and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
model_description: Less a model than an attempt at the infrastructure pediatric AI lacks: a four-year European consortium with two imaging biobanks and three paediatric oncology units, building a cloud decision-support platform on pooled anonymised imaging, clinical, molecular and genetic data for two rare childhood cancers, with external validation at independent centres and results promised to the community. The choice of two rare tumors is deliberate, since these are exactly the diseases no single centre can study alone.
release_evidence: an open cloud-based platform, with final results promised to the scientific community
title: PRIMAGE project: predictive in silico multiscale analytics to support childhood cancer personalised evaluation empowered by imaging biomarkers.
study_design: multicentre observational in silico study protocol
dataset_size: multi-institutional European cohorts for two tumour types

model_family: patch-based convolutional neural network on fractional anisotropy maps
patient_population: 77 infants born under 31 weeks gestation, imaged at 29-35 weeks postmenstrual age with motor outcome at 2 years corrected age
clinical_problem: identifying preterm infants headed for neuromotor delay early enough to refer them for intervention
model_description: Predicts abnormal motor outcome at two years from diffusion MRI acquired before term, which is earlier than most preterm prediction work and therefore closer to when intervention could start. Classification is done on image patches and aggregated with a tuned threshold, and heat maps show which brain locations drove the abnormal predictions. Accuracy is moderate and the confidence intervals are wide on 77 infants.
title: Predicting motor outcome in preterm infants from very early brain diffusion MRI using a deep learning convolutional neural network (CNN) model.
dataset_size: 77 very preterm infants (48 normal, 29 abnormal outcome)
headline_result: sensitivity 70%, specificity 74%, AUC 0.72 for abnormal motor outcome at 2 years from MRI acquired at 29-35 weeks postmenstrual age

model_family: multivariate logistic models with leave-one-out cross-validation and exhaustive feature selection over diffusion tensor metrics
patient_population: 102 very-low-birth-weight neonates (birthweight <= 1500 g, gestational age <= 32 weeks) recruited 2010-2011, of whom 92 returned for Bayley-III assessment at 18-22 months adjusted age
clinical_problem: identifying which very-low-birth-weight preterm infants are heading for language delay, early enough to intervene while neuroplasticity is greatest
model_description: Near-term diffusion imaging used as a prognostic instrument rather than a descriptive one. Exhaustive feature selection narrows to three brain regions, which keeps the model small enough to interpret and to replicate. Separate models for composite, expressive and receptive language, with the strongest performance on expressive and receptive - and a side finding that cerebellar asymmetry tracked lower receptive scores. Nearly a third of the cohort scored below 85, so the outcome is common enough for the prediction to matter.
title: Neonatal Brain Microstructure and Machine-Learning-Based Prediction of Early Language Development in Children Born Very Preterm.
headline_result: sensitivity and specificity of 89%/86% for composite, 100%/90% for expressive and 100%/90% for receptive language risk

model_family: segmentation network followed by geometric calculation
patient_population: 179 children aged 5-19 (mean 12 years) imaged for leg length discrepancy
clinical_problem: measuring leg length discrepancy, a task the paper describes as time consuming but cognitively simple
model_description: Segments the femurs and tibias on a full-length radiograph and computes each bone's length and the discrepancy between sides. The case it makes is not diagnostic accuracy but time: agreement with the radiology report was essentially perfect and the measurement took one second against 96 seconds by hand. This is the shape of the pediatric AI application most likely to pay for itself, an exact, repetitive measurement rather than a judgment call.
title: Deep Learning Measurement of Leg Length Discrepancy in Children Based on Radiographs.
headline_result: correlation 0.99 with radiologist measurements (mean absolute error 0.45 cm for individual bones, 0.51 cm for discrepancy); 1 second versus 96 seconds per study

model_family: radiomics with Kruskal-Wallis feature selection and a support vector machine
patient_population: 135 MRI slices from children with posterior fossa tumors, split into training and validation sets
clinical_problem: telling ependymoma from pilocytic astrocytoma before surgery, two posterior fossa tumors with different management that overlap on conventional MRI
model_description: A conventional radiomics pipeline whose most useful output is the feature ablation: Gabor, texture and wavelet features were compared head to head, and texture features alone matched the full 300-feature set. Small and slice-level rather than patient-level, so the headline accuracy should be read as a feasibility signal rather than a performance estimate.
journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
title: Ependymoma and pilocytic astrocytoma: Differentiation using radiomics approach based on machine learning.
headline_result: accuracy 0.878, sensitivity 0.929, specificity 0.800, AUC 0.865 on the selected feature set, with no significant loss versus the full feature set

model_family: deep CNN, pretrained on natural images and on adult radiographs
patient_population: adult cohorts for pretraining, then fine-tuned on pediatric patients for the pneumonia task
clinical_problem: flagging abnormal chest radiographs for worklist triage, and pneumonia in children specifically
model_description: Sorts frontal chest radiographs into normal and abnormal so that abnormal studies can be pushed up the worklist. The pediatric relevance is in the transfer step: a model pretrained on adult cohorts and fine-tuned on children reached higher performance for pneumonia than either alone, which is the practical recipe for a children's hospital with a smaller archive.
title: Automated abnormality classification of chest radiographs using deep convolutional neural networks.
dataset_size: about 8,500 images for the pretraining benefit analysis; cohort sizes not stated
headline_result: AUC 0.982 for normal versus abnormal, 0.944 on an external dataset, and 0.985 for normal versus pneumonia after fine-tuning on children

model_family: deep convolutional networks: segmentation of the craniocerebral region, then four-class classification, then class activation mapping for localization
patient_population: real-world clinical fetal brain ultrasound images at the transventricular and transcerebellar standard planes
clinical_problem: prenatal detection of five common fetal brain abnormalities on standard neurosonographic planes, where missed malformations change counseling and management
model_description: A three-stage design that gets weakly-supervised localization for free: the classifier is trained only on image-level labels, and lesions are then localized by class activation mapping rather than by any drawn box. That keeps the annotation burden low, and the numbers show the cost - classification is strong while localization overlap is modest. Positioned as support for junior operators, whose false negatives on fetal brain anomalies are the stated target.
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
title: Computer-aided diagnosis for fetal brain ultrasound images using deep convolutional neural networks.
headline_result: Dice 0.942 for craniocerebral segmentation, average F1 0.96 for classification, average mean IOU 0.497 for lesion localization

model_family: deep convolutional encoder-decoders with encoders pre-trained on ImageNet
patient_population: 24 shoulder examinations in children with unilateral obstetrical brachial plexus palsy, evaluated leave-one-out
clinical_problem: segmenting the four rotator cuff muscles on MRI in children with obstetrical brachial plexus palsy, so that muscle volume - and from it force - can be estimated without hours of manual tracing
model_description: A study framed around the two constraints that define pediatric musculoskeletal AI: very little annotated data, and pathological anatomy that looks nothing like the healthy training examples. It answers the transferability question directly by comparing learning schemes, and the winner combines healthy and pathological annotated data with ImageNet pre-training rather than choosing between them. Supraspinatus, the smallest and most atrophied muscle, is where it degrades.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: Healthy versus pathological learning transferability in shoulder muscle MRI segmentation using deep convolutional encoder-decoders.
headline_result: Dice 82.4% deltoid, 82.0% infraspinatus, 71.0% supraspinatus and 82.8% subscapularis, with surface estimation errors below 83 mm2 except supraspinatus at 134.6 mm2

model_family: weighted ensemble of ResNet18, Xception, InceptionV3, DenseNet121 and MobileNetV3
patient_population: children in the Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center pneumonia dataset
clinical_problem: pneumonia diagnosis on pediatric chest radiographs
model_description: Combines the predictions of five transfer-learned networks with learned weights rather than trusting any single architecture, and reports both accuracy and AUC on held-out data from the public Guangzhou pediatric dataset. The very high headline numbers should be read with that dataset's known limitations in mind: it is a single-center collection with a strong case mix, and the model has not been tested anywhere else.
title: Efficient Pneumonia Detection in Chest Xray Images Using Deep Transfer Learning.
study_design: technical development on a public dataset
dataset_size: the public Guangzhou pediatric pneumonia dataset
headline_result: 98.43% test accuracy and AUC 99.76 on unseen data from the same dataset

model_family: several state-of-the-art CNN classifiers compared
patient_population: 1,792 patients undergoing routine maternal-fetal screening ultrasound at two hospitals, imaged by several operators and machines
clinical_problem: labelling which anatomical plane a routine maternal-fetal screening ultrasound image shows
model_description: Classifies a screening ultrasound image into one of six categories (fetal abdomen, brain, femur, thorax, maternal cervix, other), and then subdivides brain images into the three standard brain planes. The point of the study is realism: the images come from two hospitals, several operators and several machines, and the models are benchmarked against the research technicians who do this task daily.
release_evidence: the dataset is stated to be made publicly available; nothing is said about the models
title: Evaluation of deep convolutional neural networks for automatic classification of common maternal fetal ultrasound planes.
headline_result: computational models performed similarly to human operators on common plane classification; fine-grained brain-plane categorization remained harder

model_family: machine-learning regression on serial fetal biometry
patient_population: healthy, well-nourished participants in the multicentre INTERGROWTH-21st study, with generalization tested in the more heterogeneous INTERBIO-21st cohort
clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy accurately in the second and third trimesters, and forecasting how a given fetus will grow
model_description: Estimates gestational age from ultrasound biometry measured across a ten-week window, and separately forecasts a specific fetus's growth trajectory six weeks ahead. The methodological move that makes it credible is the reference standard: accuracy is judged against the exactly known intervals between a woman's own scan visits rather than her recalled last menstrual period, which is itself unreliable. Generalization was checked in a different, more heterogeneous population.
title: Achieving accurate estimates of fetal gestational age and personalised predictions of fetal growth based on data from an international prospective cohort study: a population-based machine learning study.
headline_result: gestational age between 20 and 30 weeks estimated to within 3 days with 95% confidence, a prediction interval 3-5 times narrower than previous algorithms; 6-week growth forecasts accurate to within 7 days

model_family: CNN classifier on a 2D multi-channel fiber descriptor (FiberMap)
patient_population: 597 diffusion MRI scans from six independently acquired populations spanning 1 day to 82 years, including neonates and patients with brain tumors
clinical_problem: identifying named white matter tracts consistently enough to quantify them across very different subjects
model_description: Sorts the individual streamlines of a whole-brain tractogram into 54 named deep white matter tracts by classifying each fiber from an encoding of its spatial trajectory. The claim that matters clinically is consistency across subjects who look nothing alike: it identified over 99% of tracts across all subjects, including day-old neonates and brains distorted by space-occupying tumors, where registration-based methods break down.
title: Deep white matter analysis (DeepWMA): Fast and consistent tractography segmentation.
dataset_size: 1 million labeled fiber samples for training; 597 diffusion MRI scans for testing
headline_result: 90.99% fiber classification accuracy in training; over 99% of tracts successfully identified across all test subjects including neonates and tumor patients

model_family: recurrent neural network with spatial and temporal encoder-decoders, predicting motion parameters from sequences of acquired slices
patient_population: fetal MRI acquisitions, with held-out test sets including fetuses scanned at different ages and motion trajectories recorded from volunteers
clinical_problem: fetal motion during MRI, which today is handled by an operator watching slices go by and re-acquiring stacks - operator-dependent, expensive in scanner time, and hard for a pregnant woman to tolerate
model_description: Predicts where the fetus will be, not just where it was, which is what a system has to do if it is going to steer the next slice rather than fix the last one. The framing of the problem is unusually concrete about cost - scanner time, operator dependence, and the tolerability of a long scan for the mother - and the target is a navigation system rather than a better image. Prediction error is naturally larger than estimation error, and the paper reports both.
title: Deep Predictive Motion Tracking in Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Application to Fetal Imaging.
headline_result: real-time performance with average errors of 3.5 degrees for motion estimation and 8 degrees for prediction, outperforming alternative techniques

model_family: three 2D conditional generative adversarial networks combined across orthogonal planes
patient_population: 60 pediatric patients with brain tumors undergoing radiotherapy, deliberately imaged with heterogeneous MRI protocols
clinical_problem: planning photon and proton radiotherapy from MRI alone, so a child does not need a separate planning CT
model_description: Generates a synthetic CT from a T1-weighted MRI so that radiotherapy dose can be calculated without acquiring a planning CT, sparing the child that dose. Three networks work on the three orthogonal planes and their median is combined; the spread between them doubles as an uncertainty map, which flags the body contour and air cavities as the places to distrust. Trained on deliberately heterogeneous protocols, which is what a real pediatric department has.
journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
title: Deep learning-based synthetic CT generation for paediatric brain MR-only photon and proton radiotherapy.
headline_result: mean absolute error 61 ± 14 HU; dose difference -0.1 ± 0.3% (photon) and 0.1 ± 0.4% (proton) with gamma 2%/2mm pass rates of 99.5% and 99.2%

model_family: U-Net-like network generating synthetic CT from T1- and T2-weighted MRI
patient_population: 66 children with Wilms tumour or neuroblastoma (mean age 4 years) who had MRI and CT on the same day
clinical_problem: planning radiotherapy for a child from MRI alone, sparing the planning CT dose
model_description: Converts MRI intensities to CT Hounsfield units so that radiotherapy dose can be computed without a planning CT. Dose distributions calculated on the synthetic CT matched those from the real CT to within half a percent on average for both volumetric-modulated arc therapy and pencil-beam proton scanning, with gamma pass rates above 96%. For a small child this removes a CT and, with it, a dose and often a separate anesthetic.
journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
title: Deep learning-enabled MRI-only photon and proton therapy treatment planning for paediatric abdominal tumours.
dataset_size: 66 children with paired same-day MRI and CT
headline_result: mean absolute error 57 ± 12 HU; average dose differences below 0.5% with gamma pass rates above 99% (photon) and 96% (proton)

model_family: YOLOv3 lung field cropping followed by multi-class classification, comparing one-versus-one, one-versus-all and a single CNN classifier
patient_population: chest radiographs of children with common pulmonary diseases
clinical_problem: screening children's chest radiographs for the common lower respiratory problems - bronchiolitis or bronchitis, bronchopneumonia or interstitial pneumonitis, lobar pneumonia and pneumothorax - in settings where acute lower respiratory infection is the leading cause of child death
model_description: Deliberately broader than the single-disease pediatric models that preceded it: four disease categories plus normal, rather than pneumonia versus not. The honest conclusion in the abstract is the useful one - the scheme is strong at the normal-versus-abnormal decision and much weaker at telling the specific diseases apart, with per-class accuracies between 72% and 86%. That is the profile of a triage tool, and the authors say so.
title: Diagnosis of common pulmonary diseases in children by X-ray images and deep learning.
headline_result: 92.47% accuracy for abnormal versus normal; per-class accuracy 71.94% bronchiolitis/bronchitis, 72.19% bronchopneumonia, 85.42% lobar pneumonia, 85.71% pneumothorax and 80.00% normal

model_family: deep learning classification with acetabular index measurement
patient_population: 10,219 anteroposterior pelvic radiographs; the 1,138-patient test set had a mean age of 1.5 years and was 79% female
clinical_problem: diagnosing developmental dysplasia of the hip on a pelvic radiograph, where the normal anatomy changes so much with age that reading is genuinely hard
model_description: Classifies a pelvic radiograph as dislocated or not and measures the acetabular index, trained on over ten thousand radiographs labelled to a uniform standard. The size of the training set is what distinguishes it, and the reported agreement limits for acetabular index are wider in dislocated hips than normal ones, which is where measurement matters most.
title: Clinical application of artificial intelligence-assisted diagnosis using anteroposterior pelvic radiographs in children with developmental dysplasia of the hip.
headline_result: AUC 0.975 with sensitivity 95.5% and specificity 99.5% for hip dislocation; acetabular index agreement -3.27 to 2.94 degrees in non-dislocated and -7.36 to 5.36 degrees in dislocated hips

model_family: U-net with temporal and section-specific calibration
patient_population: 615 annotated frames from 421 normal fetal cardiac ultrasound videos of 211 screened pregnant women
clinical_problem: delineating the ventricular septum during fetal cardiac screening, a small structure that changes shape with every heartbeat
model_description: General-purpose segmentation networks fail badly on the fetal ventricular septum: DeepLab v3+ scored a mean intersection over union of 0.02 and U-net 0.15 on this task. This method crops to the relevant region, segments, then calibrates the output using the video's time-series information and the known section, reaching 0.55. The gap between those numbers is the honest measure of how hard small moving fetal structures are.
title: Image Segmentation of the Ventricular Septum in Fetal Cardiac Ultrasound Videos Based on Deep Learning Using Time-Series Information.
dataset_size: 615 annotated frames from 421 videos of 211 women
headline_result: mean intersection over union 0.554 versus 0.152 for U-net and 0.022 for DeepLab v3+

model_family: end-to-end confounder-invariant feature learning (adversarial fair-learning scheme)
patient_population: adolescents in the NCANDA alcohol and neurodevelopment cohort, children undergoing hand radiography, and adults with HIV
clinical_problem: stopping a model from learning a confounder instead of the disease, demonstrated partly on bone age from children's hand radiographs
model_description: A training method rather than a clinical model: it forces the learned features to be statistically independent of a named confounder (age, sex, scanner) while still predicting the outcome, borrowing from fair machine learning. Demonstrated on three tasks including bone age from pediatric hand radiographs and sex differences in adolescent brain MRI. Directly relevant to any children's hospital worried that a model has learned the scanner or the referring pathway rather than the disease.
release_evidence: the code is available at https://github.com/qingyuzhao/br-net
title: Training confounder-free deep learning models for medical applications.
headline_result: accurate prediction with reduced confounder-associated bias across all three tasks; figures not stated in the abstract

model_family: fully convolutional network with GAN-based synthetic data augmentation
patient_population: pediatric subjects with complex congenital heart disease
clinical_problem: manual chamber segmentation is the bottleneck in cardiac MRI analysis for congenital heart disease
model_description: Addresses the defining constraint of pediatric AI head on: there is not enough annotated pediatric cardiac MRI, and certainly not in complex congenital disease, so a generative network synthesizes additional images with matching chamber labels to enlarge the training set. The resulting segmentation network is benchmarked against U-Net and against cvi42, the software actually used in clinics. The authors made the pediatric congenital dataset public, which is rarer still.
release_evidence: the pediatric congenital heart disease dataset was made publicly available
journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
title: Fully‑automated deep‑learning segmentation of pediatric cardiovascular magnetic resonance of patients with complex congenital heart diseases.
dataset_size: a cohort of pediatric subjects with complex congenital heart disease
headline_result: outperformed U-Net and the clinically used cvi42 software on Dice, Jaccard, Hausdorff distance and clinical volumetric indices

model_family: three-dimensional patch-based multi-resolution pathway convolutional network, ensembled over 5-fold cross-validation
patient_population: 100 pediatric Hodgkin lymphoma patients with baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT, segmented by two nuclear medicine physicians
clinical_problem: extracting metabolic tumor volume and the other baseline PET metrics that drive risk stratification in pediatric Hodgkin lymphoma, which is slow and difficult to do by hand in high disease burden
model_description: Automation aimed squarely at a number that already changes treatment: metabolic tumor volume feeds pediatric Hodgkin risk stratification, and extracting it by hand is the bottleneck in exactly the high-burden patients where it matters most. Both PET and CT go in. The per-feature agreement is the useful part of the results - SUVmax and total lesion glycolysis are essentially solved, volume is slightly underestimated, and the disease-spread metric is not yet reliable.
release_evidence: built on DeepMedic, a published open-source 3D CNN architecture
title: Automated quantification of baseline imaging PET metrics on FDG PET/CT images of pediatric Hodgkin lymphoma patients.
headline_result: median Dice 0.86 (IQR 0.78-0.91); SUVmax matched physician values exactly in 81 of 100 cases (R = 0.95), MTV R = 0.88, TLG R = 0.94, but the disease spread metric only R = 0.51

model_family: automatic tissue segmentation with a linear discriminant analysis classifier
patient_population: 84 infants born between 26 and 36 weeks gestation, imaged shortly after birth and again at term-equivalent age, with outcomes at 18-24 months and 5 years
clinical_problem: predicting neurodevelopmental outcome after preterm birth from brain growth in the neonatal period
model_description: Automatically segments serial neonatal T2-weighted MRI into cortical gray matter, unmyelinated white matter, subcortical gray matter, cerebellum and CSF, then asks which volumes and growth rates predict motor and cognitive outcome later. Volumes at birth and term-equivalent age predicted motor outcome at 18-24 months, while volumes and growth rates predicted cognition at 5 years. The sobering finding is that family socioeconomic status was more strongly associated with cognitive outcome than any brain volume.
title: Longitudinal study of neonatal brain tissue volumes in preterm infants and their ability to predict neurodevelopmental outcome.
headline_result: brain tissue volumes contributed to prediction of motor outcome at 18-24 months and cognitive scores at 5 years; socioeconomic status was strongly associated with cognitive outcome while brain volumes were not

model_family: two-stage CNN with geodesic distance transforms and a back-propagatable CRF
patient_population: fetal MRI studies; brain tumor FLAIR MRI is the second test case
clinical_problem: producing clinically usable placental contours on fetal MRI without lengthy manual editing
model_description: One network produces an automatic segmentation, the operator marks where it is wrong, and a second network takes those marks and returns a corrected contour. User clicks are turned into geodesic distance maps and enforced as hard constraints, so a few interactions go a long way. Demonstrated on 2D placenta segmentation from fetal MRI and 3D brain tumor segmentation.
