journal: IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence
title: DeepIGeoS: A Deep Interactive Geodesic Framework for Medical Image Segmentation.
headline_result: large improvement over the automatic CNN, with comparable or better accuracy than traditional interactive methods at fewer interventions and less time

model_family: least-squares GAN with a deep residual generator
patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing contrast-enhanced abdominal MRI
clinical_problem: shortening contrast-enhanced MRI in children by reconstructing undersampled data
model_description: Takes an aliased image from undersampled k-space and returns a diagnostic-quality reconstruction in milliseconds. A generative adversarial network learns what real high-quality MR images look like, so the output keeps fine texture instead of the waxy appearance that pixel-wise losses produce. Trained and evaluated on a large contrast-enhanced pediatric MRI dataset with expert radiologist ratings.
title: Deep Generative Adversarial Neural Networks for Compressive Sensing MRI.
dataset_size: a large contrast-enhanced pediatric MR dataset; size not stated
headline_result: expert radiologists rated it higher in fine texture detail than wavelet, dictionary-learning and pixel-wise deep learning reconstructions, at two orders of magnitude faster reconstruction

model_family: 3D fully convolutional network with a multi-directional recurrent refinement network
patient_population: pregnant women undergoing volumetric prenatal ultrasound
clinical_problem: getting reliable biometry out of 3D prenatal ultrasound, which is hard to interpret and therefore little used
model_description: Segments the fetus, gestational sac and placenta simultaneously in a 3D ultrasound volume. A convolutional network makes the initial dense labeling and a recurrent network sweeping in several directions fixes the boundaries, which is where ultrasound segmentation usually fails because contrast is poor and edges are ambiguous. The measurements agreed with experts and were reproducible across scanning variation.
title: Towards Automated Semantic Segmentation in Prenatal Volumetric Ultrasound.
dataset_size: large in-house datasets; sizes not stated
headline_result: superior segmentation performance with decent agreement with expert measurements and high reproducibility against scanning variation

model_family: convolutional neural network
patient_population: 280 age- and sex-matched bone age radiographs from children aged 5 to 18
clinical_problem: whether AI assistance makes pediatric radiologists better at bone age, not whether AI alone beats them
model_description: The model itself is a bone age network the group had already published; the contribution here is the comparison design. Six subspecialty pediatric radiologists read the same 280 cases, then three read them again with the model's estimate in front of them. Every reader improved, and inter-reader variability fell. The conclusion — AI plus radiologist beats either alone — is the argument for deploying these tools as an adjunct rather than a replacement.
title: Artificial intelligence-assisted interpretation of bone age radiographs improves accuracy and decreases variability.
headline_result: AI alone 68.2% accurate versus 63.6% for the six-reader mean; pooled root mean squared error fell from 0.661 to 0.508 years with AI assistance, and every individual reader improved

model_family: regression CNN predicting angle-axis rotation and translation, trained with geodesic loss
patient_population: fetuses scanned in utero across a wide gestational age range, with generalization tested on newborns
clinical_problem: aligning fetal brain images acquired in arbitrary orientations to a standard atlas, the step that motion-robust reconstruction depends on
model_description: Predicts where an arbitrarily oriented fetal brain sits in a canonical space directly from the image, in under 100 milliseconds, replacing an iterative optimization that has a narrow capture range. Trained on T2-weighted fetal scans, it generalized to T1-weighted newborn scans once image contrast was transferred with a conditional GAN, which is a useful demonstration that a model can be moved across contrasts without retraining from scratch.
title: Real-Time Deep Pose Estimation With Geodesic Loss for Image-to-Template Rigid Registration.
headline_result: 3D pose estimation with a wide capture range in under 100 ms, generalizing to newborn scans of a different contrast

model_family: kernel regression in age with diffeomorphic tensor-to-tensor registration
patient_population: 67 healthy fetuses scanned once each between 21 and 39 weeks gestational age
clinical_problem: having a normative reference for fetal white matter development against which an individual fetus can be compared
model_description: Not a diagnostic model but the normative resource one needs before building any: the first diffusion tensor atlas of the fetal brain built from in utero images, computed by regressing motion-corrected individual tensors against gestational age. It makes group studies and computer-aided diagnosis from fetal diffusion imaging possible, which the authors note had not previously been feasible because individual in utero reconstructions are too noisy.
title: Fetal brain growth portrayed by a spatiotemporal diffusion tensor MRI atlas computed from in utero images.
headline_result: the atlas reproduced the known sequence of limbic, projection and association fiber development between 21 and 39 weeks

model_family: regression CNN with an attention module and dynamic attention loss
patient_population: children in two large hand radiograph datasets
clinical_problem: bone age assessment for endocrine, genetic and growth disorders
model_description: Regresses bone age directly from the radiograph, with an attention module that first learns where the growth-relevant regions are and a loss that weights the hard cases more heavily during training. The attention idea addresses the specific failure mode of bone age networks, which is that most of the image is irrelevant and the informative epiphyses are small.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Regression Convolutional Neural Network for Automated Pediatric Bone Age Assessment From Hand Radiograph.
dataset_size: two large datasets; sizes not stated
headline_result: average discrepancy of 5.2-5.3 months between clinical and automatic bone age on two large datasets

model_family: convolutional neural network segmentation of lumen, wall and background, combined with curved planar reformatting
patient_population: 23 pediatric patients with Crohn disease imaged at 1.5 T with a T1-weighted postcontrast VIBE sequence
clinical_problem: seeing and quantifying disease burden in pediatric Crohn disease on contrast-enhanced small bowel MRI, where following the bowel means scrolling back and forth through a 3D volume
model_description: The segmentation is a means, not the end. Curved planar reformatting straightens the bowel so its whole length is visible at once, and the CNN supplies the lumen and wall boundaries that reformatting needs - together turning a scroll-through into a set of markers. The markers are then tested for what a radiologist would want: whether they separate active from inactive segments and stricturing from non-stricturing, and whether they reproduce. Wall segmentation is more reliable than lumen.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: Curved planar reformatting and convolutional neural network-based segmentation of the small bowel for visualization and quantitative assessment of pediatric Crohn's disease from MRI.
headline_result: Dice 75 +/- 18% lumen, 81 +/- 8% wall, 97 +/- 2% background; wall thickness at minimum radius (P = 0.0013) and median relative contrast enhancement (P = 0.0033) separated active from non-active segments

model_family: support vector machine on transfer-learned deep features combined with conventional texture features
patient_population: 50 children with congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract and 50 controls, imaged during routine care
clinical_problem: identifying congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract on the ultrasound children already receive
model_description: Combines features learned by a pretrained network with hand-computed texture features and shows the combination beats either alone, which is the useful methodological finding on a 100-child dataset where a deep model alone would overfit. Uses images from routine clinical care rather than a curated research acquisition.
title: Computer-aided diagnosis of congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract in children based on ultrasound imaging data by integrating texture image features and deep transfer learning image features.
headline_result: AUC 0.92, 0.88 and 0.92 for left, right and bilateral abnormal kidney scans, significantly better than either feature set alone (p < 0.001)

model_family: CNN with GloVe embeddings, and a domain-phrase attention hierarchical recurrent network
patient_population: adult and pediatric patients whose thoracic CT reports were collected from four healthcare centers
clinical_problem: extracting whether a CT report says there is a pulmonary embolus, at scale and across institutions
model_description: Reads a free-text thoracic CT report and decides whether it describes a pulmonary embolus. The recurrent model builds up word, sentence and document representations and weights domain-specific phrases through an attention mechanism. The finding that matters for a children's hospital is the transfer: models trained on adult reports classified pediatric reports at the same F1 of 0.99, which is not what happens with image models.
title: Comparative effectiveness of convolutional neural network (CNN) and recurrent neural network (RNN) architectures for radiology text report classification.
dataset_size: over 7,370 thoracic CT reports from four centers
headline_result: F1 0.99 for pulmonary embolus in adults and 0.99 in the pediatric population, beating the rule-based PEFinder on multi-institutional test sets

model_family: convolutional neural networks (105 submitted entries)
patient_population: children whose hand radiographs make up a curated 14,236-image challenge dataset
clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment
model_description: Not one model but a public competition: RSNA released a curated set of 14,236 pediatric hand radiographs with reference bone ages and invited teams to submit algorithms, scored on mean absolute distance in months. Almost every entry used convolutional neural networks. The paper reports what a coordinated community effort achieved and is the reference point later bone-age papers compare against.
release_evidence: the data set was made available to registered challenge participants; the abstract says nothing about releasing the models
title: The RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Machine Learning Challenge.
headline_result: best five entries achieved mean absolute distance of 4.2 to 4.5 months

model_family: artificial neural network over radiologist-interpreted CT findings
patient_population: 12 902 children from the Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network traumatic brain injury dataset
clinical_problem: ruling in clinically relevant traumatic brain injury in children so that the rest can be discharged on an evidence-based basis rather than admitted for observation
model_description: Built on PECARN, the dataset that produced the clinical decision rule pediatric emergency medicine already uses, and aimed at the same decision - who can safely go home. The inputs are the radiologist's CT findings rather than the pixels, so this is decision support layered on the report rather than image analysis. Sensitivity above 99% is the operating point the problem demands, since the cost of a missed clinically relevant injury is not symmetric with the cost of an observation stay.
title: Using an artificial neural network to predict traumatic brain injury.
study_design: retrospective secondary analysis of a multi-center cohort
headline_result: prediction of clinically relevant traumatic brain injury with greater than 99% sensitivity and AUC 0.99

model_family: VGG-inspired detection network followed by a U-net measurement network
patient_population: 183 pregnant women at St. Luke's Hospital, Wolisso, Ethiopia
clinical_problem: estimating gestational age where there is no sonographer, using a sweep protocol any health worker can learn in a day
model_description: Works from sweeps acquired with a fixed protocol that requires no knowledge of ultrasound, and which will usually not contain the standard plane at all. One network finds the frames containing the fetal head, a second measures head circumference in those frames, and gestational age follows from the Hadlock curve. Validated against standard-plane measurements taken by an experienced sonographer on the same women.
title: Automated Fetal Head Detection and Circumference Estimation from Free-Hand Ultrasound Sweeps Using Deep Learning in Resource-Limited Countries.
headline_result: most automatically estimated gestational ages fell within the 2.5th to 97.5th centile interval of the Hadlock curve relative to reference measurements

model_family: unbiased template construction algorithm
patient_population: 328 cognitively normal Chinese children aged 6-12, with two independent validation datasets of 114 and 71 children
clinical_problem: whether a pediatric brain atlas built on one population is valid for children of another
model_description: A set of age-specific brain templates built from Chinese children, made because the widely used NIH pediatric atlases are derived from Caucasian children. The comparison found substantial anatomical differences in frontal and parietal regions, and using the matched atlas gave significantly better tissue segmentation and brain-age prediction in Chinese children. It is a concrete demonstration that population mismatch in a reference dataset degrades downstream results.
release_evidence: released on the NITRC website at https://www.nitrc.org/projects/chn-pd
title: Unbiased age-specific structural brain atlases for Chinese pediatric population.
dataset_size: 328 children for atlas construction; 185 children across two validation datasets
headline_result: significantly higher accuracy than the NIH pediatric atlases for both brain-age prediction and tissue segmentation in Chinese children

patient_population: adults and children in the reviewed studies, with particular attention to pediatric and deformed-lung cases
clinical_problem: isolating the lungs on a chest radiograph, the step every downstream chest analysis depends on
model_description: A review of lung segmentation on chest radiographs from 2006 to 2017, classifying methods into rule-based, pixel-classification, model-based, hybrid and deep-learning families. Its finding for a children's hospital is a gap: almost all published algorithms are validated on adult posteroanterior films of healthy-looking lungs, while pediatric films are noisier, obstructed by whoever is holding the child, and anatomically different by developmental stage.
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
title: A review on lung boundary detection in chest X-rays.
headline_result: hybrid and deep-learning methods reached inter-observer-level segmentation performance, at the cost of long training and high computational complexity

model_family: deep learning lung delineation feeding quantitative texture analysis
patient_population: 790 fetal lung ultrasound images obtained between 24 and 39 weeks gestation
clinical_problem: predicting neonatal respiratory morbidity from ultrasound instead of amniocentesis
model_description: The successor version of the commercial fetal lung maturity tool, with the manual lung outlining replaced by deep learning. The comparison that makes the paper worth reading is three-way: fully automated, the same texture analysis with manual delineation, and gestational age alone. Automation cost essentially nothing in accuracy (91.5% versus 90.3%) while both beat gestational age alone (75.6%) decisively.
release_evidence: quantusFLM version 3.0, a commercial software tool
title: Evaluation of an improved tool for non-invasive prediction of neonatal respiratory morbidity based on fully automated fetal lung ultrasound analysis.
headline_result: sensitivity 71.0%, specificity 94.7%, accuracy 91.5% fully automated, against 90.3% with manual delineation and 75.6% using gestational age alone

model_family: deep Q-network reinforcement learning agents with multi-scale hierarchical search
body_region: fetal head, adult brain and heart
patient_population: fetuses in a fetal head ultrasound dataset, alongside adult brain and cardiac MRI datasets
clinical_problem: finding anatomical landmarks automatically, the step that biometry and registration depend on
model_description: Rather than scanning the whole image, an agent starts somewhere and learns to walk toward the landmark, treating the 3D scan as an environment to navigate. Searching coarse-to-fine with hierarchical step sizes speeds this up four- to fivefold and copes with the large fields of view and noisy backgrounds where fixed-scale agents fail. Evaluated on fetal head ultrasound among three datasets.
title: Evaluating reinforcement learning agents for anatomical landmark detection.
dataset_size: three medical imaging datasets; sizes not stated
headline_result: surpassed state-of-the-art supervised and reinforcement-learning landmark methods; hierarchical steps sped up search 4-5 times

model_family: attention-gated CNN module for VGG / U-Net
patient_population: fetuses undergoing mid-pregnancy screening ultrasound; the segmentation experiments use adult abdominal CT
clinical_problem: identifying the correct standard views during fetal ultrasound screening
model_description: A drop-in module that makes a standard CNN learn where to look, suppressing irrelevant image regions without a separate organ-localization step. Demonstrated on fetal ultrasound scan-plane detection, where it reduced false positives, and on multi-organ abdominal CT segmentation. It is a general architecture contribution rather than a clinical product.
release_evidence: the source code for the proposed AG models is publicly available
title: Attention gated networks: Learning to leverage salient regions in medical images.
dataset_size: two large 3D CT abdominal datasets plus a fetal ultrasound screening set; sizes not stated
headline_result: consistent improvement in prediction performance over the base architectures across datasets and training sizes

model_family: deep learning classifier on white matter connectomes
patient_population: 75 full-term infants scanned at birth and 37 preterm infants scanned at term-equivalent age
clinical_problem: predicting cognitive ability at age 2 from the brain's wiring at birth
model_description: Builds a white matter connectome from diffusion MRI acquired at birth and classifies whether that child will score above or below the median on cognitive testing at two years, then predicts the individual score. Trained on full-term infants and evaluated separately on preterm infants, which is the transfer that matters clinically. Frontal lobe connections and their links to the rest of the brain carried the classification.
title: White matter connectomes at birth accurately predict cognitive abilities at age 2.
headline_result: 89.5% accuracy in full-term and 83.8% in preterm infants for the 2-year cognitive group; predicted and actual scores correlated at r = 0.98 and 0.96

model_family: two fine-tuned convolutional feature extractors - one on the whole image, one on discriminant cropped regions - whose classification decisions are fused
patient_population: 4074 2-D fetal ultrasound images (3109 training, 965 test)
clinical_problem: labeling which fetal structure a 2D ultrasound image shows, across 14 structures, so that large retrospective archives can be mined for indicators of abnormal development
model_description: The diagnosis of the problem is precise: crops confuse structures that look alike, such as kidney and abdomen, while the whole image lacks the local detail to say which structure is where. Fusing decisions from both, without a prior on where to look, is the contribution, and localization falls out of the same machinery. The high mean accuracy alongside much lower precision and recall reflects 14 unbalanced classes. Its stated purpose is retrospective archive mining rather than live scanning.
title: Decision Fusion-Based Fetal Ultrasound Image Plane Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks.
headline_result: mean accuracy 97.05%, precision 76.47%, recall 75.41%, Cohen kappa 0.72; 92% mean accuracy on images without scanner overlays

model_family: deep CNN on diffusion tractography streamlines with focal and center losses and a soft attention mechanism
patient_population: streamlines from 70 healthy children and 70 children with focal epilepsy, labeled by functional MRI and electrical stimulation mapping
clinical_problem: identifying eloquent white matter pathways before pediatric epilepsy surgery, so that resection spares motor, language, auditory and visual function
model_description: Aimed at the specific inadequacy of the current tools: electrical stimulation mapping is invasive and maps cortex, fMRI needs task cooperation from a child, and neither shows the fibers connecting eloquent areas. The network classifies individual tractography streamlines, with focal and center losses chosen for an extremely unbalanced label distribution and soft attention for interpretability. Ground truth comes from the invasive standard it would reduce.
release_evidence: the abstract states the implementation will be released at a GitHub repository
title: Objective Detection of Eloquent Axonal Pathways to Minimize Postoperative Deficits in Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery using Diffusion Tractography and Convolutional Neural Networks.
headline_result: 73-100% accuracy for objective detection of functionally important pathways, outperforming existing streamline classification models

model_family: classifier built on resting-state functional connectivity features
patient_population: never-depressed children aged 8-14 with familial risk for major depressive disorder and age-matched controls without familial risk, reassessed by diagnostic interview 3-4 years later
clinical_problem: identifying, before any episode occurs, which children at familial risk for major depression will develop it in adolescence
model_description: A prognostic rather than diagnostic model, and the design carries the weight: imaging at baseline in children who had never been depressed, diagnosis established 3-4 years later, and the classifier built independently of the group differences the paper also reports. Its comparator is the right one - baseline clinical rating scales - and connectivity beat them. A pilot, with the sample size that word implies.
title: Intrinsic Functional Brain Connectivity Predicts Onset of Major Depression Disorder in Adolescence: A Pilot Study.
dataset_size: pilot cohort, size not stated in the abstract
headline_result: classification of converters versus non-converters from baseline connectivity reached high accuracy, sensitivity and specificity, superior to classification from baseline clinical rating scales

model_family: fully convolutional network with a differentiable spatial-to-numerical layer
patient_population: 493 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, adult deformity and spinal stenosis
clinical_problem: measuring spinal deformity parameters (Cobb angle, kyphosis, lordosis, pelvic incidence) on biplanar radiographs
model_description: Takes biplanar spine radiographs and returns the 78 anatomical landmarks (endplate centers, hip joint centers, S1 endplate margins) from which the standard deformity angles are then computed. It is designed to cope with a wide range of conditions and fields of view. The authors are candid that although the predicted spine shape looks convincing and correlates strongly with ground truth, the standard errors on individual angles are large.
journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
title: Fully automated radiological analysis of spinal disorders and deformities: a deep learning approach.
dataset_size: 493 spines for training, 50 patients for quantitative comparison
headline_result: all parameters strongly correlated with ground truth, but standard errors from 2.7 degrees (pelvic tilt) to 11.5 degrees (L1-L5 lordosis)

patient_population: infants and young children undergoing MRI
clinical_problem: avoiding sedation and general anesthesia for MRI in infants and young children
model_description: A review of every lever available for getting a diagnostic MRI in a small child awake: environment, child life specialists, feed-and-bundle, distraction, noise reduction, and the technical routes to shorter scans, of which artificial intelligence is one. Useful as the framing document for why faster reconstruction matters in a children's hospital, rather than as a source of model performance figures.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: Techniques for minimizing sedation in pediatric MRI.

model_family: convolutional neural networks with transfer learning and classifier combination, both mixture-of-experts and simple Bayes
patient_population: children aged 5 to 10 years from the ABIDE I and ABIDE II datasets
clinical_problem: diagnosing autism spectrum disorder in young children from resting-state functional MRI, before behavioral symptoms are established enough for interview and observation to settle it
model_description: Two constraints are handled at once: small medical datasets and the need to hold the age window narrow. The age restriction to 5-10 years is a deliberate cost - it shrinks an already small dataset - taken because a diagnostic aid is only useful before the clinical diagnosis is obvious. Combining classifiers and transferring features stand in for the data that does not exist. Accuracy in the low-to-mid 70s is representative of what ABIDE supports, and is a reminder of how far this is from clinical use.
title: Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorders in Young Children Based on Resting-State Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Data Using Convolutional Neural Networks.
study_design: retrospective model development on public datasets
dataset_size: ABIDE I and ABIDE II subjects aged 5-10
headline_result: ABIDE I accuracy 0.7273, sensitivity 0.712, specificity 0.7348; ABIDE II accuracy 0.700, sensitivity 0.582, specificity 0.804

model_family: CNN landmark detection driving a statistical shape model
patient_population: 68 biplanar radiographs of asymptomatic subjects and adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients
clinical_problem: getting 3D spinal measurements from biplanar radiographs, which currently needs so much manual supervision that it stays out of routine practice
model_description: Fits a realistic statistical shape model of the spine to a pair of biplanar radiographs by having networks find the controlling anatomical landmarks, iteratively and coarse-to-fine. Reconstruction takes under a minute against the semi-automated methods it replaces, and 89% of its measurements fell inside the experts' own confidence intervals. The stated aim is dissemination: 3D measurement exists but nobody has time to do it by hand.
title: Toward Automated 3D Spine Reconstruction from Biplanar Radiographs Using CNN for Statistical Spine Model Fitting.
study_design: retrospective validation against multi-expert ground truth
headline_result: landmark errors 1.6-2.3 mm; absolute error 2.8-4.7 degrees for spinal and 1-2.1 degrees for pelvic parameters; 89% of measurements inside expert confidence intervals

model_family: deep learning pipeline with a plane acceptance check followed by head circumference and biparietal diameter estimation
patient_population: fetal ultrasound images: 102 labeled for training, 70 for validation
clinical_problem: automating head circumference and biparietal diameter on fetal ultrasound, the biometry used to assign gestational age and flag central nervous system pathology
model_description: Biometry with a gatekeeper. The pipeline first decides whether the plane is acceptable and only then measures, which is the right ordering for a measurement that is meaningless off-plane and the part most automated biometry skips. Small dataset, and the reported success rates are plane-level rather than millimetre agreement, so it reads as feasibility.
title: Automatic evaluation of fetal head biometry from ultrasound images using machine learning.
headline_result: 91.43% success for head circumference and 100% for biparietal diameter, with 87.14% accuracy on the plane acceptance check

model_family: support vector machine on clinical plus T2-weighted radiomic features
patient_population: 225 children and young adults (mean age 14.1 years) internally and 84 (mean age 13.7) in an external cohort, with known or suspected liver disease
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: estimating liver stiffness without MR elastography, which not every center has
model_description: Classifies liver stiffness above or below 3 kPa from routine T2-weighted images plus clinical data, using elastography as the reference. The point is substitution: if ordinary sequences carry enough signal, centers without elastography could still stratify fibrosis risk. Clinical and radiomic features together beat either alone, and the model held up in an independent external cohort with a modest drop.
title: Machine Learning Prediction of Liver Stiffness Using Clinical and T2-Weighted MRI Radiomic Data.
headline_result: internal AUC 0.84 combining clinical and radiomic features (0.77 clinical, 0.70 radiomic alone); external AUC 0.80 with accuracy 75.0%

model_family: two sequential CNNs with synthetic intensity-inhomogeneity augmentation
patient_population: fetuses undergoing MRI
clinical_problem: volumetric and morphologic assessment of the fetal brain, which requires tissue-level segmentation
model_description: One network extracts the intracranial volume, a second divides it into seven tissue classes: cerebellum, basal ganglia and thalami, ventricular CSF, white matter, brain stem, cortical gray matter and extracerebral CSF. The trick is in the training: rather than correcting the intensity inhomogeneity that fetal motion causes, artificial gradients are added to clean slices so the network learns to tolerate the artifact, which removes a preprocessing step entirely.
title: Automatic brain tissue segmentation in fetal MRI using convolutional neural networks.
headline_result: average Dice rose from 0.77 to 0.88 and mean surface distance fell from 0.78 mm to 0.37 mm when training data included simulated inhomogeneity

patient_population: children and subadults in the 26 studies reviewed, mostly from the United States and Western Europe
clinical_problem: the state of machine learning for bone age assessment
model_description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 26 bone age studies using machine learning. Its value is in the gaps it names: the field works almost entirely on hand and wrist radiographs and has barely explored radiation-free alternatives such as MRI, few studies address ethnic differences, the samples cluster around the medico-legal age of 18, and socioeconomic influences on skeletal maturation are untouched.
title: Bone age assessment with various machine learning techniques: A systematic literature review and meta-analysis.

model_family: self-supervised pretraining by context restoration
patient_population: fetuses imaged with 2D ultrasound; further experiments use abdominal CT and brain tumor MRI
clinical_problem: getting usable models when few images are labelled, demonstrated on fetal ultrasound scan-plane detection
model_description: A pretraining recipe rather than a clinical model: patches of an unlabelled image are swapped and the network learns to restore the original, which teaches it semantic features without any annotation. The pretrained weights are then fine-tuned for a downstream task. Demonstrated on fetal ultrasound scan-plane detection, abdominal organ localization on CT and brain tumor segmentation on MRI.
title: Self-supervised learning for medical image analysis using image context restoration.
headline_result: improved models in all three downstream tasks; magnitudes not stated in the abstract

model_family: LASSO-selected radiomic signatures from two anatomical regions, combined with a clinical factor in a predictive nomogram
patient_population: 53 children with clinically confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis and 62 with community-acquired pneumonia, split 3:1 into primary (n=86) and validation (n=29) cohorts
clinical_problem: separating primary progressive pulmonary tuberculosis from community-acquired pneumonia in children on chest CT, a distinction that changes treatment entirely and that experienced radiologists get wrong often enough to matter
model_description: Two separate radiomic signatures rather than one, extracted from the consolidation and from the lymph nodes, which mirrors how the two diseases actually differ and lets the model use nodal texture that no visual score captures. Duration of fever is the only clinical variable added. The comparator that gives the result its weight is a senior radiologist reading the same scans, who scored 0.79 against the nomogram's 0.97 - though on 29 validation patients.
title: Computed tomography-based predictive nomogram for differentiating primary progressive pulmonary tuberculosis from community-acquired pneumonia in children.
headline_result: AUC 0.971 (95% CI 0.912-1) versus 0.791 for a senior radiologist's clinical judgment and 0.832 for the clinical factor alone

model_family: random forests and deep convolutional neural networks on 3D hand MRI, with several image-input simplifications compared
patient_population: 328 hand MR images of children and adolescents; the best method was then adapted to 2D and applied to a public hand radiograph dataset
clinical_problem: estimating age in children and adolescents without ionizing radiation, for both clinical and forensic use
model_description: The MRI answer to bone age. Three problems with radiographic staging are addressed at once - radiation, the absence of MRI-specific staging systems, and examiner subjectivity - by regressing age directly from 3D volumes and skipping staging entirely. The paper is unusually careful about what is being estimated, separating biological age estimation from chronological age approximation, and it validates by porting the method to 2D radiographs where it matches published automatic methods.
title: Automated age estimation from MRI volumes of the hand.
study_design: retrospective model development with external dataset validation
headline_result: mean absolute error 0.37 +/- 0.51 years for biological age in subjects 18 or younger

model_family: multi-task faster region-based CNN with shared convolutional trunk
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound
clinical_problem: deciding whether a fetal head ultrasound image is good enough to measure from, before anyone measures from it
model_description: Detects the key anatomical structures of the fetal head, checks whether the image magnification is appropriate, and scores the plane against clinical protocol, all from one network with a shared feature trunk and task-specific heads. It returns a verdict in under half a second, which is fast enough to be useful during the scan rather than after it. Prior clinical rules are folded in to hold down false detections.
title: Multi-task learning for quality assessment of fetal head ultrasound images.
dataset_size: an institutional dataset; size not stated
headline_result: quality assessment of an ultrasound plane in under half a second, comparable with state-of-the-art methods

model_family: classical classifiers - diagonal quadratic discriminant analysis, k-nearest neighbour, random forest, naive Bayes and RBF networks - plus bagging and AdaBoost ensembles of them
patient_population: fetuses of widespread gestational ages imaged with brain MRI
clinical_problem: classifying fetal brain abnormalities on MRI before birth, across a wide span of gestational ages rather than at one fixed age
model_description: Pre-deep-learning in method but pointed in framing: most work on early brain abnormality classification had been done on newborns and premature infants, and this pushes the same question back before birth and across gestational ages rather than at a single one. Handcrafted features with a bank of classical classifiers and ensembles compared against their base models; k-nearest neighbour won.
title: Fetal Brain Abnormality Classification from MRI Images of Different Gestational Age.
headline_result: highest accuracy and AUC around 95% using the k-nearest neighbour classifier

model_family: machine-learning classifier on a routine biomarker signature
patient_population: 590 children and adolescents aged 0-17 with suspected appendicitis at a Berlin hospital (473 histologically confirmed, 117 negative)
clinical_problem: deciding whether a child with abdominal pain has appendicitis, and whether it is complicated
model_description: Combines the appendiceal diameter measured on ultrasound with the full blood count and C-reactive protein, all of which are obtained routinely anyway, and returns a diagnosis of appendicitis. The framing is investigator-independent: no expert interpretation is needed. Discrimination of appendicitis from no appendicitis is good; separating complicated from uncomplicated inflammation, the decision that would actually change management toward antibiotics, is not.
title: Diagnosis and classification of pediatric acute appendicitis by artificial intelligence methods: An investigator-independent approach.
dataset_size: 590 patients, with at most 35% used for discovery and training
headline_result: 90% accuracy for appendicitis (93% sensitivity, 67% specificity); only 51% accuracy for identifying complicated inflammation

model_family: test-time augmentation for CNN segmentation uncertainty
patient_population: fetuses imaged with MRI; brain tumor MRI is used as a second test case
clinical_problem: knowing when to distrust an automated fetal brain segmentation
model_description: A way of putting an uncertainty estimate on a segmentation: the same image is transformed several ways at test time and the spread of the resulting segmentations is treated as image-based uncertainty, formalized as Monte Carlo sampling over an image acquisition model. Applied to fetal brain and brain tumor MRI, it flags overconfident wrong predictions better than dropout-based model uncertainty alone.
title: Aleatoric uncertainty estimation with test-time augmentation for medical image segmentation with convolutional neural networks.
headline_result: better uncertainty estimation than test-time dropout alone, and higher accuracy than single-prediction segmentation

model_family: deep learning image classifiers
patient_population: adolescents undergoing scoliosis screening
clinical_problem: screening adolescents for idiopathic scoliosis without radiographs and without unnecessary referrals
model_description: The input is an unclothed photograph of the back, not a radiograph, which is the point: current school screening has such low positive predictive value that it sends many children for radiographs they did not need. The algorithms detect scoliosis, flag curves of 20 degrees or more, and grade severity, with the aim of triaging who actually needs imaging and of following untreated cases without repeated radiation.
title: Development and validation of deep learning algorithms for scoliosis screening using back images.
headline_result: accuracy superior to human specialists for detecting scoliosis, for detecting curves of 20 degrees or more, and for severity grading

model_family: multi-task CNN optimizing segmentation Dice and ellipse parameters jointly
patient_population: fetuses across all trimesters in an ultrasound dataset
clinical_problem: head circumference measurement for fetal growth assessment and gestational age estimation
model_description: Trains segmentation and ellipse fitting together in one loss rather than segmenting first and fitting afterwards, so the network optimizes for the measurement that will actually be reported. Evaluated across trimesters, which matters because the fetal head looks very different early and late in pregnancy.
journal: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
title: Fetal Ultrasound Image Segmentation for Measuring Biometric Parameters Using Multi-Task Deep Learning.
headline_result: segmentation and head circumference measurements matched radiologist annotations, comparable to the state of the art

model_family: unsupervised convolutional network taking two 3D volumes and outputting a motion field, regularized by the Frobenius norm of the field's Jacobian
patient_population: trained and tested on 150 cardiac MRI patients, then validated on a synthetic set (n = 100) and a pediatric set (n = 33)
clinical_problem: estimating three-dimensional deformable cardiac motion from 2D cine MR images, the measurement that strain and function analyses rest on
model_description: A registration network that learns motion without labels: two volumes in, a smooth displacement field out. Its interest for pediatrics is the validation design rather than the architecture, since the pediatric cohort is a held-out generalization test on hearts the network never trained on. It matched or beat five established non-rigid registration methods on every dataset.
title: Implementation and Validation of a Three-dimensional Cardiac Motion Estimation Network.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
headline_result: median Dice 0.77 on the pediatric data, higher than or similar to all five comparison registration methods; 0.85 on synthetic data versus 0.67-0.84 for the alternatives

model_name: 2017 RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge ensembles
model_family: ensembles of up to 10 of the 48 challenge submissions
patient_population: 12 611 pediatric hand radiographs for development and a 200-radiograph test set labeled by the weighted average of six pediatric radiologist ratings
clinical_problem: automated skeletal age estimation from hand radiographs, and how much accuracy is left on the table by using a single model
model_description: A post-hoc study of the RSNA challenge that asks a question the leaderboard could not: what happens when you combine the entries. The useful finding is counter-intuitive and directly actionable for anyone assembling a clinical bone-age system - combining four less-correlated models beat combining the eight top scorers, so model diversity bought more than individual accuracy did.
title: Improving Automated Pediatric Bone Age Estimation Using Ensembles of Models from the 2017 RSNA Machine Learning Challenge.
study_design: secondary analysis of a public challenge
dataset_size: 48 challenge submissions; 12 611 training radiographs; 200 test radiographs
headline_result: single-model generalization error 4.55 months versus 3.79 months for the best four-model ensemble; naively combining the top eight models reached only 3.93 months

model_family: convolution, pooling and transposed convolution defined on the spherical manifold
patient_population: infants
clinical_problem: parcellating the infant cortical surface and predicting how its attributes will develop
model_description: Standard convolutions assume a regular grid, which a cortical surface mesh is not: vertex counts and local connectivity vary between and within subjects. This defines the convolution on the sphere instead, so a U-Net can operate natively on cortical surfaces. Applied to infant cortical parcellation and to predicting how cortical attribute maps will develop, both of which are prerequisites for detecting abnormal early brain growth.
journal: Information processing in medical imaging : proceedings of the ... conference
title: Spherical U-Net on Cortical Surfaces: Methods and Applications.
headline_result: competitive accuracy and computational efficiency against state-of-the-art methods on infant cortical parcellation and attribute map prediction

model_family: 3D convolutional neural network detecting fetal keypoint landmarks per volume frame
patient_population: low-spatial-resolution, high-temporal-resolution MRI volumes of the gravid abdomen acquired over 10-30 minute durations
clinical_problem: fetal motion during MRI, which forces single-shot acquisition with poor signal-to-noise and diagnostic contrast and often ruins the study - and about which surprisingly little is quantitatively known
model_description: Estimates the fetus's pose - its actual posture - in every frame, which converts a long low-resolution acquisition into a kinematic record. Two things follow that a motion-correction method alone would not give: fetal movement becomes something measurable in health and disease, and the movement statistics can train models that anticipate motion rather than correct it afterwards. A MICCAI paper, and the conference venue is where much of this methods work lives.
journal: Medical image computing and computer-assisted intervention : MICCAI ... International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
title: Fetal Pose Estimation in Volumetric MRI using a 3D Convolution Neural Network.
headline_result: average error 4.47 mm and 96.4% accuracy at a 10 mm threshold for fetal landmark localization

model_family: neural architecture search via Google Cloud AutoML
patient_population: children in the Guangzhou pediatric chest radiograph dataset, alongside adult chest radiographs and three non-radiologic datasets
clinical_problem: pneumonia on pediatric chest radiographs, as one of five diagnostic classification tasks
model_description: The subject is not a model but a question: can clinicians with no coding experience build a usable image classifier? Five public datasets, including pediatric chest radiographs, were fed to a commercial automated architecture-search service and the resulting classifiers evaluated. Binary tasks did well; multi-class tasks were uneven, and external validation on an unseen skin dataset collapsed, which is the paper's cautionary finding.
title: Automated deep learning design for medical image classification by health-care professionals with no coding experience: a feasibility study.
headline_result: binary tasks: sensitivity 73.3-97.0%, specificity 67-100%, AUPRC 0.87-1.00; external validation on the Edinburgh skin dataset fell to AUPRC 0.47

model_family: convolutional network feeding a recurrent network across views
patient_population: 21,456 elbow radiographic studies from a dedicated children's hospital over four years; mean age 7.2 years, 43% girls
clinical_problem: identifying acute traumatic abnormality on pediatric elbow radiographs, where skeletal immaturity changes the normal appearance with age
model_description: Rather than judging each radiograph alone, the model reads the whole three-view series and reaches one decision, which is how a radiologist actually works. Labels came from the reports of a four-year archive at one children's hospital. The published error breakdown is worth reading: it missed 1 of 241 supracondylar and 1 of 88 lateral condylar fractures, but 15 of 77 effusions without fracture, which is the harder and more subtle call.
title: Binomial Classification of Pediatric Elbow Fractures Using a Deep Learning Multiview Approach Emulating Radiologist Decision Making.
headline_result: AUC 0.95, accuracy 88%, sensitivity 91%, specificity 84%

model_family: multivariate classification on standardized cortical and subcortical measures
patient_population: 2,304 patients and 2,068 controls across 46 datasets, spanning adult and pediatric (<18) samples
clinical_problem: whether structural MRI can distinguish an individual with obsessive-compulsive disorder from a healthy control, which no diagnostic biomarker currently does
model_description: A large negative result, and the most useful kind. Across 46 sites, classification of obsessive-compulsive disorder from structural MRI was poor within the pooled sample and fell to chance when models were validated on data from sites they had never seen. Good performance appeared only within medication-defined subgroups, which is a warning that an apparent imaging biomarker can be a treatment marker. Anyone quoting single-site classification accuracies in a developmental disorder should read this first.
title: Structural neuroimaging biomarkers for obsessive-compulsive disorder in the ENIGMA-OCD consortium: medication matters
headline_result: AUC 0.57-0.62 on the pooled sample and no better than chance (0.51-0.54) on completely new sites; above 0.8 only within medication-stratified subgroups

model_family: graph-theoretic network features with a similarity network fusion classifier
patient_population: 29 drug-naive children with Tourette syndrome and 37 healthy children
clinical_problem: diagnosing Tourette syndrome in children, which currently rests on qualitative description of symptoms
model_description: Builds whole-brain functional connectivity networks and uses their topological properties, rather than individual connections, as classification features. Drug-naive patients avoid the usual medication confound. The discriminative regions extended beyond sensorimotor circuits into visual, default-mode and language areas. Sample size is small, so the accuracy should be read as promising rather than established.
title: Combining Disrupted and Discriminative Topological Properties of Functional Connectivity Networks as Neuroimaging Biomarkers for Accurate Diagnosis of Early Tourette Syndrome Children.
headline_result: 88.79% classification accuracy from network topological properties

model_family: 16-layer deep CNN with global average pooling and transfer learning
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound
clinical_problem: acquiring the fetal facial standard plane, the precondition for any subsequent facial measurement or diagnosis
model_description: Recognizes whether an ultrasound image is a fetal facial standard plane, a task that defeated hand-crafted features because these planes vary greatly among themselves while resembling many non-standard planes. Global average pooling in place of a large fully connected layer cuts parameters sharply, which is the practical response to having limited training data.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: A Deep Convolutional Neural Network-Based Framework for Automatic Fetal Facial Standard Plane Recognition.
headline_result: outperformed traditional hand-crafted feature approaches; figures not stated in the abstract

model_family: machine learning on placental shape and texture features
patient_population: 80 pregnancies between 18 and 39 weeks: 46 healthy and 34 with fetal growth restriction
clinical_problem: identifying fetal growth restriction and estimating birth weight before delivery
model_description: Characterizes the placenta rather than the fetus, on the reasoning that placental function is what constrains growth. Shape features (volume, thickness, elongation) are combined with first-order and co-occurrence texture measures from 3D T2-weighted MRI to identify growth-restricted pregnancies and estimate birth weight, in both healthy and affected fetuses.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: In vivo placental MRI shape and textural features predict fetal growth restriction and postnatal outcome.
headline_result: 86% accuracy, 77% precision and 86% recall for identifying fetal growth restriction; birth weight error 0.3% in healthy and -2.6% in growth-restricted fetuses

model_family: support vector machine on 3D texture features
patient_population: children with brain tumors imaged at multiple UK centres
clinical_problem: non-invasive diagnosis of childhood brain tumors, which despite advances in MRI has not reached routine practice
model_description: The question this asks is the one most single-centre radiomics papers do not: does a texture classifier trained at one hospital work at another. It answers it by rigorous pairwise testing between centres, finding AUCs of 76-86% on unseen sites and that similar texture features are enhanced by images from different hospitals. It also examines class imbalance, which is unavoidable when some childhood tumor types are much rarer than others.
title: Radiomics in paediatric neuro-oncology: A multicentre study on MRI texture analysis.
dataset_size: a multicentre clinical MRI cohort; size not stated
headline_result: AUC 76-86% across pairwise cross-centre testing, indicating transferable tumour texture information

model_family: data-driven fiber clustering with a machine-learning classifier on cluster diffusion features
patient_population: 149 children: 70 with autism spectrum disorder and 79 typically developing controls
clinical_problem: identifying which white matter connections are altered in autism, and whether that can classify individual children
model_description: Clusters whole-brain tractography into anatomically meaningful fiber groups, describes each cluster by its diffusion properties, and uses those as features to classify a child as autistic or not. Because the features are named tracts rather than voxels, the model says which connections carried the decision: corpus callosum, arcuate and uncinate fasciculi, aslant tract, and cerebellar and brainstem connections, with the crossing-fiber tensor most affected.
title: Whole brain white matter connectivity analysis using machine learning: An application to autism.
headline_result: 78.33% cross-validated classification accuracy

model_family: deep convolutional neural network
patient_population: children undergoing clinical hand radiography at two children's hospitals
clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment in the workup of endocrine and metabolic disorders
model_description: Takes a hand radiograph and returns an estimated bone age. Trained on 14,036 clinical hand radiographs and their reports from two children's hospitals, then compared against the mean of the clinical report and three additional reviewers on a 200-examination test set, and against a published automated model on the public Digital Hand Atlas.
title: Performance of a Deep-Learning Neural Network Model in Assessing Skeletal Maturity on Pediatric Hand Radiographs.
study_design: retrospective two-center diagnostic accuracy with reader comparison
dataset_size: 14,036 clinical hand radiographs for training and validation; 200-examination and 913-examination test sets
headline_result: mean difference from reviewers 0 years; root mean square 0.63 years and mean absolute difference 0.50 years

model_family: random forest on shape and diffusion radiomic features
patient_population: 83 newly diagnosed, never-treated children with ADHD aged 7-14 and 87 age- and sex-matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: diagnosis of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and separation of its inattentive and combined subtypes
model_description: Takes structural and diffusion MRI, extracts gray-matter shape and white-matter diffusion features, selects the ones with real discriminative power inside cross-validation loops, and classifies a child as having ADHD or not, and then which subtype. Notably, total brain and tissue volumes did not differ between groups, so whatever signal exists is in shape rather than size.
title: Psychoradiologic Utility of MR Imaging for Diagnosis of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder: A Radiomics Analysis.
headline_result: 73.7% accuracy for ADHD versus control, 80.1% for inattentive versus combined subtype

model_family: random forest plus community detection on the resulting proximity matrix
patient_population: 47 children with autism and 58 typically developing children aged 9-13
clinical_problem: whether autism spectrum disorder contains distinct cognitive subtypes with different brain signatures
model_description: First classifies a child as autistic or typically developing from seven cognitive tasks, then reuses the forest's internal proximity between subjects to cluster them into subgroups, and finally asks whether those data-driven subgroups differ in resting-state functional connectivity. The clinical interest is in subtyping a heterogeneous diagnosis rather than in the classification accuracy, which is moderate.
title: Subtyping cognitive profiles in Autism Spectrum Disorder using a Functional Random Forest algorithm.
headline_result: 72.7% classification accuracy (specificity 80.7%, sensitivity 63.1%); three autism and four typically developing subgroups identified

model_family: multi-voxel pattern analysis classifier over task fMRI conflict-related activation
patient_population: two samples of adolescents with bulimia nervosa spectrum symptoms differing in severity, illness duration and age, compared with healthy adolescents, scanned during a Simon task
clinical_problem: whether the fronto-striatal disturbance of bulimia nervosa is present early, when the clinical picture is still subthreshold and the diagnosis is least certain
model_description: The design does something most classification studies do not: the classifier trained to separate fully symptomatic patients from healthy adolescents is then applied to the subthreshold group, and it transfers. That cross-severity generalization is a stronger claim than in-sample accuracy, because it says the same circuit disturbance is present before the disorder is, which is what would make it a risk marker rather than a consequence.
title: Abnormal fronto-striatal activation as a marker of threshold and subthreshold Bulimia Nervosa.
study_design: retrospective analysis of task fMRI cohorts
dataset_size: two adolescent patient samples plus healthy controls, sizes not stated in the abstract
headline_result: both threshold and subthreshold bulimia adolescents were accurately discriminated from healthy adolescents, and patterns learned from the severe group generalized to the subthreshold group

model_family: machine-learning classifiers on regional neuroanatomical density and spatial pattern similarity
patient_population: children implanted before 3.5 years of age, compared against age-matched normally hearing children
clinical_problem: predicting which deaf children will gain speech perception from a cochlear implant, before the operation
model_description: Takes presurgical brain MRI from a cochlear implant candidate and predicts how much that individual child's speech perception will improve after implantation. The method first identifies which anatomical networks auditory deprivation has and has not affected; the predictive signal came from the unaffected regions, particularly auditory association and cognitive areas, suggesting what is preserved matters more than what is lost.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
title: Neural preservation underlies speech improvement from auditory deprivation in young cochlear implant recipients.
headline_result: highest classification accuracy, specificity and sensitivity came from brain regions unaffected by auditory deprivation

model_family: custom convolutional network trained from scratch
patient_population: 10,289 skeletal age examinations, 8,909 from one institution's archive and 1,383 from the public Digital Hand Atlas
clinical_problem: bone age assessment, which is tedious and time consuming for the radiologist
model_description: Argues, and demonstrates, that a network designed and trained from scratch for the specific task can beat transfer learning from natural images, given a large enough institutional dataset. Training is split into four cohorts by sex and age band, which reflects how Greulich and Pyle is applied in practice. Testing uses 20 radiographs per one-year age cohort rather than a random split, so performance is visible across the age range instead of averaged over it.
title: MABAL: a Novel Deep-Learning Architecture for Machine-Assisted Bone Age Labeling.
dataset_size: 10,289 training images across four sex and age cohorts
headline_result: reported to outperform existing proposed bone age algorithms; figures not stated in the abstract

model_family: Inception-v3 transfer learning
patient_population: children undergoing chest radiography for suspected pneumonia; the primary cohort is adults with retinal OCT
clinical_problem: pediatric pneumonia on chest radiographs, and bacterial vs viral origin
model_description: A transfer-learning framework that takes a single image and returns a diagnostic label, with an occlusion map highlighting the regions that drove the decision. It was developed on retinal OCT images and then retrained on pediatric chest radiographs to separate normal from pneumonia and bacterial from viral pneumonia. The paper's argument is that a general transfer-learning recipe needs far less labelled data than training from scratch.
title: Identifying Medical Diagnoses and Treatable Diseases by Image-Based Deep Learning.
study_design: retrospective technical development with expert comparison
dataset_size: not stated in the abstract for the chest radiograph cohort
headline_result: performance comparable to human experts on the retinal task; the pediatric chest radiograph result is not quantified in the abstract

model_family: multi-task fully convolutional network
patient_population: 140 fetal ultrasound volumes, gestational age 26.0 ± 4.4 weeks
clinical_problem: putting 3D fetal neurosonography volumes into a common reference frame despite arbitrary fetal position
model_description: Localizes the fetal brain, segments its structures, and aligns the volume to a reference coordinate system, all from one network with shared features and task-specific outputs. The coordinate system is defined anatomically from the skull boundary, eye sockets and head pose predicted from intracranial structures, which is what makes alignment robust to how the fetus happens to be lying.
title: Fully-automated alignment of 3D fetal brain ultrasound to a canonical reference space using multi-task learning.
headline_result: high brain overlap and low eye localization error on co-alignment, independent of gestational age or head size

model_family: deep belief network on combined functional and structural features
patient_population: 185 children aged 5-10 from the ABIDE I and II datasets (116 with autism, 69 controls)
clinical_problem: diagnosing autism spectrum disorder in young children, where early diagnosis changes what intervention is possible
model_description: Combines resting-state functional MRI with gray and white matter measures over anatomically labelled regions and learns a joint representation with a deep belief network, on the argument that earlier work used only shallow hand-computed features. Deliberately restricted to 5-10 year olds because that is where diagnosis matters. The accuracy is modest and the specificity is poor, which the numbers make plain.
title: Combination of rs-fMRI and sMRI Data to Discriminate Autism Spectrum Disorders in Young Children Using Deep Belief Network.
study_design: technical development on a public dataset
headline_result: 65.56% accuracy (sensitivity 84%, specificity 33%, F1 74.76%) by 10-fold cross-validation

model_family: stacked sparse autoencoder for feature selection with a support vector machine classifier
patient_population: 28 infants born at 23-31 weeks without brain injury, scanned at term-equivalent age; features pretrained on 884 subjects from a public database
clinical_problem: identifying at term-equivalent age which very preterm infants will have cognitive deficits at 2 years
model_description: Learns a compressed representation of the functional connectome without labels, using a large public dataset, then uses that representation to predict 2-year cognitive outcome in a small preterm cohort. The transfer step is the point: neonatal cohorts are too small to train a deep model directly. Frontal lobe and somatosensory regions contributed most. The authors present it explicitly as proof of concept given the sample size.
title: Early prediction of cognitive deficits in very preterm infants using functional connectome data in an artificial neural network framework.
dataset_size: 884 subjects for unsupervised pretraining; 28 very preterm infants for prediction
headline_result: 70.6% accuracy and AUC 0.76 for cognitive deficit at 2 years corrected age

model_family: CNN with image-specific fine tuning inside a bounding-box and scribble pipeline
patient_population: fetuses imaged with MRI; a second application uses brain tumor MRI
clinical_problem: outlining fetal organs on MRI when only some organ classes were annotated for training
model_description: The radiologist draws a bounding box, and optionally scribbles, and the network segments the structure inside it, fine-tuning itself on that specific image before producing the final contour. Because it adapts per image, it can outline organ classes that were never annotated during training. Demonstrated on fetal MRI organs and on brain tumor MRI.
title: Interactive Medical Image Segmentation Using Deep Learning With Image-Specific Fine Tuning.
headline_result: more robust than state-of-the-art CNNs on unseen object classes, with fewer user interactions and less user time than traditional interactive segmentation

model_family: supervised machine-learning brain-age regression on T1-weighted MRI
patient_population: 953 healthy children aged 3-21 for model development; 275 clinically high-risk individuals (39 of whom developed psychosis) and 109 controls aged 12-21 for application
clinical_problem: identifying which clinically high-risk adolescents will convert to psychosis
model_description: A model trained on structural MRI of healthy children to predict chronological age; the gap between that predicted age and the child's real age is then read as a measure of deviant neuroanatomical maturation. Applied to clinically high-risk adolescents, a larger gap was associated with higher risk of developing psychosis, but only in the younger part of the range.
title: Use of Machine Learning to Determine Deviance in Neuroanatomical Maturity Associated With Future Psychosis in Youths at Clinically High Risk.
dataset_size: 953 healthy children for training; 384 subjects for external validation and application
headline_result: clinically high-risk individuals showed a mean 0.64-year gap between predicted and chronological age versus controls (P = .008); greater deviation was associated with psychosis risk (P = .01)

model_family: convolutional network classifying anatomical landmarks, followed by a Hough transform to fit the circumference
patient_population: clinical ultrasound data from 56 pregnant women, with two experts providing acceptance judgments
clinical_problem: automating abdominal circumference measurement, the hardest of the standard fetal biometry parameters because the abdomen has low and non-uniform contrast against its surroundings and an irregular outline
model_description: Built around how the sonographer decides rather than around end-to-end regression: the network is trained to recognize the three landmarks that define an acceptable abdominal plane - stomach bubble, amniotic fluid and umbilical vein - and only then does a Hough transform fit the circle. That keeps the training requirement small and the failures interpretable. The paper names its failure modes plainly, which is unusual: an oversized fetus, absent amniotic fluid, or a distorted abdominal outline.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Automatic Estimation of Fetal Abdominal Circumference From Ultrasound Images.
study_design: retrospective model development with expert acceptance check
headline_result: agreement of 0.809 and 0.771 with two experts, against 0.905 agreement between the two experts themselves; stable even on images degraded by shadowing

model_family: CNN regression predicting rigid transformations to a learned canonical atlas
patient_population: fetuses at around 20 weeks gestation, including heavily moving cases, plus simulated data
clinical_problem: initializing slice-to-volume registration for fetal MRI, where heavy in-utero motion breaks optimization-based methods
model_description: Predicts where an arbitrarily oriented 2D slice belongs in a canonical 3D atlas space from intensity alone, with no initialization. Conventional registration has a narrow capture range and needs a good starting estimate, which a heavily moving fetus does not provide; this removes that dependency and slots into a full reconstruction and motion compensation pipeline. It runs fast enough for real-time use.
title: 3-D Reconstruction in Canonical Co-Ordinate Space From Arbitrarily Oriented 2-D Images.
dataset_size: simulated MRI plus real fetal MRI data
headline_result: average spatial prediction error 7 mm on simulated data, with qualitatively improved reconstructions for heavily moving fetuses at around 20 weeks

model_family: commercial automated plane identification and measurement software
patient_population: 30 fetuses at 17-30 weeks gestation, each with two 3D volumes and a conventional 2D image
clinical_problem: finding the transthalamic plane and measuring biparietal diameter and head circumference from a 3D volume rather than by hand
model_description: Extracts the standard measurement plane out of an acquired 3D volume and measures it, removing the operator's plane selection from the equation. Agreement with two experienced sonographers was good, and the confidence intervals quantify what automation costs: about 4 mm on biparietal diameter and 11 mm on head circumference against manual 2D measurement, which is the number to weigh against the reproducibility gain.
release_evidence: artificial intelligence software (Smartplanes)
title: Artificial intelligence assistance for fetal head biometry: Assessment of automated measurement software.
headline_result: intra- and interobserver ICC above 0.98; 95% confidence intervals 4 mm for biparietal diameter and 11 mm for head circumference between automated 3D and manual 2D measurement

model_family: previously validated machine-learning classifier on CSF volume, brain volume, age and sex
patient_population: 159 children aged 2-4 with autism spectrum disorder (both simplex and multiplex families) and 77 with typical development
clinical_problem: whether extra-axial cerebrospinal fluid volume is an imaging marker of autism beyond infancy
model_description: Applies a classifier previously validated in infants to an independent cohort of 2-4 year olds, using extra-axial CSF volume together with brain volume, age and sex to separate children with autism from typically developing controls. The substantive finding is replication: the CSF excess is present in an independent sample, persists beyond infancy, and is the same in children with and without a family history.
title: Extra-axial cerebrospinal fluid in high-risk and normal-risk children with autism aged 2-4 years: a case-control study.
headline_result: 15.1% more extra-axial CSF in the autism group after adjustment (p = 0.007, Cohen's d 0.39)

model_family: deep convolutional neural networks of varying depth and architecture, some ImageNet-pretrained and some randomly initialized
patient_population: 882 children presenting to the emergency department with upper extremity trauma, 901 lateral elbow radiographs
clinical_problem: detecting traumatic joint effusion on lateral elbow radiographs, the indirect sign that often stands in for an occult pediatric fracture
model_description: A direct test of whether a small pediatric dataset is enough. Fewer than 700 training radiographs, transfer learning from ImageNet, and a hyperparameter search on 115 validation images produced a classifier that reads elbow effusion at roughly 91 percent sensitivity and specificity. The clinical framing matters more than the numbers: effusion is the finding that tells the emergency physician to treat a child as fractured when no fracture line is visible.
title: Detection of Traumatic Pediatric Elbow Joint Effusion Using a Deep Convolutional Neural Network.
headline_result: test-set AUC 0.943, sensitivity 0.909, specificity 0.906

model_family: deep features from three pre-trained convolutional networks combined by majority voting
patient_population: 33 retrospective pullbacks of intracoronary cross-sectional OCT images from pediatric patients with Kawasaki disease
clinical_problem: characterizing the intracoronary tissue changes caused by Kawasaki disease on optical coherence tomography, so that coronary involvement can be classified without expert manual interpretation of every cross-section
model_description: An unusual corner of pediatric imaging AI: intravascular OCT in the coronary arteries of children with Kawasaki disease, where the pathological formations differ from adult atherosclerosis and no reader has seen many of them. Rather than train from scratch on 33 cases, the authors take deep features from three ImageNet-pretrained networks and vote - the standard small-data recipe, applied to a disease that will never have a large dataset.
title: Characterization of coronary artery pathological formations from OCT imaging using deep learning.
headline_result: accuracy, sensitivity and specificity up to 0.99 +/- 0.01 per tissue class with the majority voting scheme

model_family: artificial neural network
patient_population: 565 children under 18 who sustained traumatic brain injury and had a head CT within 24 hours
clinical_problem: predicting six-month outcome after pediatric traumatic brain injury, where adult CT grading systems are the only tools available
model_description: Predicts whether a child will have a favorable Glasgow Outcome Scale score six months after traumatic brain injury, from the admission head CT and clinical record. The comparison is the point: the established adult CT grading systems (Helsinki, Rotterdam, Marshall) were first evaluated on this pediatric cohort and found only moderately predictive, and the pediatric-specific network substantially outperformed all three.
title: Machine-learning analysis outperforms conventional statistical models and CT classification systems in predicting 6-month outcomes in pediatric patients sustaining traumatic brain injury.
headline_result: AUC 0.946 ± 0.042 versus 0.781-0.838 for the Helsinki, Rotterdam and Marshall CT scores

model_family: neural network on brightness-distribution feature vectors
patient_population: 21 children under 5 in Lima, Peru (15 with clinically and radiographically confirmed pneumonia, 6 without lung disease)
clinical_problem: diagnosing childhood pneumonia where there is no radiologist and no radiography, using lung ultrasound
model_description: Strips out skin, fat and muscle from a lung ultrasound frame, divides the remaining image into rectangular segments, and classifies the brightness pattern of each as consolidated or normal lung. The motivation is explicitly resource-constrained: lung ultrasound detects pneumonia well but needs a trained interpreter, and this removes that requirement. The cohort is very small, which the accuracy figures should be read against.
title: Automatic classification of pediatric pneumonia based on lung ultrasound pattern recognition.
dataset_size: 60 lung ultrasound frames from 21 children; 3,055 feature vectors
headline_result: 90.9% sensitivity and 100% specificity for pneumonia infiltrates

model_family: deep learning for MR-derived attenuation correction
patient_population: 79 pediatric brain tumor examinations, 36 with active tumor volume above 1 mL analyzed
clinical_problem: quantitatively accurate FET-PET/MRI in children without a CT for attenuation correction, and without a second sedation
model_description: Generates the attenuation map that PET reconstruction needs directly from MRI, so a child having simultaneous FET-PET/MRI does not need a CT and does not need a second sedation for a sequential scan. Compared against a CT-derived reference and against a non-learned MR-based method on the clinical metrics that actually drive decisions, tumor-to-background activity ratios.
title: Deep Learning Based Attenuation Correction of PET/MRI in Pediatric Brain Tumor Patients: Evaluation in a Clinical Setting.
headline_result: the only method with all patients inside predefined clinical limits; tumor-to-background difference from CT-based reference -0.1% (95% CI -0.8 to 0.5) versus 5.9% for Dixon-based correction

model_family: convolutional neural network that localizes the structure, establishes correspondences and regresses PCA loadings in a point distribution model, trained with a shape-statistics data augmentation scheme
patient_population: three applications, the first of which is pediatric cranial CT for characterizing metopic craniosynostosis; the others are adult femur CT and left atrium MRI
clinical_problem: building statistical shape models straight from raw images, replacing a registration-segmentation-correspondence pipeline that needs parameter tuning, manual delineation and quality control at every step
model_description: A MICCAI-workshop method paper whose lead application is pediatric: metopic craniosynostosis is a shape diagnosis, and statistical shape modeling is how shape is quantified, but the conventional pipeline is too hand-operated to run at scale. The augmentation trick is the enabling piece - 40-50 processed scans with known shape parameters are resampled into thousands of plausible training images, which is how a deep network gets trained on a surgical cohort's worth of data.
journal: Shape in medical imaging : International Workshop, ShapeMI 2018, held in conjunction with MICCAI 2018, Granada, Spain, September 20, 2018 : proceedings. ShapeMI (Workshop) (2018 : Granada, Spain)
title: DeepSSM: A Deep Learning Framework for Statistical Shape Modeling from Raw Images.
dataset_size: 40-50 processed CT/MRI scans per application, augmented into thousands of training images
headline_result: accurate low-dimensional shape representations produced directly from unseen 3D images with essentially no parameter tuning or user assistance

model_family: customized VGG16 with visualization of class-relevant regions
patient_population: children undergoing chest radiography for suspected pneumonia
clinical_problem: pneumonia detection in children, and separating bacterial from viral pneumonia
model_description: Classifies a pediatric chest radiograph as normal or pneumonia and then as bacterial or viral, and, unusually for this literature, spends most of its effort on showing where the model looked. It introduces a way of localizing the region that drives predictions across all images of a class rather than one image at a time, on the argument that an unexplained black box is unusable for screening decisions.
