title: Visualization and Interpretation of Convolutional Neural Network Predictions in Detecting Pneumonia in Pediatric Chest Radiographs.
headline_result: 96.2% accuracy detecting pneumonia and 93.6% distinguishing bacterial from viral

model_family: random forest classification
patient_population: 137 healthy substance-naive adolescents aged 12-14, followed annually to age 18
clinical_problem: identifying adolescents at risk of initiating heavy alcohol use before they start
model_description: Takes structural and functional MRI together with demographic and neuropsychological measures from a substance-naive 12-14 year old and predicts whether that adolescent will have initiated moderate to heavy drinking by 18. The model is used as a variable-importance tool rather than a deployed classifier: its output is the ranked list of 34 contributing predictors, which mixes imaging with behavioral and social factors.
title: Neural Predictors of Initiating Alcohol Use During Adolescence.
dataset_size: 137 adolescents (70 later initiated use, 67 did not)
headline_result: 34 predictors identified, including thinner cortex and reduced activation in diffusely distributed regions alongside demographic and behavioral factors; discrimination not quantified in the abstract

model_family: CNN with edge-to-edge, edge-to-node and node-to-graph convolutions on connectivity matrices
patient_population: infants born preterm, scanned between 27 and 46 weeks postmenstrual age
clinical_problem: predicting neurodevelopmental outcome after preterm birth
model_description: Takes a structural connectivity matrix built from diffusion tensor imaging and returns predicted Bayley-III cognitive and motor scores at 18 months, corrected for prematurity. The convolutions are designed for network topology rather than image space. It also estimates postmenstrual age at scan, and the learned edge weights can be inspected to see which connections drive the prediction.
title: BrainNetCNN: Convolutional neural networks for brain networks; towards predicting neurodevelopment.
study_design: technical development on a preterm cohort
headline_result: outperformed a fully connected network with the same parameter count and other comparison methods; estimated postmenstrual age to within about 2 weeks

model_family: support vector regression on structural MRI measures
patient_population: 64 ultra-high-risk and 62 typically developing adolescents aged 12-18, with outcome determined for 43 at six years
clinical_problem: predicting six-year functional and clinical outcome in adolescents at ultra-high risk for psychosis, most of whom will not convert
model_description: Predicts long-term functioning and symptom scores as continuous values rather than converting versus not converting, on the argument that most ultra-high-risk adolescents turn out resilient and a binary label throws that away. Baseline subcortical volumes carried the strongest signal. The effect size is medium and the authors are careful not to overclaim individual-level prediction from it.
title: Individual prediction of long-term outcome in adolescents at ultra-high risk for psychosis: Applying machine learning techniques to brain imaging data.
dataset_size: 126 adolescents at baseline; 43 with six-year outcome
headline_result: highest predictive correlation r = 0.42 between baseline subcortical volumes and long-term level of functioning

model_family: deep CNN, several architectures compared
patient_population: children across all age ranges, races and both sexes in a public hand-radiograph dataset
clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment in endocrine, genetic and growth disorders
model_description: Takes a left-hand radiograph and returns a bone age, replacing Greulich-Pyle or Tanner-Whitehouse atlas matching. The paper's contribution is as much methodological as clinical: it is the first bone-age model tested on a public dataset across all ages, races and both sexes with source code released, and it uses that setting to compare learned against hand-crafted features and to ask how to train a network on few images.
release_evidence: first automated bone age work tested on a public dataset for which the source code is available
title: Deep learning for automated skeletal bone age assessment in X-ray images.
study_design: technical development on a public benchmark
dataset_size: a public hand-radiograph dataset; size not stated
headline_result: average discrepancy between manual and automatic bone age of about 0.8 years

model_family: CNN in a densely connected conditional random field, trained from bounding boxes
patient_population: fetuses in a fetal MRI dataset
clinical_problem: segmenting fetal brain and lung on MRI without pixel-level annotation
model_description: Turns cheap annotation into pixel-level segmentations: an annotator draws only a bounding box, and the method alternates between training a network and re-estimating the segmentation inside the box until it converges. Extends the classical GrabCut idea with a learned classifier. Tested on fetal brain and lung segmentation from MRI.
title: DeepCut: Object Segmentation From Bounding Box Annotations Using Convolutional Neural Networks.
headline_result: encouraging accuracy on fetal brain and lung segmentation from bounding boxes alone; figures not stated in the abstract

model_family: random forest classifier over regional cortical thickness, volume and surface area features
patient_population: 46 children with autism spectrum disorder and 39 children with developmental delay, aged 18 to 37 months
clinical_problem: finding an objective imaging biomarker to supplement autism diagnosis in toddlers, which currently rests on psychological evaluation, clinical observation and history and is therefore subjective and reporter-dependent
model_description: The comparison group is the useful design choice: developmental delay rather than typical development, which is the discrimination that is actually hard in a toddler clinic. Three anatomical feature families are compared head to head, and cortical thickness beats both volume and surface area. The authors are careful about the claim - a supplementary line of evidence for a diagnosis, not a replacement - which is the appropriate register for 85 toddlers.
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
title: Diagnostic model generated by MRI-derived brain features in toddlers with autism spectrum disorder.
headline_result: best performance from regional average cortical thickness of the 20 most important random forest features, outperforming volume-based and surface-area-based classification

model_family: machine learning on global graph metrics of resting-state networks
patient_population: 45 children aged 4-19 with focal epilepsy, with full-scale IQ measured by a pediatric neuropsychologist
clinical_problem: quantifying the cumulative impact of epilepsy on a developing brain, as a route to a marker of cognitive deterioration
model_description: Parcellates the cortex into about 700 nodes, computes five global network metrics from resting-state MRI, and predicts epilepsy duration from them, using duration as a stand-in for how much the disease has affected the brain. Duration was itself inversely related to IQ. The prediction is near-perfect, which given 45 patients and five predictors warrants caution, but the framing — imaging metrics as a patient-level marker of cognitive deterioration — is the useful part.
title: Metrics of brain network architecture capture the impact of disease in children with epilepsy.
headline_result: predicted and actual epilepsy duration correlated at r = 0.95 (p = 0.0001), driven mainly by network modularity

model_family: frame-by-frame classifier regularized by a conditional random field over time, with a kernelized linear dynamical model for heartbeat detection
patient_population: 323 predefined free-hand ultrasound videos sweeping the maternal abdomen
clinical_problem: confirming pregnancy viability and fetal presentation - the two first questions of any obstetric ultrasound - from a simple predefined sweep that a novice can perform
model_description: Task-shifting by design. The scanning protocol is engineered so that a fixed straight sweep is guaranteed to cross the skull, abdomen and heart, and the algorithm then does the interpreting - which is what lets someone with no sonography training establish viability and presentation. Temporal structure is used twice: a conditional random field smooths the per-frame labels, and heartbeat is read out of the dynamics of consecutive cardiac frames rather than from any single image.
title: A framework for analysis of linear ultrasound videos to detect fetal presentation and heartbeat.
headline_result: mean classification accuracy 83.4% for detecting fetal skull, abdomen and heart, and 93.1% for heartbeat detection

model_family: neural network classifier on surface-based morphometric features
patient_population: 22 children with focal epilepsy (mean age 12.1 years) and 28 healthy controls (mean age 14.6 years)
clinical_problem: finding focal cortical dysplasia on MRI in children with drug-resistant epilepsy, where detection determines whether surgery is offered
model_description: Scans the cortical surface vertex by vertex and flags candidate dysplastic regions. Alongside established measures (cortical thickness, gray-white blurring, FLAIR intensity, sulcal depth, curvature) it adds features designed for a developing brain: local cortical deformation, a doughnut measure of local variability against the surrounding cortex, and per-vertex interhemispheric asymmetry. Existing adult tools had not worked on children, which is precisely the gap it addresses.
title: Novel surface features for automated detection of focal cortical dysplasias in paediatric epilepsy.
headline_result: sensitivity rose from 59% with established features alone to 73% with the added novel features

model_family: deep-learning classifier on cortical surface area features
patient_population: 106 infants at high familial risk of autism and 42 low-risk infants, imaged at 6, 12 and 24 months
clinical_problem: prediction of an autism spectrum disorder diagnosis before behavioral symptoms are established
model_description: Takes brain MRI acquired at 6 and 12 months of age, chiefly cortical surface area measurements, and returns a prediction of whether that individual child will meet criteria for autism at 24 months. Trained and cross-validated within a prospective high-familial-risk infant cohort. The clinical interest is identifying children before symptoms emerge, when early intervention is still possible.
title: Early brain development in infants at high risk for autism spectrum disorder.
headline_result: positive predictive value 81%, sensitivity 88% for a 24-month autism diagnosis

model_family: ImageNet-pretrained CNN, fine-tuned
patient_population: children undergoing hand radiography for bone age assessment, analyzed separately by sex
clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment in endocrine and metabolic workup
model_description: An end-to-end pipeline: it finds and crops the hand, standardizes the radiograph, and returns a bone age, with attention maps showing which growth centers drove the estimate. The authors report deploying it in their clinical environment as a decision-support tool returning a result in under two seconds.
release_evidence: deployed in the authors' clinical environment as a decision-support system; no external availability stated
title: Fully Automated Deep Learning System for Bone Age Assessment.
study_design: retrospective single-center development with clinical deployment
headline_result: bone age within 1 year in 90.4% (female) and 94.2% (male) of test radiographs; within 2 years in 98.1% and 99.0%

model_family: two CNNs (localization network and quality-classification network)
patient_population: fetuses undergoing obstetric ultrasound examination
clinical_problem: automatic quality control of obstetric ultrasound images before biometric measurements are taken from them
model_description: One network finds the fetal abdominal region in the image, a second scores whether the key landmarks (stomach bubble and umbilical vein) are adequately depicted. The output is a quality verdict, not a diagnosis: it is meant to catch a badly acquired or wrongly chosen slice before someone measures from it, which is a common and unmonitored source of biometric error.
title: FUIQA: Fetal Ultrasound Image Quality Assessment With Deep Convolutional Networks.
headline_result: quality assessment comparable to the subjective ratings of three medical doctors

model_family: composite convolutional and recurrent network with multitask learning
patient_population: fetuses in hundreds of obstetric ultrasound videos
clinical_problem: acquiring the correct standard planes during obstetric ultrasound, which currently depends on operator experience
model_description: Identifies several different fetal standard planes from ultrasound video with one general framework, rather than a separate detector per plane as earlier work did. The convolutional part learns appearance within a frame and the recurrent part learns how frames relate over time; multitask learning shares what is common between plane types, which is how it copes with limited training data.
title: Ultrasound Standard Plane Detection Using a Composite Neural Network Framework.
headline_result: better standard-plane detection than plane-specific prior methods; figures not stated in the abstract

model_family: hierarchical sparse feature selection with an extreme learning machine
patient_population: children in the public ADHD-200 dataset
clinical_problem: separating ADHD inattentive from ADHD combined from typical development on imaging
model_description: Combines structural measures (cortical thickness and its variability, volume, surface area, intensity) with functional connectivity maps, selects the most discriminative features hierarchically, and classifies into three groups rather than two. Multi-class performance is much weaker than binary, which is the honest and clinically relevant part: telling ADHD from typical development is easier than telling the subtypes apart.
title: Multi-modal, Multi-measure, and Multi-class Discrimination of ADHD with Hierarchical Feature Extraction and Extreme Learning Machine Using Structural and Functional Brain MRI.
study_design: technical development on a public dataset
dataset_size: selected subjects from the public ADHD-200 dataset
headline_result: 76.19% accuracy in the three-class setting and 92.86% in the binary setting (both p < 0.0001)

model_family: cross-validated machine-learning classifier on functional connectivity features
patient_population: 59 six-month-old infants at high familial risk for autism
clinical_problem: prediction of an autism spectrum disorder diagnosis at 24 months from imaging at 6 months
model_description: Takes resting-state functional connectivity MRI acquired at 6 months of age and returns a prediction of whether that child will receive an autism diagnosis at 24 months. Functional connections were first related to 24-month social, language, motor and repetitive-behavior scores, then used as features in a fully cross-validated classifier.
title: Functional neuroimaging of high-risk 6-month-old infants predicts a diagnosis of autism at 24 months of age.
headline_result: positive predictive value 100% (95% CI 62.9-100), sensitivity 81.8%, specificity 100%

model_family: auto-context CNN (voxelwise multi-plane and U-net variants)
patient_population: public adult benchmark datasets plus reconstructed fetal brain MRI
clinical_problem: extracting the brain from surrounding tissue on MRI, including fetal brains in arbitrary orientations
model_description: Separates brain from non-brain on MRI without registering to an atlas and without assuming anything about image geometry, which is what makes it work on a fetal brain lying in an arbitrary orientation inside the uterus. It feeds its own probability maps back in as context, iteratively, so the network learns the shape and connectedness of the brain rather than only local intensity.
title: Auto-Context Convolutional Neural Network (Auto-Net) for Brain Extraction in Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
dataset_size: two public benchmarks (LPBA40, OASIS) plus a fetal brain MRI set
headline_result: Dice 97.73% and 97.62% on the public adult benchmarks and 95.97% on arbitrarily oriented fetal brains, where competing methods performed poorly

model_family: real-time CNN with weakly supervised localization
patient_population: fetuses undergoing routine mid-pregnancy anomaly screening ultrasound
clinical_problem: finding and labelling the standard views required by the mid-pregnancy anomaly scan
model_description: Watches freehand 2D ultrasound as it is acquired and, in real time, names which of 13 standard fetal views is on screen and draws a box around the relevant anatomy. The localization is learned from image-level labels alone, with no manual boxes. Intended to help less experienced operators acquire and recognize the required views, and to pull the right frames out of stored video afterwards.
title: SonoNet: Real-Time Detection and Localisation of Fetal Standard Scan Planes in Freehand Ultrasound.
study_design: technical development on clinical screening data
dataset_size: images and video from a large set of full clinical anomaly screenings; size not stated
headline_result: F1 0.798 for real-time detection, 90.1% accuracy for retrospective frame retrieval, 77.8% for localization

model_family: deep learning implementing the Greulich-Pyle method
patient_population: 200 patients aged 3-17 undergoing left-hand radiography
clinical_problem: bone age estimation, and whether software assistance makes radiologists faster without making them worse
model_description: Takes a left-hand radiograph and returns a ranked list of candidate Greulich-Pyle bone ages. The study is designed around the assisted workflow rather than the model alone: two radiologists read the same 200 cases with the software and with the atlas, and both concordance with the reference and reading time were measured. This is the question a department actually faces before buying such a tool.
release_evidence: described as a new automatic software system; the abstract does not say whether it is commercially available
title: Computerized Bone Age Estimation Using Deep Learning Based Program: Evaluation of the Accuracy and Efficiency.
headline_result: software alone concordant in 69.5% of cases (r = 0.992 with reference); concordance rose from 63.0% to 72.5% and 49.5% to 57.5% for the two readers, with reading times cut by 18% and 40%

model_family: three-stage deep learning pipeline (localization, region detection, acoustic pattern verification)
patient_population: a large clinical dataset of 2D mid-gestation fetal images
clinical_problem: checking that a transventricular fetal brain plane meets the clinical standard before biometry is taken from it
model_description: Verifies that an acquired fetal neurosonographic plane actually satisfies the imaging protocol, by locating the brain, finding the regions that should contain named structures, and then learning the acoustic patterns that distinguish a compliant plane from a near-miss. This is quality control against a written clinical standard rather than diagnosis, and the standard is what non-experts find hardest to meet.
title: A Deep Learning Solution for Automatic Fetal Neurosonographic Diagnostic Plane Verification Using Clinical Standard Constraints.
dataset_size: a large real-world clinical dataset; size not stated
headline_result: automatic verification approached human expert assessment

model_family: trained machine-learning algorithm for individual resting-state network identification
patient_population: 20 children aged 1.9-18.4 years undergoing craniotomy, six of whom needed sedation for imaging
clinical_problem: mapping eloquent cortex before craniotomy in children who cannot perform task-based fMRI
model_description: The clinical case for this is unusually clear: task-based functional mapping requires a cooperative patient, and many children are not, whether through age, cognitive deficit or the need for sedation. A trained classifier identifies resting-state networks in the individual child, and the maps are loaded straight into the surgical navigation system. Six of the twenty children were sedated and it still worked, which is the point.
title: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging for surgical planning in pediatric patients: a preliminary experience.
headline_result: resting-state network maps produced for all 20 patients and uploaded to clinical navigation systems, including in six sedated children

model_family: ensemble of deep networks trained end to end on whole hands and hand regions
patient_population: 12,600 hand radiographs from the 2017 RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge
clinical_problem: bone age assessment for endocrine and metabolic disorders of child development
model_description: A challenge entry that goes further than winning: by training separately on whole hands and on specific hand regions, it measures which bones actually carry the bone age signal, and evaluates performance separately by skeletal development stage rather than as one average. That per-stage breakdown is what a clinician needs, because accuracy at the extremes of childhood is where these models tend to fail.
title: Pediatric Bone Age Assessment Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
headline_result: outperformed other common bone age methods on the challenge data

model_family: random-forest feature selection with a nonlinear support vector machine
patient_population: 105 preterm infants scanned at term-equivalent age and 26 healthy term-born neonates
clinical_problem: characterizing how preterm birth has altered functional brain organization by term-equivalent age
model_description: Builds whole-brain functional connectivity networks from neonatal resting-state MRI, selects the small set of connections that actually distinguish preterm from term infants, and classifies each infant from connectivity alone. The discriminative connections clustered in the basal ganglia and between subcortical structures and association cortex, which localizes the disruption rather than only detecting it.
title: Machine-learning to characterise neonatal functional connectivity in the preterm brain.
headline_result: 80% cross-validated classification accuracy from a small set of discriminative connections

model_family: quantitative image analysis producing 131 morphological parameters, with machine learning used to fit safety thresholds
patient_population: 50 consecutive children with hydronephrosis of varying severity who had both 2D sonography and diuretic MAG3 renography
clinical_problem: deciding which children with hydronephrosis actually need a diuretic nuclear renogram, using the ultrasound they have already had
model_description: A triage model rather than a diagnostic one, and the design reflects that: thresholds are fitted at 100 percent sensitivity, so the model is only allowed to rule out. What it buys is concrete and measurable in avoided studies - up to 62 percent of children spared a diuretic renogram, which for this population means avoided radiopharmaceutical, catheterization and sedation. It also beats the two scoring systems urologists actually use, the Society for Fetal Urology grade and the hydronephrosis index.
title: Quantitative Ultrasound for Measuring Obstructive Severity in Children with Hydronephrosis.
headline_result: at 100% sensitivity, specificity 94%, 70% and 74% for the three washout thresholds (AUC 0.98, 0.94, 0.94), significantly better than SFU grade and the hydronephrosis index; up to 62% of diuretic renograms avoidable

model_family: linear support vector machine on regional white-matter features
patient_population: 28 school-aged children with developmental dyslexia and 33 age-matched controls
clinical_problem: identifying developmental dyslexia from imaging rather than behavioral testing alone
model_description: Takes structural and diffusion MRI, reduces each white-matter region to five measures (volume, fractional anisotropy, mean, axial and radial diffusivity), and classifies a child as dyslexic or not. The features that carried the classification extended well beyond the classical reading network into limbic and motor tracts, which is the paper's substantive claim.
title: Disrupted white matter connectivity underlying developmental dyslexia: A machine learning approach.
headline_result: 83.61% classification accuracy, replicated with a logistic regression classifier

model_family: stacked autoencoders with unsupervised clustering
patient_population: 663 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients across 915 visits, reviewed by the Scoliosis Research Society 3D Classification Committee
clinical_problem: classifying three-dimensional spinal deformity in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, which the two-dimensional Lenke system does not capture
model_description: Compresses each patient's 3D spine reconstruction into a learned code and clusters those codes with no assumptions about how many groups there should be or what defines them. Eleven groups emerged, discriminated mainly by curve location, kyphosis and lordosis, and subgroups appeared within existing Lenke types. This is data-driven taxonomy rather than diagnosis, aimed at replacing a classification the field agrees is inadequate.
journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
title: Three-dimensional morphology study of surgical adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patient from encoded geometric models.
headline_result: eleven clusters identified with curve location, kyphosis and lordosis as the discriminating factors, revealing subgroups within existing Lenke types

model_family: genetic algorithm searching polynomial regression equations
patient_population: 4,229 women with certain menstrual dates from eight geographically defined urban populations in the INTERGROWTH-21st Fetal Growth Longitudinal Study
clinical_problem: estimating gestational age in women who first present late in pregnancy with unknown menstrual dates
model_description: Takes routine fetal biometry from a single late ultrasound and returns an estimated gestational age. An automated search over more than 64,000 candidate polynomial equations picked head circumference and femur length as the best pair. The clinical value is in antenatal care where first-trimester dating was never done; the honest limitation, stated by the authors, is that accuracy degrades to worse than two weeks in the third trimester.
release_evidence: the prediction equations are published in full in the abstract
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Ultrasound-based gestational-age estimation in late pregnancy.
headline_result: gestational age uncertainty of 6-7 days at 14 weeks, 12-14 days at 26 weeks, and more than 14 days in the third trimester

model_family: support vector machine and support vector regression on resting-state connectivity
patient_population: 50 infants born at 23-29 weeks without moderate or severe brain injury, scanned at term-equivalent age, and 50 term-born controls
clinical_problem: quantifying how much preterm birth has disrupted brain development, as a route to predicting neurodevelopmental outcome
model_description: Takes resting-state functional MRI from a term-equivalent infant and either classifies them as preterm or term born, or estimates their birth gestational age as a continuous measure of how disrupted development has been. The regression output is the interesting one clinically: it gives a per-infant number rather than a group difference, which is what a prediction of individual outcome would need.
title: Prediction of brain maturity in infants using machine-learning algorithms.
headline_result: 84% accuracy distinguishing term from preterm infants (p < 0.0001), with quantitative estimation of birth gestational age in single subjects

model_family: surface-mesh fMRI-seeded diffusion tractography pipeline with a machine-learning track classifier
patient_population: 31 children with unilateral cerebral palsy
clinical_problem: running diffusion tractography in brains with major pathology, where automated cortical parcellation fails, manual region drawing is slow and error-prone, and the usual structure-function assumptions break down after cortical reorganisation
model_description: Aimed at exactly the situation pediatric neuroimaging keeps running into: the brain is too abnormal for atlas-based methods and too numerous for hand-drawn regions. Seeding from the child's own functional activation sidesteps the atlas, surface meshes tighten the seed, and a learned track classifier removes the irrelevant pathways that fMRI smoothing drags in. The head-to-head against the standard voxelwise approach is decisive on the metric that matters for a clinical pipeline - how many children could be processed at all.
title: Surface-Based fMRI-Driven Diffusion Tractography in the Presence of Significant Brain Pathology: A Study Linking Structure and Function in Cerebral Palsy.
headline_result: processed 87% of participants versus 65% for the voxelwise approach, with 15 of 20 diffusion-clinical correlations significant (R2 0.43-0.73) versus 2 for voxelwise

model_family: random forest (trainable Weka segmentation) on filter-bank image features
patient_population: pediatric and adult patients undergoing diagnostic CT under their respective protocols
clinical_problem: knowing which tissue is where in a CT, which patient-specific dose calculation and radiomics both depend on
model_description: Labels every voxel of a neck-to-pelvis CT as one of seven materials: background, air or gas, fat, muscle, solid organ parenchyma, blood or enhanced fluid, and bone. It is deliberately built for both pediatric and adult protocols, because organ-level knowledge is the prerequisite for patient-specific dose estimation in exactly the population where dose matters most.
title: Tissue segmentation of computed tomography images using a Random Forest algorithm: a feasibility study.
headline_result: median Dice 0.86 ± 0.03 for pediatric protocols and 0.85 ± 0.04 for adult protocols across seven material classes

model_family: support vector machine with a Gaussian kernel over word-stem and bigram features of radiology report text
patient_population: 1500 pediatric emergency department radiology reports (1000 training, 500 test), with blinded independent review by two physicians as the reference standard
clinical_problem: finding the children who had a long bone fracture, from free-text radiology reports, so that pediatric emergency medicine quality improvement can be measured on real cases rather than on billing codes
model_description: Not image analysis but report analysis, and its comparator is what makes it worth recording: diagnosis codes, which are how quality measurement is done today. The classifier beat them on accuracy, precision and F1, which means a quality program built on codes is measuring the wrong denominator. Built entirely from freely available statistical packages, and the paper is explicit that natural language processing tools rarely leave the laboratories that build them.
release_evidence: implemented using freely available statistical software packages
title: Identification of Long Bone Fractures in Radiology Reports Using Natural Language Processing to support Healthcare Quality Improvement.
headline_result: accuracy 0.958, recall 0.969, precision 0.940, F1 0.954, versus 0.932/0.960/0.896/0.927 for diagnosis codes

model_family: fully convolutional network trained on crowdsourced super-pixel annotations
patient_population: fetuses imaged with T2-weighted MRI
clinical_problem: the shortage of expert pixel-wise annotation that limits fetal brain segmentation research
model_description: Attacks the annotation bottleneck rather than the architecture: super-pixel labelling tasks were distributed to a crowd of non-expert raters through a crowdsourcing platform, and the resulting weak labels used to train a fetal brain segmentation network. Results approached fully supervised methods trained on expert annotation, which if it holds is a cheap route past the constraint that binds most pediatric imaging work.
title: Learning under Distributed Weak Supervision
headline_result: encouraging results compared with highly targeted fully supervised methods

model_family: quantitative texture analysis with machine-learning classifiers
patient_population: 144 neonates delivered between 28 and 39 weeks, imaged within 48 hours of delivery
clinical_problem: predicting neonatal respiratory morbidity before delivery, currently done by amniocentesis
model_description: Analyses the texture of the fetal lung on a routine ultrasound image and returns a risk of respiratory distress syndrome or transient tachypnea of the newborn. The clinical claim is a substitution: it predicted respiratory morbidity about as accurately as amniotic fluid tests do, without an amniocentesis. Blinded validation was done in an independent set of 144 neonates.
release_evidence: the method is named quantusFLM and marked as a trademark in the abstract
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Quantitative ultrasound texture analysis of fetal lungs to predict neonatal respiratory morbidity.
dataset_size: over 13,000 non-clinical and 900 fetal lung images for development; 144 neonates for blinded validation
headline_result: sensitivity 86.2%, specificity 87.0%, positive predictive value 62.5%, negative predictive value 96.2%

model_family: domain-transferred CNN (transfer learning from natural images)
patient_population: fetuses imaged with 2D ultrasound video
clinical_problem: finding the fetal abdominal standard plane in an ultrasound video
model_description: Takes frames of a fetal ultrasound video and identifies the one containing the fetal abdominal standard plane, which is where the biometric measurements are taken. The lower layers are transferred from a network trained on everyday photographs, which is what makes it trainable on the small ultrasound dataset available.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Standard Plane Localization in Fetal Ultrasound via Domain Transferred Deep Neural Networks.
headline_result: outperformed the previous state of the art for fetal abdominal standard plane localization and a network trained on the ultrasound data alone

model_family: multivariable logistic models and a neural network
patient_population: 2,259 children aged 0-60 months imaged after urinary tract infection, from 3,995 with same-day ultrasound and cystourethrogram
clinical_problem: whether renal and bladder ultrasound findings can decide which child after a urinary tract infection needs a voiding cystourethrogram
model_description: Tests the assumption behind the AAP guideline, which is that ultrasound can triage who needs a cystourethrogram. Individual ultrasound findings were strongly associated with reflux, but neither multivariable modelling nor a neural network produced a usefully predictive model. This is a negative result about a widely followed guideline, and it is more informative than another high-accuracy classifier.
title: Predictive value of specific ultrasound findings when used as a screening test for abnormalities on VCUG.
dataset_size: 2,259 children with urinary tract infection as the imaging indication
headline_result: many individual ultrasound findings were significantly associated with reflux, but multivariable and neural network models did not yield a usefully predictive model

model_family: machine-learning classifier on five surface-based morphometric features
patient_population: patients with histopathologically confirmed focal cortical dysplasia, 7 MRI-positive and 24 MRI-negative; ages not stated, in a disease that is the commonest cause of pediatric epilepsy
clinical_problem: finding focal cortical dysplasia in patients whose MRI was reported as normal, which is what stands between them and epilepsy surgery
model_description: Computes five surface-based MRI measures at every cortical vertex and classifies each vertex as lesional or not, with accuracy judged against the region that was actually resected. The result that matters is on the MRI-negative cases: in patients whose scans radiologists had read as normal, it found the histologically confirmed lesion in 14 of 24. Separating thick from thin cortex and sulcal from gyral regions into distinct classifiers was what made this work.
title: Cortical feature analysis and machine learning improves detection of "MRI-negative" focal cortical dysplasia.
headline_result: lesion detected in 6 of 7 MRI-positive patients and in 14 of 24 (58%) MRI-negative patients

model_family: support vector machine on voxel- and region-level morphometry
patient_population: male children with autism spectrum disorder and controls matched for age and non-verbal IQ
clinical_problem: whether autism can be predicted from subtle structural brain differences in young children
model_description: Compares two standard preprocessing pipelines and two spatial scales, voxel and region, to see which representation of brain morphology carries the autism signal. Gray matter subregion features did best. The accuracy is modest and rises when low-IQ subjects are excluded, which is itself informative about what the classifier is partly picking up.
journal: Journal of neuroimaging : official journal of the American Society of Neuroimaging
title: Gray Matter Alterations in Young Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders: Comparing Morphometry at the Voxel and Regional Level.
headline_result: AUC 74%, rising to 80% when restricted to subjects with non-verbal IQ over 70

model_family: supervised classifiers on 3D texture features (six algorithms compared)
patient_population: 48 children with brain tumors of three histological types
clinical_problem: telling medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma and ependymoma apart before biopsy
model_description: Extracts texture features from ordinary pre-contrast T1 and T2 images, in three dimensions rather than slice by slice, and classifies which of the three common childhood posterior fossa tumors it is. The comparison against 2D features is the substance: 3D features improved area under the curve by 12% for a neural network classifier, a difference significant for four of six algorithms tested. The stated goal is fewer surgical procedures and better treatment planning.
title: Three-dimensional textural features of conventional MRI improve diagnostic classification of childhood brain tumours.
headline_result: 3D texture features improved area under the curve by 12% and overall accuracy by 19% over 2D features for a neural network classifier

model_family: support vector machine on cortical thickness
patient_population: 33 never-disordered adolescents aged 10-15, followed for 5 years
clinical_problem: identifying adolescents who will develop major depression before symptoms appear
model_description: Takes baseline structural MRI from a healthy 10-15 year old and predicts whether that adolescent will develop clinically significant depressive symptoms over the next five years, using cortical thickness alone. The features that carried the classification were right medial orbitofrontal, right precentral, left anterior cingulate and bilateral insular cortex. The sample is small, which is the main caveat on the accuracy figure.
journal: International journal of developmental neuroscience : the official journal of the International Society for Developmental Neuroscience
title: Cortical thickness predicts the first onset of major depression in adolescence.
headline_result: 70% overall accuracy predicting future depression onset (69% sensitivity, 70% specificity, p = 0.021)

model_family: predictive modeling on resting-state functional connectivity
patient_population: individuals with autism spectrum disorder without co-occurring intellectual disability, followed for a mean of about three years after scanning
clinical_problem: predicting which individuals with autism will improve in adaptive behavior and autistic traits
model_description: Uses resting-state functional connectivity to predict the part of long-term outcome that baseline behavior and IQ leave unexplained: future autistic traits and the change in adaptive behavior at least a year after the scan. Connectivity of the salience, default-mode and frontoparietal control networks carried the prediction, with salience network connectivity identifying reliable improvers at 100% sensitivity and 70.6% precision.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
title: Resting-state functional connectivity predicts longitudinal change in autistic traits and adaptive functioning in autism.
headline_result: salience network connectivity predicted reliable improvement in adaptive behavior with 100% sensitivity and 70.59% precision
